<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Exogenous Effects:</font>&#160;&#160;As a result of the major storms and health care legislation items described above, we deferred $4.2 million of costs in 2010 for future recovery. See Retail Rates and Alternative Regulation below for additional information.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">New Hydro-Qu&#233;bec Agreement:</font>&#160;&#160;On August 12, 2010 we, along with GMP, VPPSA, Vermont Electric Cooperative, Inc., Vermont Marble, Town of Stowe Electric Department, City of Burlington, Vermont Electric Department, Washington Electric Cooperative, Inc. and the 13 municipal members of VPPSA (collectively, the &#8220;Buyers&#8221;) entered into an agreement for the purchase of shares of 218 MW to 225 MW of energy and environmental attributes from HQUS commencing on November 1, 2012 and continuing through 2038.&#160;&#160;For more information on this agreement, see Power Supply Matters below.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Financial Initiatives:</font>&#160;&#160;Our financial initiatives include maintaining sufficient liquidity to support ongoing operations, the dividend on our common stock and investments in our electric utility infrastructure; planning for replacement power when our long-term power contracts expire; and evaluating opportunities to further invest in Transco.&#160;&#160;Continued focus on these financial initiatives is critical to maintaining our corporate credit rating.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We discuss these financial initiatives and the risks facing our business in more detail below.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">RETAIL RATES AND ALTERNATIVE REGULATION</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Retail Rates </font>Our retail rates are approved by the PSB after considering the recommendations of Vermont&#8217;s consumer advocate, the DPS.&#160;&#160;Fair regulatory treatment is fundamental to maintaining our financial stability.&#160;&#160;Rates must be set at levels to recover costs, including a market rate of return to equity and debt holders, in order to attract capital.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Alternative Regulation Plan I:</font>&#160;&#160;On September 30, 2008, the PSB issued an order approving our alternative regulation plan.&#160;&#160;The plan became effective on November 1, 2008.&#160;&#160;It expires on December 31, 2011, but we have petitioned for an extension through December, 2013.&#160;&#160;The plan allows for quarterly PCAM adjustment to reflect changes in power supply and transmission-by-others costs); annual base rate adjustments to reflect changing costs; and an annual ESAM adjustment to reflect changes, within predetermined limits, from the allowed earnings level.&#160;&#160;Under the plan, the allowed return on equity is adjusted annually to reflect one-half of the change in the average yield on the 10-year Treasury note as measured over the last 20 trading days prior to October 15 of each year.&#160;&#160;The ESAM provides for the return on equity of the regulated portion of our business to fall between 75 basis points above or below the allowed return on equity before any adjustment is made.&#160;&#160;If the actual return on equity of the regulated portion of our business exceeds 75 basis points above the allowed return, the excess amount is returned to customers in a future period.&#160;&#160;If the actual return on equity of our regulated business falls between 75 and 125 basis points below the allowed return on equity, the shortfall is shared equally between shareholders and customers.&#160;&#160;Any earnings shortfall in excess of 125 basis points below the allowed return on equity is fully recovered from customers.&#160;&#160;As such, the minimum return for our regulated business is 100 basis points below the allowed return.&#160;&#160;These adjustments are made at the end of each fiscal year.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The ESAM also provides for an exogenous effects provision.&#160;&#160;Under this provision,<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font>we are allowed to defer the unexpected impacts, to the extent these costs exceed $0.6 million, of changes in GAAP, tax laws, FERC or ISO-NE rules and major unplanned operation, maintenance costs, such as those due to major storms and other factors including loss of load not due to variations in heating and cooling temperatures.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On December 31, 2009, the PSB issued its order approving our 2010 base rate filing, which increased rates 5.58 percent, effective for bills rendered beginning January 1, 2010. The allowed rate of return for 2010, calculated in accordance with the plan, was 9.59 percent.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On February 2, 2010, the PSB held a prehearing conference, followed by a workshop, to consider the proposal to amend the non-power cost cap formula of our alternative regulation plan to allow for full cost recovery for new initiatives arising after the effective date of the plan. The DPS supported the proposal, and the 2010 base rate filing increase approved by the PSB included recovery of costs for two new initiatives.&#160; On September 3, 2010, the PSB approved the implementation of a new initiatives adder under our alternative regulation plan.&#160;&#160;In order to qualify for treatment as a new initiative the following criteria must be met: 1) the risk associated with implementing the new initiative is of a nature that is distinct from the ordinary business risk that we assume in discharging our public service obligation, and 2) the costs associated with implementing the new initiative are material.&#160;&#160;In our 2010 base rate filing we were allowed recovery of $0.2 million for a new initiative that does not meet the PSB criteria.&#160;&#160;This amount will be returned to customers in 2011.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On November 1, 2010, we submitted two versions of a base rate filing for the rate year beginning January 1, 2011.&#160;&#160;The first version was for a $21.8 million or 7.46 percent increase in retail rates pursuant to our existing alternative regulation plan, reflecting an allowed ROE of 9.18 percent as a result of the existing ROE adjustment formula.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>

This increase was premised upon the PSB approving certain modifications to our existing alternative regulation plan as discussed below in the section titled Alternative Regulation Plan II.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Under our existing alternative regulation plan, the annual change in the non-power costs, as reflected in our base rate filing, is limited to any increase in the U.S. Consumer Price Index for the northeast, less a 1 percent productivity adjustment. The non-power costs associated with the implementation of our Asset Management Plan and our CVPS SmartPower<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">TM</font> project are excluded from the non-power cost cap.&#160;&#160;&#160;Our 2011 non-power costs did not exceed the non-power cost cap.</font></div>

At this time we do not expect that this will result in any change to the 7.46 percent rate increase implemented on January 1, 2011.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Alternative Regulation Plan II:</font>&#160;&#160;On June 30, 2010, we filed a required Alternative Regulation Plan Analysis of Plan Performance with the PSB.&#160; This analysis evaluated the effectiveness of the Plan&#8217;s performance in achieving the goals of Vermont alternative regulation.&#160; As described in the evaluation, the implementation of the current plan has helped to advance these goals; however, we also identified concerns and impediments that limit its overall effectiveness in satisfying all of the objectives of Vermont alternative regulation.&#160;</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">To address these concerns, on July 6, 2010 we petitioned the PSB to approve changes to the current plan to: a) extend its duration; b) alter the methodology for implementing the non-power cost cap; and c) reset the allowed ROE as noted above to 10.22 percent.&#160;&#160;If these changes are approved as initially proposed, the revised plan will expire on December 31, 2013 and the allowed ROE will be reset as of January 1, 2011.&#160;&#160;Thereafter, the existing annual ROE adjustment methodology would apply for the duration of the plan.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The ARP MOU filed on December 21, 2010 would provide final resolution to all issues regarding our petition to modify and extend our existing alternative regulation plan. Under the ARP MOU, the term of the alternative regulation plan would be extended through 2013 and the allowed ROE would be set at 9.59 percent for 2011.&#160;&#160;In addition, the ARP MOU provides for a modification to the alternative regulation plan to include a benchmarking mechanism that affects the non-power cost cap for rate years 2012 and 2013.&#160;&#160;There is also a provision to adjust the non-power cost cap for any cost of service change resulting from an ROE change.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">As discussed above, the PSB felt a meaningful assessment of the ARP MOU could not occur before January 1, 2011 and opened an investigation.&#160;&#160;Technical hearings on the ARP MOU were held on January 5 and 6, 2011.&#160;&#160;We expect to receive a PSB order in the first quarter of 2011.&#160;&#160;The PSB may approve, reject or modify the ARP MOU.&#160;&#160;Based on its ruling on the ARP MOU, the retail rate increase ultimately approved for 2011 may be modified in the investigation.&#160;&#160;By order dated March 3, 2011, the PSB approved further amendments to the alternative regulation plan that: 1) extend its duration until December 31, 2013; 2) alter the methodology for implementing the non-power-cost cap contained in the plan; 3) reset our allowed ROE; and 4) remove provisions no longer applicable to the provision of our services. These amendments are consistent with the terms of an ARP MOU that was filed with the PSB on December 21, 2010, except that the PSB approved an ROE for us for 2011 of 9.45 percent, rather than the 9.59 percent contained in the ARP MOU.&#160;&#160;At this time we do not expect there will be any change to the 7.46 percent rate increase implemented on January 1, 2011.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Staffing Level Investigation</font> On February 13, 2009, the PSB opened an investigation into the staffing levels of the company as requested by us and the DPS.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On November 30, 2009, we filed the Staffing MOU with the PSB setting forth agreements that we reached with the DPS regarding the PSB&#8217;s investigation into our staffing levels. Under the Staffing MOU, in lieu of retaining a management consultant to perform a comprehensive review of our organizational structure and staffing, we and the DPS have agreed that we will reduce our staffing levels over a five-year period by a total of 17 positions as compared to the 549 positions we had on January 1, 2009. This reduction shall be in addition to the staffing reductions contemplated by the implementation of CVPS SmartPower<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">TM</font>. We retain discretion in how to achieve the staffing reductions, and the DPS has agreed that it shall not oppose the recovery in rates of all reasonable costs associated with staffing and related compensation during the term of the Staffing MOU, provided that recovery of such costs is otherwise consistent with normal ratemaking standards. By December 31, 2010 we had reduced staffing levels to 517 employees.&#160;&#160;&#160;Nothing in the Staffing MOU precludes us from seeking to add staff as reasonably necessary in response to new requirements imposed by the state or federal government.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On April 7, 2010, we filed the CVPS SmartPower<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">TM</font> MOU with the PSB that included, among other things, the agreement we reached with the DPS on the recovery of costs we will incur due to CVPS SmartPower<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">TM</font> implementation.&#160;&#160;We received the PSB&#8217;s order approving the cost recovery principles contained in the CVPS SmartPower<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">TM</font> MOU on August 6, 2010.&#160;&#160;On September 3, 2010, the PSB recognized the CVPS SmartPower<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">TM</font> plan as an authorized initiative under the new initiative adder discussed above.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The CVPS SmartPower<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">TM</font> MOU allows us to defer the difference between the actual costs included in the approved CVPS SmartPower<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">TM</font> plan and amounts collected through rates.&#160;&#160;Actual 2010 costs exceeded the amounts collected through rates by less than $0.1 million and were recorded as a regulatory asset.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">LIQUIDITY, CAPITAL RESOURCES AND COMMITMENTS</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Cash Flows </font>At December 31, 2010, we had cash and cash equivalents of $2.7 million and at December 31, 2009, we had cash and cash equivalents of $2.1 million.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our primary sources of cash in 2010 were from our electric utility operations, distributions received from affiliates, income tax refunds, reduced cash collateral deposits, reimbursements from restricted cash of debt-financed project costs, borrowings under our revolving credit facility, net proceeds from our at-the-market common stock issuance program and a long-term debt financing.&#160;&#160;In 2010, we received $1.7 million of federal stimulus fund reimbursements for operating and capital costs from the DOE.&#160;&#160;Our primary uses of cash in 2010 included capital expenditures, investments in affiliates, a restricted cash fund comprised of unreimbursed VEDA bond financing proceeds, common and preferred dividend payments, repayments of borrowings under our revolving credit facility, contributions to the pension and postretirement medical plans and working capital needs.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Operating Activities:</font>&#160;Operating activities provided $53.5 million in 2010, compared to $42.1 million in 2009.&#160;&#160;The increase of $11.4 million was primarily due to: $13.2 million from our 5.58 percent rate increase effective January 1, 2010; lower transmission expenses of $8.9 million due to a higher level of NOATT reimbursements; $7.1 million from replacing power contract-related cash collateral with a letter of credit; $3.5 million in earnings from affiliates resulting from our 2009 investment in Transco; $0.6 million less in employee benefit plan funding due to lower benefit costs in 2010; $0.9 million of federal stimulus funds received in 2010.&#160;&#160;These items were partially offset by $11.3 million less from resale sales as a result of reduced contract rates for resale power sales; $5.2 million increase in operations and maintenance expense from increased storm costs; and a $2.8 million increase in purchased power expense due to the planned outages at the Vermont Yankee and Millstone Unit #3 nuclear plants in 2010.&#160;&#160;We received lower net income tax refunds of $5.7 million in 2010 compared to $6.5 million in 2009.&#160;&#160;Tax refunds in both years primarily related to our elections for federal bonus depreciation on our assets.&#160;&#160;The 2009 tax refunds also included bonus depreciation on our share of Transco assets placed in service during 2008.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Operating activities provided $42.1 million in 2009, compared to $28.4 million in 2008.&#160;&#160;The increase of $13.7 million was primarily due to an increase in earnings and income tax refunds received in 2009.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Cash Flow Risks </font>Based on our current cash forecasts, we will require outside capital in addition to cash flow from operations and our $40 million and $15 million unsecured revolving credit facilities to fund our business over the next few years.&#160;&#160;Prolonged upheaval in the global capital markets could negatively impact our ability to obtain outside capital on reasonable terms.&#160;&#160;If we were ever unable to obtain needed capital, we would re-evaluate and prioritize our planned capital expenditures and operating activities.&#160;&#160;In addition, an extended unplanned Vermont Yankee plant outage or similar event could significantly impact our liquidity due to the potentially high cost of replacement power and performance assurance requirements arising from purchases through ISO-NE or third parties.&#160;&#160;An extended unplanned Vermont Yankee plant outage could involve cost recovery under the PCAM but in general would not be expected to materially impact our financial results, if the costs are recovered in retail rates in a timely fashion.</font></div>

Realty and CRC.&#160;&#160;The purpose of the facility is to provide liquidity for general corporate purposes, including working capital and power contract performance assurance requirements, in the form of funds borrowed and letters of credit.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010, $13.7 million in loans and $5.5 million in letters of credit were outstanding under this credit facility.&#160;&#160;We had periodic borrowings under this facility during 2010.&#160;&#160;In 2011 we intend to renew or replace this facility.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We also have a three-year, $15 million unsecured revolving credit facility with a different lending institution pursuant to a Credit Agreement dated December 22, 2010 that expires in December 2013.&#160;&#160;This facility replaced a 364-day, $15 million unsecured revolving credit facility that matured on December 29, 2010.&#160;&#160;The purpose and obligation under this credit agreement are the same as described above.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010, there were no borrowings or letters of credit outstanding under the credit facility and through December 31, 2010, and we have not used this facility for borrowings or letters of credit.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our first mortgage bond and industrial/economic development bond financing documents do not contain cross-default provisions to affiliates outside of the consolidated entity.&#160;&#160;Certain of our debt financing documents contain cross-default provisions to our wholly owned subsidiaries, East Barnet and C.V. Realty, Inc.&#160;&#160;These cross-default provisions generally relate to an inability to pay debt or debt acceleration, inappropriate affiliate transactions, a breach of warranty or performance of an obligation, or the levy of significant judgments, attachments against our property or insolvency.&#160;&#160;Currently, we are not in default under any of our debt financing documents.&#160;&#160;Scheduled sinking fund payments and maturities for the next five years are $20 million in 2011, $0 in 2012, $5.8 million in 2013, $0 in 2014 and $5 million in 2015.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Industrial/economic development bonds:</font>&#160;&#160;The CDA and VIDA bonds are tax-exempt, floating rate, monthly demand revenue bonds.&#160;&#160;There are no interim sinking fund payments due prior to their maturity.&#160;&#160;The interest rates reset monthly.&#160;&#160;Both series are callable at par as follows: 1) at our option or the bondholders&#8217; option on each monthly interest payment date; or 2) at the option of the bondholders on any business day.&#160;&#160;There is a remarketing feature if the bonds are put for redemption.&#160;&#160;Historically, these bonds have been remarketed in the secondary bond market.&#160;&#160;These two series of bonds are supported by letters of credit, discussed below.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Letters of credit: </font>We have two outstanding unsecured letters of credit, issued by one bank, that support the CDA and VIDA revenue bonds.&#160;&#160;These letters of credit total $11.1 million in support of the two revenue bond issues totaling $10.8 million, discussed above. We pay an annual fee of 2.4 percent on the letters of credit, based on our unsecured issuer rating.&#160;&#160;These letters of credit expire on November 30, 2012. The letters of credit contain cross-default provisions to our wholly owned subsidiaries. These cross-default provisions generally relate to an inability to pay debt or debt acceleration, the levy of significant judgments or insolvency.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010, there were no amounts drawn under these letters of credit.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our credit ratings are influenced by our levels of cash flow and debt, and other factors published by Moody&#8217;s.&#160;&#160;If our rating were to decline to a non-investment-grade level, we could be asked to provide additional collateral in the form of cash or letters of credit primarily under our power contracts or power transactions through ISO-NE.&#160;&#160;&#160;While our current credit facilities are sufficient in amounts that would be required to meet collateral calls at a higher level, our ability to meet any future collateral calls would depend on our liquidity and access to bank credit lines and the capital markets at such time.&#160;&#160;Additionally, a decline in our issuer rating could jeopardize our ability to secure power contracts, including the replacement of our long-term power contracts, at reasonable terms.&#160;&#160;Maintaining our investment-grade ratings is a top priority for us, and Moody&#8217;s has provided clear credit metrics and guidelines used in their consideration of our credit ratings.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">OTHER BUSINESS RISKS</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our ERM program serves to protect our assets, safeguard shareholder investment, ensure compliance with applicable legal requirements and effectively serve our customers.&#160;&#160;The ERM program is intended to provide an integrated and effective governance structure for risk identification and management and legal compliance within the company.&#160;&#160;Among other things, we use metrics to assess key risks, including the potential impact and likelihood of the key risks.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We are also subject to regulatory risk and wholesale power market risk related to our Vermont electric utility business.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Regulatory Risk:</font>&#160;&#160;Historically, electric utility rates in Vermont have been based on a utility&#8217;s costs of service.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, we are entitled to charge rates that are sufficient to allow us an opportunity to recover reasonable operation and capital costs and a reasonable return on investment to attract needed capital and maintain our financial integrity, while also protecting relevant public interests.&#160;&#160;We are subject to certain accounting standards that allow regulated entities, in appropriate circumstances, to establish regulatory assets and liabilities, and thereby defer the income statement impact of certain costs and revenues that are expected to be realized in future rates.&#160;&#160;There is no assurance that the PSB will approve the recovery of all costs incurred for the operation, maintenance, and construction of our regulated assets, as well as a return on investment.&#160;&#160;Adverse regulatory changes could have a significant impact on future results of operations and financial condition.&#160;&#160;See Critical Accounting Policies and Estimates, below</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The State of Vermont has passed several laws since 2005 that impact our regulated business and will continue to impact it in the future.&#160;&#160;Some changes include requirements for renewable energy supplies and opportunities for alternative regulation plans.&#160;&#160;See Recent Energy Policy Initiatives, below.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Power Supply Risk: </font>Our contract for power purchases from VYNPC ends in March 2012, but there is a risk that the plant could be shut down earlier than expected if Entergy-Vermont Yankee determines that it is not economical to continue operating the plant, or due to environmental concerns.&#160; Hydro-Qu&#233;bec contract deliveries through our current contract end in 2016, but the average level of deliveries decreases by approximately 19 percent after 2012, and by approximately 84 percent after 2015.&#160;&#160;In August 2010, we signed a new contract for ongoing Hydro-Qu&#233;bec supplies.&#160;&#160;The agreement is subject to certain government approvals.&#160;&#160;We continue to seek out other power sources but there is a risk that future sources available may not be as reliable and the price of such replacement power could be significantly higher than what we have in place today.&#160;&#160;However, we have been planning for the expiration of these contracts for several years, and a robust effort, described further below, is in place to ensure a safe, reliable, environmentally beneficial and relatively affordable energy supply going forward.&#160;&#160;See Power Supply Matters, below.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Wholesale Power Market Price Risk:</font>&#160;&#160;Our material power supply contracts are with Hydro-Qu&#233;bec and VYNPC.&#160;&#160;These contracts comprise the majority of our total annual MWh purchases.&#160;&#160;If one or both of these sources becomes unavailable for a period of time, there could be exposure to high wholesale power prices and that amount could be material.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We are responsible for procuring replacement energy during periods of scheduled or unscheduled outages of our power sources.&#160;&#160;Average market prices at the times when we purchase replacement energy might be higher than amounts included for recovery in our retail rates.&#160;&#160;We have forced outage insurance through March 21, 2011 to cover additional costs, if any, of obtaining replacement power from other sources if the Vermont Yankee plant experiences unplanned outages.&#160;&#160;We do not plan to renew the outage insurance.&#160;&#160;The PCAM within our alternative regulation plan allows recovery of power costs.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Market Risk: </font>See Part II, Item 7A, Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">CRITICAL ACCOUNTING POLICIES AND ESTIMATES</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The preparation of financial statements in conformity with U.S. GAAP requires management to make estimates and judgments that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities and disclosures of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the financial statements, and reported amounts of revenues and expenses during the reporting period.&#160;&#160;We believe that the areas described below require significant judgment in the application of accounting policy or in making estimates and assumptions in matters that are inherently uncertain and that may change in subsequent periods.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Regulatory Accounting</font>&#160;We prepare the financial statements for our utility operations in accordance with FASB guidance for regulated operations.&#160;&#160;Regulatory assets or liabilities arise as a result of a difference between accounting principles generally accepted in the U.S. and the accounting principles imposed by the regulatory agencies.&#160;&#160;Generally, regulatory assets represent incurred costs that have been deferred as they are probable of recovery in future rates.&#160;&#160;In some circumstances, we record regulatory assets before approval for recovery has been received from the regulatory commission.&#160;&#160;We must use judgment to conclude that costs deferred as regulatory assets are probable of future recovery.&#160;&#160;We base our conclusions on a number of factors including, but not limited to, changes in the regulatory environment, recent rate orders issued and the status of any potential new legislation.&#160;&#160;Regulatory liabilities represent obligations to make refunds to customers or amounts collected in rates for which the costs have not yet been incurred.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The assumptions and judgments used by regulatory authorities may have an impact on the recovery of costs, the rate of return on invested capital and the timing and amount of assets to be recovered by rates.&#160;&#160;A change in these assumptions may have a material impact on our results of operations.&#160;&#160;In the event that we determine our regulated business no longer meets the criteria for regulated operations and there is not a rate mechanism to recover these costs, the impact would be, among other things, a charge to operations of $11.8 million pre-tax at December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;The continued applicability of accounting for regulated operations is assessed at each reporting period. We believe our regulated operations will be subject to this accounting guidance for the foreseeable future.&#160;&#160;Also, see Recent Accounting Pronouncements below.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Valuation of Long-Lived Assets </font>We periodically evaluate the carrying value of long-lived assets, including our investments in nuclear generating companies, our unregulated investments, and our interests in jointly owned generating facilities, when events and circumstances warrant such a review.&#160;&#160;The carrying value of such an asset is considered impaired when the anticipated undiscounted cash flow from the asset is separately identifiable and is less than its carrying value.&#160;&#160;In that event, a loss is recognized in the amount by which the carrying value exceeds the fair value of the long-lived asset.&#160;&#160;No impairments of long-lived assets were recorded in 2010, 2009 or 2008.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Revenues&#160;</font>Revenues from the sale of electricity to retail customers are based on PSB-approved rates.&#160;&#160;Our revenues are recorded when service is rendered or when energy is delivered to customers.&#160;&#160;We accrue revenue based on estimates of electric service rendered and unbilled revenue at the end of each accounting period.&#160;&#160;This unbilled revenue is estimated each month based on daily generation volumes (territory load), estimated line losses and applicable customer rates.&#160;&#160;We estimate line losses at 5.4 percent.&#160;&#160;A one percent change in line losses would result in a $2.9 million change in annual revenues.&#160;&#160;Factors that could affect the estimate of unbilled revenues include seasonal weather conditions, changes in meter reading schedules, the number and type of customers scheduled for each meter reading date, estimated customer usage by class, applicable customer rates and estimated losses of energy during transmission and delivery.&#160;&#160;Unbilled revenues totaled $21 million at December 31, 2010 and $20.8 million at December 31, 2009.&#160;&#160;We believe that these assumptions have resulted in a reasonable approximation of our unbilled revenues and are reasonably likely to continue.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Pension and Postretirement Medical Benefits</font>&#160;FASB&#8217;s accounting guidance for employee retirement benefits requires an employer with a defined benefit plan or other postretirement plan to recognize an asset or liability on its balance sheet for the overfunded or underfunded status of the plan.</font></div>

<br>
<div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160; </font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We use the fair value method to value all asset classes included in our pension and postretirement medical benefit trust funds.&#160;&#160;Assumptions are made regarding the valuation of benefit obligations and future performance of plan assets.&#160;&#160;Delayed recognition of differences between actual results and those assumed is a required principle of these standards.&#160;&#160;This approach allows for systematic recognition of changes in benefit obligations and plan performance over the working lives of the employees who benefit under the plans.&#160;&#160;The following assumptions are reviewed annually, with a December 31 measurement date:</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Discount Rate</font>: The discount rate is used to record the value of benefits, based on future projections, expressed in today&#8217;s dollars.&#160;&#160;The selection methodology used in determining the discount rate includes portfolios of &#8220;Aa&#8221;-rated bonds; all are United States issues and non-callable (or callable with make-whole features) and each issue is at least $50 million in par value.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, the pension discount rate changed from 6 percent to 5.75 percent and the postretirement medical discount rate changed from 5.5 percent to 5.25 percent.&#160;&#160;The conditions in the credit market have been volatile since the third quarter of 2008, and decreases in the discount rates could increase our benefit obligations, which may also result in higher costs and funding requirements.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Expected Return on Plan Assets</font>: We project the future ROA based principally on historical returns by asset category and expectations for future returns, based in part on simulated capital market performance, over the next 10 years.&#160;&#160;The projected future value of assets reduces the benefit obligation a company will record.&#160;&#160;The expected long-term ROA assumption was 7.85 percent as of December 31, 2010 and 2009.&#160;&#160;This rate was also used to determine the annual expense for 2010 and will be used to determine the 2011 expense.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Rate of Compensation Increase:</font> We project employees&#8217; compensation increases, including annual increases, promotions and other pay adjustments, based on our expectations for future long-term experience reflecting general trends.&#160;&#160;This projection is used to estimate employees&#8217; pension benefits at retirement.&#160;&#160;The projected rate of compensation increase was 4.25 percent as of the measurement date in both 2010 and 2009.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Post-retirement Health Care Cost Trend:</font> We project expected increases in the cost of health care.&#160;&#160;We are self-insured, and in recent years have managed costs such that the increases we have experienced have been below the increases at the national level.&#160;&#160;For measuring annual cost, we assumed an 8.5 percent annual rate of increase in the per capita cost of covered health care benefits for fiscal 2010, for pre-age 65 and post-age 65 participant claims costs.&#160;&#160;After three years, the rate is assumed to decrease by 0.5 percent each year, when an estimated ultimate rate of 5 percent is reached in 2019.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Amortization of Gains/(Losses</font>): The assets and liabilities of the pension and postretirement medical benefit plans are affected by changing market conditions as well as differences between assumed and actual plan experience.&#160;&#160;Such events result in gains and losses.&#160;&#160;Investment gains and losses are deferred and recognized in pension and postretirement medical benefit costs over a period of years.&#160;&#160;If, as of the annual measurement date, the plan&#8217;s unrecognized net gain or loss exceeds 10 percent of the greater of the projected benefit obligation or the market-related value of plan assets, the excess is amortized over the average remaining service period of active plan participants.&#160;&#160;This 10-percent corridor method helps to mitigate volatility of net periodic benefit costs from year to year.&#160;&#160;Asset gains and losses related to certain asset classes such as equity, emerging-markets equity, high-yield debt and emerging-markets debt are recognized in the calculation of the market-related value of assets over a five-year period.&#160;&#160;The fixed income assets are invested in longer-duration bonds to match changes in plan liabilities.&#160;&#160;The gains and losses related to this asset class are recognized in the market-related value of assets immediately.&#160;&#160;Also see Part II, Item 8, Note 17 - Pension and Postretirement Medical Benefits.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Fair Value Measurements&#160;</font>We follow FASB&#8217;s fair value guidance that establishes criteria to be considered when measuring the fair value of assets and liabilities and requires disclosures about fair value measurements.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">A fair value hierarchy is used to prioritize the inputs included in valuation techniques. The hierarchy is designed to indicate the relative reliability of the fair value measure. The highest priority is given to quoted prices in active markets, and the lowest to unobservable data, such as an entity&#8217;s internal information. The lower the level of the input of a fair value measurement, the more extensive the disclosure requirements.&#160;&#160;The three broad levels include: quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities (Level 1); significant other observable inputs (Level 2); and significant unobservable inputs (Level 3).</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our assets and liabilities that are recorded at fair value on a recurring basis include cash equivalents and restricted cash consisting of money market funds and other short-term investments, power-related derivatives and our Millstone decommissioning trust.&#160;&#160;Money market funds are classified as Level 1.&#160;&#160;Other short-term investments are classified as Level 2.&#160;&#160;Power-related derivatives are classified as Level 3.&#160;&#160;The Millstone decommissioning trust funds include treasury securities, other agency and corporate fixed income securities and equity securities that are classified as Level 1 and Level 2.&#160;&#160;Our assessment of the significance of a particular input to the fair value measurement requires judgment, and may affect the valuation of the fair value of assets and liabilities and their placement within the fair value hierarchy levels.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">At December 31, 2010, the fair value of money market funds was $1.7 million, the fair value of short-term investments included in restricted cash was $23.5 million and the fair value of decommissioning trust assets was $5.7 million.&#160;&#160;The fair value of power-related derivatives was less than $0.1 million at December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;See Part II, Item 7A, Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk for additional information about power-related derivatives and Part II, Item 8, Note 6 &#8211; Fair Value.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Derivative Financial Instruments</font>&#160;We account for certain power contracts as derivatives under the provisions of FASB&#8217;s guidance for derivatives and hedging. This guidance requires that derivatives be recorded on the balance sheet at fair value.&#160;&#160;Derivatives are recorded as current and long-term assets or liabilities depending on the duration of the contracts.&#160;&#160;Our derivative financial instruments are related to managing our power supply resources to serve our customers, and are not for trading purposes. Contracts that qualify for the normal purchase and sale exception to derivative accounting are not included in derivative assets and liabilities. Additionally, we have not elected hedge accounting for our power-related derivatives.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Based on a PSB-approved Accounting Order, we record the changes in fair value of all power-related derivative financial instruments as deferred charges or deferred credits on the balance sheet, depending on whether the change in fair value is an unrealized loss or gain.&#160;&#160;Realized gains and losses on sales are recorded as increases to or reductions of operating revenues, respectively. For purchase contracts, realized gains and losses are recorded as reductions of or additions to purchased power expense, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our power-related derivatives at December 31, 2010 include annual and monthly financial transmission rights. All of our power-related derivatives are commodity contracts. For additional information about power-related derivatives, see Part II, Item 8, Note 6 - Fair Value and Note 16 - Power-Related Derivatives.</font></div>

</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Income Taxes </font>The application of income tax law is complex and we are required to make many subjective assumptions and judgments in determining our provision for income taxes, deferred tax assets and liabilities, uncertain tax positions and valuation allowances, if applicable.&#160;&#160;We record income tax expense quarterly using an estimated annualized effective tax rate.&#160;&#160;Adjustments to these estimates and changes in our subjective assumptions and judgments can materially affect amounts recognized on the income statement, balance sheet and statement of cash flows.&#160;&#160;See Income Tax Matters below.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Other </font>See Part II, Item 8, Note 2 - Summary of Significant Accounting Policies for a discussion of newly adopted accounting policies and recently issued accounting pronouncements.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">INCOME TAX MATTERS</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Capitalized Repairs Project&#160;</font>The Capitalized Repairs Project included the review of 1999 through 2009 property, plant and equipment additions included in Utility Plant on the Consolidated Balance Sheets.&#160;&#160;The review was performed to identify capitalized additions, which could be expensed, resulting in accelerated income tax deductions.&#160;&#160;In 2010, as a result of our Capitalized Repairs Project, we recorded a $13.6 million increase in prepayments and a $14.2 increase in deferred income tax liabilities on the Consolidated Balance Sheets.&#160;&#160;As of year end, we have requested $10.4 million of income tax refunds which we expect to receive in early 2011.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Since these deductions are temporary timing differences, they normally would not affect total income tax expense or the effective tax rate.&#160;&#160;However, due primarily to a Vermont limitation on the state net operating loss carryforward, we recorded a net increase in combined federal and state GAAP tax expense of $0.7 million.&#160;&#160;This increase in federal and state income tax expense was subsequently reduced to $0.4 million after the establishment of an uncertain tax position as discussed below.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Casualty Loss Refund Claim Settlement</font> During 2007, we determined that we would file amended federal income tax returns totaling $2.8 million for our Casualty Loss refund claims related to the tax years 2003 through 2006.&#160;&#160;We concurrently recorded unrecognized tax benefits of $1.2 million.&#160;&#160;Because of the impact of deferred tax accounting, the disallowance of this item did not affect the effective tax rate.&#160;&#160;Our Casualty Loss refund claims for the tax years 2003 through 2006 were denied during the IRS audit of these years, and were reviewed and settled by IRS Appeals during 2010.&#160;&#160;Our settlement allowed 100 percent of the Casualty Loss refund claims for the tax years 2003 through 2005, which totaled $1.9 million plus $0.4 million interest, and allowed none of the 2006 tax year refund claim.&#160;&#160;In 2010, the remaining Casualty Loss refund unrecognized tax benefit of $1 million was removed from the balance of unrecognized tax benefits.&#160;&#160;See Uncertain Tax Positions below.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Health Care Reform Legislation </font>On March 23, 2010, the federal PPACA was signed into law. The PPACA is a comprehensive health care reform bill that includes revenue-raising provisions for nearly $400 billion over 10 years through tax increases on high-income individuals, excise taxes on high-cost group health plans, and new fees on selected health-care-related industries.&#160;&#160;In addition, on March 25, 2010, the Health Care and Education Affordability Reconciliation Act of 2010 was passed into law, which modifies certain provisions of the PPACA.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Together, the legislation repeals the current rule permitting a tax deduction for prescription drug coverage expense under our postretirement medical plan that is actuarially equivalent to that provided under Medicare Part D.&#160;&#160;This provision is effective for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2012.&#160;&#160;As required, in March 2010 we recorded an increase of $2.1 million in regulatory assets and an increase of $2.8 million in deferred income taxes on the Consolidated Balance Sheets, resulting in an increase of $0.7 million in income tax expense on the Consolidated Statements of Income, related to postretirement medical expenditures that will not be deductible in the future.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Tax Bonus Depreciation&#160;</font>The Small Business Jobs Act of 2010, which became law on September 27, 2010, extended 50 percent bonus depreciation to 2010.&#160;&#160;In addition, as a result of the Tax Relief, Unemployment Insurance Reauthorization, and Job Creation Act of 2010, which became law on December 17, 2010, the 50 percent bonus depreciation was extended through 2012, and a 100 percent expensing was allowed for property placed in service after September 8, 2010 through 2011.&#160;&#160;The combined impact of the additional bonus depreciation allowed as a result of these Acts was $6.7 million that was recorded to prepayments and deferred income tax liabilities on the 2010 Consolidated Balance Sheet.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Uncertain Tax Positions </font>During 2010, unrecognized tax benefits were increased by $2.6 million, which is the net of a $3.6 million increase in unrecognized tax benefits established for our Capitalized Repairs deduction and a $1 million decrease in unrecognized tax benefits due to the settlement of our Casualty Loss claims.&#160;&#160;Due to the impact of deferred tax accounting, the establishment of the $3.6 million Capitalized Repairs unrecognized tax benefit resulted in $0.3 million that would affect the effective tax rate if recognized and the $1 million reduction of the Casualty Loss uncertain tax benefit had no effect on the effective tax rate.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The following is a detailed discussion of the results of operations for the past three years.&#160;&#160;This should be read in conjunction with the consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes included in this report.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic">Consolidated Summary </font>Our consolidated earnings for 2010 were $21 million, or $1.66 per diluted share of common stock.&#160;&#160;This compares to consolidated earnings for 2009 of $20.7 million, or $1.74 per diluted share of common stock and 2008 consolidated earnings of $16.4 million, or $1.52 cents per diluted share of common stock.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Operating Revenues </font>The majority of operating revenues is generated through retail electric sales.&#160;&#160;Retail sales are affected by weather and economic conditions since these factors influence customer use.&#160;&#160;Resale sales represent the sale of power into the wholesale market normally sourced from owned and purchased power supply in excess of that needed by our retail customers. The amount of resale revenue is affected by the availability of excess power for resale, the types of sales we enter into and the price of those sales.&#160;&#160;Operating revenues and related MWh sales are summarized below.</font></div>

These Other costs are amortizations and deferrals based on PSB-approved regulatory accounting, and include net accounting deferrals and amortizations for incremental energy costs related to Millstone Unit #3 scheduled refueling outages and deferrals for our share of nuclear insurance refunds received by VYNPC.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Production:</font>&#160;These costs represent the cost of fuel, operation and maintenance, property insurance, property tax for our wholly and jointly owned production units, and forced outage insurance for the Vermont Yankee plant.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">There was no significant variance for 2010 versus 2009 or for 2009 versus 2008.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Transmission - affiliates:</font> These expenses represent our share of the net cost of service of Transco as well as some direct charges for facilities that we rent.&#160;&#160;Transco allocates its monthly cost of service through the VTA, net of NOATT reimbursements and certain direct charges.&#160;&#160;The NOATT is the mechanism through which the costs of New England&#8217;s high-voltage (so-called PTF) transmission facilities are collected from load-serving entities using the system and redistributed to the owners of the facilities, including Transco.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The decrease of $11.8 million was principally due to higher NOATT reimbursements under the VTA, related to the overall transmission expansion in New England, partially offset by higher charges under the VTA resulting from Transco&#8217;s capital projects.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Transmission - other:&#160;&#160;</font>The majority of these expenses are for purchases of regional transmission service under the NOATT and charges for the Phase I and II transmission facilities.&#160;&#160;The increase of $2.9 million primarily resulted from higher rates and overall transmission expansion in New England.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Other operation</font>: These expenses are related to operating activities such as customer accounting, customer service, administrative and general activities, regulatory deferrals and amortizations and other operating costs incurred to support our core business.&#160;&#160;The decrease of $2.5 million was primarily due to $1.6 million of lower net regulatory amortizations, largely due to an exogenous effect deferral entry of $4.2 million recorded in 2010, comprised of $3.4 million related to major storms and $0.8 million related to income taxes.&#160;&#160;We also had $2.1 million of lower reserves for uncollectible accounts, primarily due to a large customer bankruptcy in 2009 and subsequent recovery of $1.1 million in 2010.&#160;&#160;These decreases were partially offset by $1.2 million of higher employee benefit costs, including higher pension and active employee medical costs, partially offset by lower retiree medical costs.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Maintenance:</font>&#160;&#160;These expenses are associated with maintaining our electric distribution system and include costs of our jointly owned generation and transmission facilities.&#160;&#160;The increase of $5.6 million was largely due to higher service restoration costs related to major storms in 2010.&#160;&#160;We were able to defer $3.4 million of these costs as an exogenous effect deferral as described above in Other operation.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Depreciation:</font> We use the straight-line remaining-life method of depreciation.&#160;&#160;The increase of $0.6 million was due to a higher level of utility plant assets.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Taxes other than income: </font>This is related primarily to property taxes and payroll taxes.&#160;&#160;The increase of $0.7 million was largely due to increases in property taxes.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Income tax expense: </font>Federal and state income taxes fluctuate with the level of pre-tax earnings in relation to permanent differences, tax credits, tax settlements and changes in valuation allowances for the periods.&#160;&#160;The effective combined federal and state income tax rate for 2010 is 41.2 percent compared to 34 percent for 2009 and 39.6 percent for 2008.&#160;&#160;The 2010 versus 2009 variance includes the impact of the PPACA, as modified by the Health Care and Education Reconciliation Act, which represents 2 percent of the 2010 effective tax rate.&#160;&#160;This item is considered an exogenous event and is included in the exogenous effects deferral.&#160;&#160;Also see Part II, Item 8, Note 18 - Income Taxes.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">* variance exceeds 100 percent</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">There was no significant variance for 2010 versus 2009 or for 2009 versus 2008.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">POWER SUPPLY MATTERS</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Power Supply Management </font>Our power supply portfolio includes a mix of baseload and dispatchable resources.&#160;&#160;These resources serve our retail electric load requirements and any wholesale sale obligations into which we enter as part of a hedging strategy.&#160;&#160;We manage our power supply portfolio by attempting to optimize the economic value of these resources and create a balance between our power supplies and load obligations.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our power supply management philosophy is to strike a balance between cost and risk.&#160;&#160;We strive to minimize power costs while simultaneously keeping liquidity risks at conservative levels.&#160;&#160;Risk mitigation strategies are built around minimizing both forward price risks and operational risks while strictly limiting the potential for both our collateral exposure and inefficient deployment of capital.&#160;&#160;Other risks are mitigated by the power and transmission cost recovery process contained in the PCAM (see Retail Rates and Alternative Regulation). We also mitigate price risks through limited wholesale transactions that hedge market price risk, as discussed below.&#160;&#160;In addition, we purchased outage insurance, currently effective through early 2011, to help cover unexpected costs of major unplanned Vermont Yankee outages that could cause the plant to curtail deliveries under the current VY PPA. We do not plan to renew the outage insurance.&#160;&#160;FTR auctions provide us with opportunities to economically hedge our exposure to congestion charges that result from transmission system constraints between generator locations and where load is served.&#160;&#160;FTRs are awarded to successful bidders in periodic auctions that are administered by ISO-NE.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our current power forecast suggests we have excess energy supply during 2011.&#160;&#160;We recently conducted a successful online auction to sell most of our excess energy in the forward market, on a unit-contingent basis, at fixed prices in order to reduce market price volatility and gain a measure of revenue certainty while remaining strictly within potential collateral exposure limits.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Attaining an investment-grade credit rating expanded the available collateral limits with our current counterparties and we have attracted additional counterparties that appear willing to transact with us.&#160;&#160;However, regardless of collateral limits and available counterparties, we expect to maintain our practice of constraining net transaction volumes with individual counterparties to mitigate potential collateral exposures during stressed market conditions.</font></div>
