<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The following is a discussion of our primary sources of energy.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Vermont Yankee:</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>We are purchasing our entitlement share of Vermont Yankee plant output through the VY PPA between Entergy-Vermont Yankee and VYNPC.&#160;&#160;We have one secondary purchaser that receives less than 0.5 percent of our entitlement.&#160;&#160;See Part II, Item 8, Note 4 &#8211; Investments in Affiliates for additional information on the VY PPA.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Entergy-Vermont Yankee has no obligation to supply energy to VYNPC over its entitlement share of plant output, so we receive reduced amounts when the plant is operating at a reduced level, and no energy when the plant is not operating.&#160;&#160;We purchase replacement energy as needed when the Vermont Yankee plant is not operating or is operating at reduced levels.&#160;&#160;We typically acquire most of this replacement energy through forward purchase contracts and account for those contracts as derivatives.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The plant normally shuts down for about one month every 18 months for maintenance and to insert new fuel into the reactor.&#160;&#160;A refueling outage was completed in May 2010 and estimated incremental costs for replacement power were factored into our 2010 base rates.&#160;&#160;Our total VYNPC purchases were $58.7 million in 2010, $64 million in 2009 and $57.7 million in 2008.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We have a forced outage insurance policy to cover additional costs, if any, of obtaining replacement power from other sources if the Vermont Yankee plant experiences unplanned outages.&#160;&#160;The current policy covers March 22, 2010 through March 21, 2011.&#160;&#160;This outage insurance does not apply to derates or acts of terrorism.&#160;&#160;The coverage applies to unplanned outages of up to 90 consecutive calendar days per outage event, and provides for payment of the difference between the hourly spot market price and $42/MWh. The aggregate maximum coverage is $9 million with a $1.2 million deductible. We do not plan to renew the outage insurance.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Prices under the VY PPA increase $1 per megawatt-hour each calendar year and will be $44 per MWh in 2011 and $45 per MWh in 2012.&#160;&#160;The VY PPA contains a provision known as the &#8220;low market adjuster&#8221; that calls for a downward adjustment in the contract price if market prices for electricity fall by defined amounts.&#160;&#160;Estimated annual purchases are expected to be $65.7 million for 2011 and $16.6 million for 2012 when the contract expires in March.&#160;&#160;The total cost estimates are based on projected MWh purchase volumes at PPA rates, plus estimates of VYNPC costs, primarily net interest expense and the cost of capital.&#160;&#160;Actual amounts may differ.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On June 22, 2010, we, along with GMP, made a claim under the September 6, 2001 VY PPA.&#160;&#160;The claim is that Entergy-Vermont Yankee breached its obligations under the agreement by failing to detect and remedy the conditions that resulted in cooling tower-related failures at the Vermont Yankee nuclear plant in 2007 and 2008. Those failures caused us and GMP to incur substantial incremental replacement power costs.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We are seeking recovery of the incremental costs from Entergy-Vermont Yankee under the terms of the VY PPA based upon the results of certain reports, including an NRC inspection, in which the inspection team found that Entergy-Vermont Yankee, among other things, did not have sufficient design documentation available to help it prevent problems with the cooling towers.&#160;&#160;The NRC released its findings on October 14, 2008.&#160;&#160;In considering whether to seek recovery, we also reviewed the 2007 and 2008 root cause analysis reports by Entergy-Vermont Yankee and a December 22, 2008 reliability assessment provided by Nuclear Safety Associates to the State of Vermont.&#160;&#160;Entergy-Vermont Yankee disputes our claim.&#160;&#160;We cannot predict the outcome of this matter at this time.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The VY PPA contains a formula for determining the VYNPC power entitlement following an uprate in 2006 that increased the plant&#8217;s operating capacity by approximately 20 percent.&#160;&#160;VYNPC and Entergy-Vermont Yankee are seeking to resolve certain differences in the interpretation of the formula.&#160;&#160;At issue is how much capacity and energy VYNPC Sponsors receive under the VY PPA following the uprate.&#160;&#160;Based on VYNPC&#8217;s calculations the VYNPC Sponsors should be entitled to slightly more capacity and energy than they have been receiving under the VY PPA since the uprate.&#160;&#160;We cannot predict the outcome of this matter at this time.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our contract for power purchases from VYNPC ends in March 2012, but there is a risk that we could lose this resource if the plant shuts down for any reason before that date. An early shutdown could cause our customers to lose the economic benefit of an energy volume of close to 50 percent of our total committed supply and we would have to acquire replacement power resources for approximately 40 percent of our estimated power supply needs.&#160;&#160;Based on forward market prices as of December 31, 2010, the incremental replacement cost of lost power is estimated to be $14.3 million over the remaining life of the contract.&#160;&#160;We are not able to predict whether there will be an early shutdown of the Vermont Yankee plant or whether the PSB would allow timely and full recovery of increased costs related to such shutdown.&#160;&#160;An early shutdown, depending upon the specific circumstances, could involve recovery of increased costs under the PCAM but, in general, would not be expected to materially impact financial results if the costs are recovered in retail rates in a timely fashion.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On February 24, 2010, in a non-binding vote, the Vermont Senate voted against allowing the PSB to consider granting the Vermont Yankee plant another 20-year operating license after 2012.&#160; The new Vermont Legislature elected on November 2, 2010 could vote differently, although the political makeup of the House and Senate remains largely unchanged.&#160; Also, Vermont elected a new governor who advocated as a member of the Vermont Senate and during the gubernatorial campaign that the Vermont Yankee plant should close when its current license expires.&#160; While circumstances could change and we expect to engage in a constructive dialogue with the new administration and legislature related to the continued operation of the Vermont Yankee plant, we are unable to predict the outcome at this time.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On March 10, 2011, the NRC voted 4-0 to approve the 20-year license extension through March 21, 2032 requested by Entergy-Vermont Yankee.&#160;&#160;This approval removes the last federal level regulatory requirement for relicensing of the Vermont Yankee station.&#160;&#160;However, the Vermont Legislature has not approved the license extension and such approval is considered unlikely at this time.&#160;&#160;Under Vermont law, in addition to a favorable Vermont legislative vote, the PSB needs to issue a Certificate of Public Good for the plant to continue to operate after March 21, 2012.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Entergy-Vermont Yankee is attempting to overcome legislative concerns, but has also recently intimated that it may challenge the state&#8217;s authority as it relates to relicensing.&#160;&#160;In April 2010, we began a new round of negotiations on a new contract.&#160;&#160;While we rejected Entergy-Vermont Yankee&#8217;s December 2009 public proposal of contract terms, we continue to exchange information and proposals with them.&#160;&#160;We cannot predict the outcome of this matter at this time.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Hydro-Qu&#233;bec:</font> We are purchasing power from Hydro-Qu&#233;bec under the VJO power contract.&#160;&#160;The VJO power contract has been in place since 1987 and purchases began in 1990.&#160;&#160;Related contracts were subsequently negotiated between us and Hydro-Qu&#233;bec, altering the terms and conditions contained in the original contract by reducing the overall power requirements and related costs.&#160;&#160;The VJO power contract runs through 2020, but our purchases under the contract end in 2016.&#160;&#160;The average level of deliveries under the current contract decreases by approximately 19 percent after 2012, and by approximately 84 percent after 2015.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The annual load factor is 75 percent for the remainder of the VJO power contract, unless the contract is changed or there is a reduction due to the adverse hydraulic conditions described below.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">There are two sellback contracts with provisions that apply to existing and future VJO power contract purchases.&#160;&#160;The first resulted in the sellback of 25 MW of capacity and associated energy through April 30, 2012, which has no net impact currently since an identical 25 MW purchase was made in conjunction with the sellback. We have a 23 MW share of the 25 MW sellback. However, since the sellback ends six months before the corresponding purchase ends, the first sellback will result in a 23 MW increase in our capacity and energy purchases for the period from May 1, 2012 through October 31, 2012.</font></div>

This second option can be exercised five times through October 2015 but due to the notice provision there is a maximum remaining application of three times available.&#160;&#160;To date, Hydro-Qu&#233;bec has not exercised this option. We have determined that this second option is not a derivative because it is contingent upon a physical variable.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">There are specific contractual provisions providing that in the event any VJO member fails to meet its obligation under the contract with Hydro-Qu&#233;bec, the remaining VJO participants will &#8220;step-up&#8221; to the defaulting party&#8217;s share on a pro-rata basis.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, our obligation is about 47 percent of the total VJO power contract through 2016, and represents approximately $285.7 million, on a nominal basis.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In accordance with FASB&#8217;s guidance for guarantees, we are required to disclose the &#8220;maximum potential amount of future payments (undiscounted) the guarantor could be required to make under the guarantee.&#8221;&#160;&#160;Such disclosure is required even if the likelihood of the event is remote.&#160;&#160;With regard to the &#8220;step-up&#8221; provision in the VJO power contract, we must assume that all members of the VJO simultaneously default in order to estimate the &#8220;maximum potential&#8221; amount of future payments.&#160;&#160;We believe this is a highly unlikely scenario given that the majority of VJO members are regulated utilities with regulated cost recovery.&#160;&#160;Each VJO participant has received regulatory approval to recover the cost of this purchased power contract in its most recent rate applications.&#160;&#160;Despite the remote chance that such an event could occur, we estimate that our undiscounted purchase obligation would be an additional $335.1 million for the remainder of the contract, assuming that all members of the VJO defaulted by January 1, 2011 and remained in default for the duration of the contract.&#160;&#160;In such a scenario, we would then own the power and could seek to recover our costs from the defaulting members or our retail customers, or resell the power in the wholesale power markets in New England.&#160;&#160;The range of outcomes (full cost recovery, potential loss or potential profit) would be highly dependent on Vermont regulation and wholesale market prices at the time.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Total purchases from Hydro-Qu&#233;bec were $63 million in 2010, $63.1 million in 2009 and $63.7 million in 2008.&#160;&#160;Annual capacity costs decreased by $2.2 million starting November 1, 2009, and that cost reduction will continue for six contract years.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Independent Power Producers:</font> <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>We purchase power from several IPPs.&#160;&#160;These plants use water or biomass as fuel.&#160;&#160;Most of the power comes to us through a state-appointed purchasing agent that allocates power to all Vermont utilities under PSB rules.&#160;&#160;Our total purchases from IPPs were $22.9 million in 2010, $22.6 million in 2009 and $26.4 million in 2008.&#160;&#160;Estimated annual purchases are expected to range from $7.7 million to $22.6 million for the years 2011 through 2015.&#160;&#160;Cost will begin to decrease when a major contract obligation ends in 2012.&#160;&#160;These estimates are based on assumptions regarding average weather conditions and other factors affecting generating unit output, so actual amounts may differ.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font><br>
&#160;</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Wholly owned hydro and thermal: </font>Our wholly owned plants are located in Vermont, and have a combined nameplate capacity of about 74.2 MW.&#160;&#160;We operate all of these plants, which include 20 hydroelectric generating facilities with nameplate capacities ranging from a low of 0.3 MW to a high of 7.5 MW, for an aggregate nameplate capacity of 45.3 MW; two oil-fired gas turbines with a combined nameplate capacity of 26.5 MW; and one diesel peaking unit with a nameplate capacity of 2.4 MW, which is currently deactivated.&#160;&#160;In 2009, we upgraded our Arnold Falls unit in St. Johnsbury, VT, investing approximately $1.4 million in the facility.&#160;&#160;The improvements are expected to ensure the plant&#8217;s long-term viability and increase production by about 10 percent.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Jointly owned units:</font> Our jointly owned units include: 1) a 1.7303 percent interest in Unit #3 of the Millstone Nuclear Power Station, a 1,155 MW nuclear generating facility; 2) a 20 percent interest in Joseph C. McNeil, a 54 MW wood-, gas- and oil-fired unit; and 3) a 1.7769 percent joint-ownership in Wyman #4, a 609 MW oil-fired unit.&#160; We account for these units on a proportionate consolidated basis using our ownership interest in each facility.&#160;&#160;Therefore, our share of the assets, liabilities and operating expenses of each facility is included in the corresponding accounts in our consolidated financial statements.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">DNC is the lead owner of Millstone Unit #3 with about 93.4707 percent of the plant joint-ownership.&#160;&#160;The plant&#8217;s operating license has been extended from November 2025 to November 2045.&#160;&#160;We have an external trust dedicated to funding our share of future decommissioning costs, but we have suspended contributions to the Millstone Unit #3 Trust Fund because the minimum NRC funding requirements are being met or exceeded.&#160;&#160;If a need for additional decommissioning funding is necessary, we will be obligated to resume contributions to the Trust Fund.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In August 2008, the NRC approved a request by DNC to increase the Millstone Unit #3 plant&#8217;s generating capacity by approximately 7 percent.&#160;&#160;We are obligated to pay our share of the related costs based on our ownership share described above.&#160;&#160;The uprate was completed during the scheduled refueling outage that concluded in November 2008 and our share of plant output increased by 1.4 MW.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In January 2004 DNC filed, on behalf of itself and the two minority owners, including us, a lawsuit against the DOE seeking recovery of costs related to the storage of spent nuclear fuel arising from the failure of the DOE to comply with its obligations to commence accepting such fuel in 1998.&#160; A trial commenced in May 2008.&#160; On October 15, 2008, the United States Court of Federal Claims issued a favorable decision in the case, including damages specific to Millstone Unit #3.&#160; The DOE appealed the court&#8217;s decision in December 2008.&#160;&#160;On February 20, 2009, the government filed a motion seeking an indefinite stay of the briefing schedule. On March 18, 2009, the court granted the government&#8217;s request to stay the appeal.&#160;&#160;On November 19, 2009, DNC filed a motion to lift the stay.&#160;&#160;On April 12, 2010, the stay was lifted and a staggered briefing schedule was proposed, to which DNC has responded with a request to expedite the briefing schedule so that the appeals of all parties can be heard concurrently.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;On June 30, 2010, the DOE filed its initial brief in the spent fuel damages litigation. This brief focuses on the costs awarded in connection with Millstone Unit #3.&#160;&#160;DNC replied to the government&#8217;s brief in August, 2010.&#160;&#160;The government&#8217;s reply brief was filed September 14, 2010 and briefing on the appeal is now complete.&#160;&#160;Oral argument on the government&#8217;s appeal occurred before the Federal Circuit on January 12, 2011</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We continue to pay our share of the DOE Spent Fuel assessment expenses levied on actual generation and will share in recovery from the lawsuit, if any, in proportion to our ownership interest.&#160;&#160;We expect that our share of a recovery, if any, would be credited to our retail customers.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Other:&#160; </font>Other sources of energy are primarily short-term purchases from third parties in New England and the wholesale markets in ISO-NE.&#160; On an hourly basis, power is sold or bought through ISO-NE to balance our resource output and load requirements through the normal settlement process.&#160; On a monthly basis, we aggregate hourly sales and purchases and record them as operating revenues and purchased power, respectively.&#160; We are also charged for a number of ancillary services through ISO-NE, including costs for congestion, line losses, reserves and regulation that vary in part due to changes in the price of energy.&#160; The methods for settling the costs of ancillary services are administered by ISO-NE and are subject to change.&#160; Congestion and loss charges represent costs related to our power generation, purchase and delivery of energy to customers and reflect energy prices, customer demand, and the demands on transmission and generation resources.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">ISO-NE has a market mechanism referred to as the FCM to compensate owners of new and existing generation capacity, including demand reduction.&#160; ISO-NE believes that higher capacity payments in constrained areas will encourage the development of new generation where needed. Capacity requirements for load-serving entities, including us, are currently based on each entity&#8217;s percentage share of ISO-NE&#8217;s prior year coincident peak demand&#160;and the amount of qualifying capacity in the pool. Net FCM charges in 2010 were about $3.4 million.&#160;&#160;Based on specified rates through December, 2011, we expect net FCM charges of about $3.2 million.&#160;</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We continue to monitor potential changes to the rules in the wholesale energy markets in New England.&#160; Such changes could have a material impact on power supply costs.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Future Power Agreements</font>&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">New Hydro-Qu&#233;bec</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Agreement:</font>&#160;&#160;On August 12, 2010 we, along with GMP, VPPSA, Vermont Electric Cooperative, Inc., Vermont Marble, Town of Stowe Electric Department, City of Burlington, Vermont Electric Department, Washington Electric Cooperative, Inc and the 13 municipal members of VPPSA (collectively, the &#8220;Buyers&#8221;) entered into an agreement for the purchase of shares of 218 MW to 225 MW of energy and environmental attributes from HQUS commencing on November 1, 2012 and continuing through 2038.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The rights and obligations of the Buyers under the HQUS PPA, including payment of the contract price and indemnification obligations, are several and not joint or joint and several. Therefore, we shall have no responsibility for the obligations, financial or otherwise, of any other party to the HQUS PPA. The parties have also entered into related agreements, including collateral agreements between each Buyer and HQUS, a Hydro-Qu&#233;bec guaranty, an allocation agreement among the Buyers, and an assignment and assumption agreement between us and Vermont Marble, related to the pending acquisition.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The HQUS PPA will replace approximately 65 percent of the existing VJO power contract discussed above, which along with the VY PPA supply the majority of Vermont&#8217;s current power needs. The VJO power contract and the VY PPA expire within the next several years.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Under the Agreement, subject to regulatory approval, we would be entitled to purchase an energy quantity of up to 85.4 MW from November 1, 2015 to October 31, 2016; 96.4 MW from November 1, 2016 to October 31, 2020; 98.4 MW from November 1, 2020 to October 31, 2030; 112.1 MW from November 1, 2030 to October 31, 2035; and 26.7 MW from November 1, 2035 to October 31, 2038.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Other Future Power Agreements:&#160;&#160;</font>As we continue to build and diversify our power portfolio as planned and to comply with state law which establishes goals for including renewable power in our mix, we have recently signed several agreements for clean and competitively priced renewable energy.&#160;&#160;On September 9, 2010 we agreed to terms for purchasing output over nine years from Iberdrola Renewables&#8217; planned Deerfield Wind Project.&#160;&#160;The agreement was signed by the parties December 13, 2010.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Other recently signed agreements include: two separate agreements to purchase 30.3 percent of the actual output from Granite Reliable Wind project for 20 years beginning April 1, 2012 and an additional 20 percent for 15 years beginning in November 2012; an agreement to purchase the entire 4.99 MW output of Ampersand Gilman Hydro for five years starting April 1, 2012; and 15 MW of around-the-clock energy from J.P. Morgan Ventures Energy for the calendar years 2013 through 2015.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Decommissioned Nuclear Plants</font> We own, through equity investments, 2 percent of Maine Yankee, 2 percent of Connecticut Yankee and 3.5 percent of Yankee Atomic.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, all three have completed decommissioning activities and their operating licenses have been amended to operation of Independent Spent Fuel Storage Installation.&#160;&#160;They remain separately responsible for safe storage of each plant&#8217;s spent nuclear fuel and waste at the sites until the DOE meets its obligation to remove the material from the site or until some other suitable storage arrangement can be developed.&#160;&#160;All three collect decommissioning and closure costs through FERC-approved wholesale rates charged under power purchase agreements with several New England utilities, including us.&#160;&#160;We believe that, based on historical rate recovery, our share of decommissioning and closure costs for each plant will continue to be recovered through the regulatory process.&#160;&#160;However, if the FERC disallows recovery of any of their costs, there is a risk that the PSB would disallow recovery of our share in retail rates.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Based on estimates from Maine Yankee, Connecticut Yankee and Yankee Atomic as of December 31, 2010, the total remaining approximate cost for decommissioning and other costs of each plant is as follows: $32.5 million for Maine Yankee, $219.1 million for Connecticut Yankee and $51.2 million for Yankee Atomic.&#160;&#160;Our share of the remaining obligations amounts to $0.6 million for Maine Yankee, $4.4 million for Connecticut Yankee and $1.8 million for Yankee Atomic.&#160;&#160;These estimates may be revised from time to time based on information available regarding future costs.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">All three companies have been seeking recovery of fuel storage-related costs stemming from the default of the DOE under the 1983 fuel disposal contracts that were mandated by the United States Congress under the Nuclear Waste Policy Act of 1982.&#160;&#160;Under the Act, the companies believe the DOE was required to begin removing spent nuclear fuel and greater than Class C waste from the nuclear plants no later than January 31, 1998 in return for payments by each company into the nuclear waste fund.&#160;&#160;No fuel or greater than Class C waste has been collected by the DOE, and each company&#8217;s spent fuel is stored at its own site.&#160;&#160;Maine Yankee, Connecticut Yankee and Yankee Atomic collected the funds from us and other wholesale utility customers, under FERC-approved wholesale rates, and our share of these payments was collected from our retail customers.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In 2006, the United States Court of Federal Claims issued judgment in the spent fuel litigation.&#160;&#160;Maine Yankee was awarded $75.8 million in damages through 2002, Connecticut Yankee was awarded $34.2 million through 2001 and Yankee Atomic was awarded $32.9 million through 2001.&#160;&#160;In December 2006, the DOE filed a notice of appeal of the court&#8217;s decision and all three companies filed notices of cross appeals.&#160;&#160;In August 2008, the United States Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit reversed the award of damages and remanded the cases back to the trial court.&#160;&#160;The remand directed the trial court to apply the acceptance rate in 1987 annual capacity reports when determining damages.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On March 6, 2009, the three companies submitted their revised statement of claimed damages for the case on remand.&#160;&#160;Maine Yankee claimed $81.7 million through 2002, Connecticut Yankee claimed $39.7 million and Yankee Atomic claimed $53.9 million in damages through 2001.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The trial phase of the remanded case occurred in August 2009.&#160;&#160;Post-trial briefing was completed in early November 2009, and final arguments were heard on December 10, 2009.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">A final ruling in favor of the three companies was issued on September 7, 2010.&#160;&#160;Maine Yankee was awarded $81.7 million, Connecticut Yankee was awarded $39.7 million and Yankee Atomic was awarded $21.2 million.&#160;&#160;The DOE filed an appeal on November 8, 2010 and the three Yankee companies filed cross-appeals on November 19, 2010.&#160;&#160;Interest on the judgments does not start to accrue until all appeals have been decided.&#160;&#160;Our share of the claimed damages of $3.2 million is based on our ownership percentages described above.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Court of Federal Claims&#8217; original decision established the DOE&#8217;s responsibility for reimbursing Maine Yankee for its actual costs through 2002 and Connecticut Yankee and Yankee Atomic for their actual costs through 2001 related to the incremental spent fuel storage, security, construction and other costs of the spent fuel storage installation.&#160;&#160;Although the decision did not resolve the question regarding damages in subsequent years, the decision did support future claims for the remaining spent fuel storage installation construction costs.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In December 2007, Maine Yankee, Connecticut Yankee and Yankee Atomic filed additional claims against the DOE for unspecified damages incurred for periods subsequent to the original case discussed above.&#160;&#160;On July 1, 2009, in a notification to the DOE, Maine Yankee, Connecticut Yankee and Yankee Atomic filed their claimed costs for damages.&#160;&#160;Maine Yankee claimed $43 million since January 1, 2003 and Connecticut Yankee and Yankee Atomic claimed $135.4 million and $86.1 million, respectively since January 1, 2002.&#160;&#160;For all three companies the damages were claimed through December 31, 2008. A trial date has been set for the beginning of August 2011.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Due to the complexity of these issues and the potential for further appeals, the three companies cannot predict the timing of the final determinations or the amount of damages that will actually be received.&#160;&#160;Each of the companies&#8217; respective FERC settlements requires that damage payments, net of taxes and further spent fuel trust funding, if any, be credited to wholesale ratepayers including us.&#160;&#160;We expect that our share of these awards, if any, would be credited to our retail customers.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">TRANSMISSION MATTERS</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">As a load-serving entity in Vermont, we are required to share the costs of facilities used to transmit power to our system, including the region&#8217;s qualifying PTF network, the state&#8217;s non-PTF network and facilities that we utilize that are owned by individual utilities and generators.&#160;&#160;These are all referred to as TbyO.&#160;&#160;Our greatest TbyO cost is for our share of the region&#8217;s high-voltage PTF transmission system through payments made under the NOATT.&#160;&#160;Our obligation is based on our percentage share of regional peak loads and the total PTF cost of service. The total PTF cost has increased significantly in recent years so that our average 1.8 percent share now yields an annual NOATT charge of over $20 million. While this regional cost-sharing approach greatly reduces our costs related to qualifying Vermont transmission facilities, we pay our share of the costs of all new and existing NOATT-qualifying facilities located throughout New England.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In recent years there have been a number of major transmission projects in Vermont undertaken by Transco, some of which are already in service.&#160;&#160;The majority of the costs of these projects are classified as PTF and have been approved by NEPOOL for NOATT cost-sharing treatment. However, certain Vermont transmission facilities do not qualify for such cost sharing.&#160;&#160;Our share of the costs of these local facilities is charged through the VTA and is determined by the classification of each project.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Transco has been working with us on a project to solve load-serving and reliability issues related to a 46-kV transmission line extending from Bennington to Brattleboro, Vermont, which we refer to as the Southern Loop.&#160;&#160;It serves about 25 percent of our load.&#160;&#160;We initiated a public engagement process in late 2005 to gain input on how best to improve and ensure reliable electric service in southern Vermont.&#160;&#160;Based on input from this process, in the fourth quarter of 2006 we filed a petition with the PSB for approval to purchase and install two synchronous condensers along the Southern Loop.&#160;&#160;This project was approved by the PSB in April 2008.&#160;&#160;Work commenced in June 2008 and was completed in February 2009.&#160;&#160;The condensers are rotating machines similar to motors used to provide reactive support on the electric power transmission systems without burning fuel.&#160;&#160;The condensers have improved the reliability in the Stratton/Manchester area of the Southern Loop.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Transco also worked with us on a proposal to construct additional transmission lines in the area to improve reliability to the Brattleboro area of the Southern Loop.&#160;&#160;This included the construction of a new line in the existing 345 kV corridor between Vermont Yankee in Vernon and our substation in Coolidge.&#160;&#160;The plan also included a new substation in Vernon and an expansion of the Coolidge Substation.&#160;&#160;These components are collectively known as the &#8220;Coolidge Connector.&#8221;</font></div>

<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160; </font></div>

<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160; </font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">To address local reliability problems on our system, on February 12, 2009 the PSB also approved construction of a new substation in Newfane and a 345 kV loop between the new substation and the 345 kV Vernon-to-Cavendish line.&#160;&#160;The effort to involve the public in a meaningful dialogue about these issues has been hailed as a vast improvement over previous project-review processes.&#160;&#160;We believe this new way of conducting business led to better solutions, lower costs, and improved community relations.&#160;&#160;In fact, a statewide transmission planning committee was created in the wake of the Southern Loop outreach effort, patterned in many respects after it.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The RTO for New England began operating on February 1, 2005 pursuant to FERC Order 2000.&#160;&#160;We are a participant in this organization, which provides the PTF service on a non-discriminatory basis throughout New England via the NOATT.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Under the RTO, the Highgate Converter and related facilities owned by a number of Vermont utilities, including us, and Transco are classified as the Highgate Transmission Facility with RNS reimbursement treatment.&#160;&#160;Our net cost for the Highgate facilities is based on our NEPOOL network load share (about 2 percent) rather than our 48 percent ownership share of the facilities.&#160;&#160;Our share of reimbursements is about $3.7 million a year.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">RECENT ENERGY POLICY INITIATIVES</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In 2005, the state of Vermont created a renewable energy mandate under SPEED.&#160;&#160;The primary SPEED goal is that, by January 1, 2012, Vermont utilities produce or purchase energy equal to 5 percent of the 2005 electricity sales, plus sales growth since then, from small-scale solar, wind, hydro and methane energy production.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">An additional SPEED goal is that, by 2017, SPEED resources account for 20 percent of Vermont&#8217;s electricity sales.&#160;&#160;The SPEED goal is a statewide target, rather than something specific to each utility.&#160;&#160;We believe we are on pace to achieve the 2012 SPEED targets.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In May, 2009, the Vermont Legislature amended the SPEED law to create a Feed-In Tariff rate for SPEED resources smaller than 2.2 MW in capacity.&#160;&#160;Feed-In Tariff rates are available for a maximum of 50 MW of capacity.&#160;&#160;The incremental cost of electricity from Feed-In Tariff projects is to be borne proportionately by all Vermont utilities except Washington Electric Cooperative, which was exempted from the program.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In May 2010, the Vermont Legislature amended the SPEED law to allow existing farm methane generators (including our &#8220;Cow Power&#8221; generators) to qualify for the Feed-In Tariff.&#160;&#160;We supported this action.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The 2010 Legislature also repealed a Vermont law that precluded hydroelectric facilities with capacity above 80 MW from being considered as &#8220;renewable&#8221; resources.&#160;&#160;While there are no such facilities in Vermont, CVPS purchases power from Hydro-Qu&#233;bec, which does operate facilities larger than 80 MW.&#160;&#160;We anticipate no immediate impact from this change in policy.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">RECENT ACCOUNTING PRONOUNCEMENTS AND TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Dodd-Frank Act</font> On July 21, 2010, the Dodd-Frank Act was signed into law. While the Dodd-Frank Act has broad implications to the financial services industry, there are some new mandates for public companies that may require changes in corporate governance, compensation, government regulation of the over-the-counter derivatives market, accounting and other areas.&#160;&#160;The regulations implementing the Dodd-Frank Act have not yet been drafted; however the SEC has begun issuing concept releases under certain provisions.&#160;&#160;We have already implemented changes related to non-binding shareholder advisory votes on executive compensation and compensation and benefit plan risk assessments.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Act requires entities to clear most over-the-counter derivatives through regulated central clearing organizations and to trade the derivatives on regulated exchanges.&#160;&#160;In September 2010, we filed for a waiver of the Dodd-Frank provision that ends the exemption under Section 2(h) of the Commodity Exchange Act.&#160;&#160;If granted, an extension of time will be provided, exempting us while regulatory rulemaking is taking place and while we evaluate whether our derivatives are subject to the regulations in the Commodity Exchange Act or as adjusted in the Dodd-Frank Act.&#160;&#160;Even with this exemption, however, we may be subject to reporting requirements pursuant to an interim rule due out soon that will pertain to swap arrangements entered into before the Dodd-Frank Act.&#160;&#160;We are monitoring and evaluating developments to ensure compliance with any such reporting requirements.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We are uncertain to what degree this legislation may affect our business in the future, but we are evaluating these additional regulatory requirements and the potential impact on our financial statements.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">FASB &#8211; IASB Convergence </font>The FASB and IASB are working on joint projects to bring U.S. GAAP closer to IFRS, resulting in a major overhaul and reshaping of U.S. GAAP.&#160; The FASB&#8217;s project plan anticipates the completion of many projects in 2011; however, it will consider staggering the effective dates of new standards to ensure an orderly transition to any new requirements.&#160;&#160;We have not yet evaluated the impact, if any, that the adoption of the new standards may have on our consolidated financial statements.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On February 24, 2010, the SEC issued a statement of its position regarding global accounting standards.&#160; Among other things, the SEC stated that it has directed its staff to execute a work plan, which will include consideration of IFRS as it exists today and after the completion of various convergence projects currently underway between U.S. and international accounting standards-setters.&#160; During 2011, the SEC is expected to provide an update on their work plan.&#160;&#160;If the SEC determines in 2011 to move forward with IFRS, the first time that U.S. companies would report under such a system would be no earlier than 2015.&#160; If so, since we are an accelerated filer, we would be required to adopt IFRS in 2016.&#160;</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Also, see Part II, Item 8, Note 2 - Summary of Significant Accounting Policies.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline"><a name="Item7a">Item 7A.</a>&#160;&#160;Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The matters discussed in this item may contain forward-looking statements as described in our &#8220;Cautionary Statement Regarding Forward-Looking Information&#8221; section preceding Part I, Item 1, Business of this Form 10-K.&#160;&#160;Also see Part I, Item 1A, Risk Factors.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We consider our most significant market-related risks to be associated with wholesale power markets, equity markets and interest rates.&#160;&#160;Although 2008 was a challenging year in the financial markets with record low market returns and extraordinary volatility, the markets began to stabilize and trend toward more normal performance in the second half of 2009 and throughout 2010.&#160;&#160;Further decreases in the values of the assets in our pension, postretirement medical and nuclear decommissioning trust funds could increase our future cash outflows related to trust fund contributions.&#160;&#160;Fair and adequate rate relief through cost-based rate regulation can limit our exposure to market volatility.&#160;&#160;Below is a discussion of the primary market-related risks associated with our business.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Investment Price Risk</font>&#160;We are subject to investment price risk associated with equity market fluctuations and interest rate changes.&#160;&#160;Those risks are described in more detail below.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Interest Rate Risk:&#160;&#160;</font>&#160;Interest rate changes could impact the value of the debt securities in our pension and postretirement medical benefit trust funds and the valuations of estimated pension and other benefit liabilities, affecting pension and other benefit expenses, contributions to the external trust funds and ultimately our ability to meet future pension and postretirement benefit obligations.&#160;&#160;We have adopted a diversified investment policy with a goal to mitigate these market impacts.&#160;&#160;See Part II, Item 7, Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations, Critical Accounting Policies and Estimates, and Part II, Item 8, Note 17 - Pension and Postretirement Medical Benefits.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Interest rate changes could also impact the value of the debt securities in our Millstone Unit #3 decommissioning trust and in our Rabbi Trust.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010, the decommissioning trust held debt securities in the amount of $1.3 million and the Rabbi Trust held debt securities in the amount of $2.4 million.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">As of December 31, 2010, we had $10.8 million of Industrial Development Revenue bonds outstanding, which have an interest rate that resets monthly.&#160;&#160;The interest rate amounts borrowed at year end under our $40 million credit facility resets daily.&#160;&#160;All other utility debt has a fixed rate.&#160;&#160;There are no interest rate locks or swap agreements in place.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The table below provides information about interest rates on our long-term debt.&#160;&#160;The expected variable rates are based on rates in effect at December 31, 2010 (dollars in millions).</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Currently, our power forecast shows energy purchase and production amounts in excess of our load requirements through 2011.&#160;&#160;Because of this projected power surplus, we enter into forward sale transactions from time to time to reduce price volatility of our net power costs.&#160;&#160;The effect of increases or decreases in average wholesale power market prices is highly dependent on whether our net power resources at the time are sufficient to meet load requirements.&#160;&#160;If they are not sufficient to meet load requirements, such as when power from Vermont Yankee is not available as expected, we are in a purchase position.&#160;&#160;In that case, increased wholesale power market prices would increase our net power costs.&#160;&#160;If our net power resources are sufficient to meet load requirements, we are in a sale position.&#160;&#160;In that case, increased wholesale power market prices would decrease our net power costs.&#160;&#160;The PCAM within our alternative regulation plan allows more timely recovery of our power costs in 2009, 2010 and 2011.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">REPORT OF INDEPENDENT REGISTERED PUBLIC ACCOUNTING FIRM</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">To the Board of Directors and Stockholders of</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Central Vermont Public Service Corporation</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheets of Central Vermont Public Service Corporation and subsidiaries (the "Company") as of December 31, 2010 and 2009, and the related consolidated statements of income, comprehensive income, changes in common stock equity, and cash flows for each of the three years in the period ended December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;These consolidated financial statements are the responsibility of the Company's management.&#160; Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the consolidated financial statements based on our audits.&#160;&#160;We did not audit the financial statements of Vermont Transco LLC (&#8220;Transco&#8221;) and Vermont Electric Power Company, Inc. (&#8220;Velco&#8221;), the Company&#8217;s investments in which are accounted for by use of the equity method.&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s equity of $168,500,000 and $126,742,000 in Transco&#8217;s and Velco&#8217;s net assets as of December 31, 2010 and 2009, respectively, and of $20,795,000, $17,124,000 and $16,102,000 in Transco&#8217;s and Velco&#8217;s net income for each of the three years in the period ended December 31, 2010, are included in the accompanying consolidated financial statements.&#160;&#160;Those financial statements were audited by other auditors whose reports (which as to Velco included an explanatory paragraph concerning a change in accounting for non-controlling interests) have been furnished to us, and our opinion, insofar as it relates to the amounts included for Transco and Velco, is based solely on the reports of other auditors.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States).&#160; Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement.&#160; An audit includes examining, on a test basis, evidence supporting the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements.&#160; An audit also includes assessing the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall financial statement presentation.&#160; We believe that our audits and the reports of other auditors provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In our opinion, based on our audits and the reports of other auditors, such consolidated financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of Central Vermont Public Service Corporation and subsidiaries as of December 31, 2010 and 2009, and the results of their operations and their cash flows for each of the three years in the period ended December 31, 2010, in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We have also audited, in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States), the Company's internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2010, based on the criteria established in <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Internal Control&#8212;Integrated Framework</font> issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission and our report dated March 14, 2011 expressed an unqualified opinion on the Company's internal control over financial reporting.</font></div>

<br>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">CENTRAL VERMONT PUBLIC SERVICE CORPORATION</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">NOTE 1 - BUSINESS ORGANIZATION</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">General Description of Business </font>Central Vermont Public Service Corporation (&#8220;we&#8221;, &#8220;us&#8221;, &#8220;CVPS&#8221; or the &#8220;company&#8221;) is the largest electric utility in Vermont.&#160;&#160;We engage principally in the purchase, production, transmission, distribution and sale of electricity.&#160;&#160;We serve approximately 159,000 customers in 163 of the towns and cities in Vermont.&#160;&#160;Our Vermont utility operation is our core business.&#160;&#160;We typically generate most of our revenues through retail electricity sales.&#160;&#160;We also sell excess power, if any, to third parties in New England and to ISO-NE, the operator of the region&#8217;s bulk power system and wholesale electricity markets.&#160;&#160;The resale revenue generated from these sales helps to mitigate our power supply costs.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our wholly owned subsidiaries include C.V. Realty, Inc., East Barnet and CRC.&#160;&#160;We have equity ownership interests in VYNPC, VELCO, Transco, Maine Yankee, Connecticut Yankee and Yankee Atomic.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">NOTE 2 - SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Basis of Presentation&#160;</font>These audited financial statements have been prepared pursuant to the rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission and in accordance U.S. GAAP.&#160;&#160;The accompanying consolidated financial statements contain all normal, recurring adjustments considered necessary to present fairly the financial position as of December 31, 2010, and the results of operations and cash flows for the years ended December 31, 2010, 2009 and 2008. These consolidated financial statements should be read in conjunction with the accompanying notes.&#160;&#160;We consider events or transactions that occur after the balance sheet date, but before the financial statements are issued, to provide additional evidence relative to certain estimates or to identify matters that require additional disclosure.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Financial Statement Presentation </font>The focus of the Consolidated Statements of Income is on the regulatory treatment of revenues and expenses of the regulated utility as opposed to other enterprises where the focus is on income from continuing operations.&#160;&#160;Operating revenues and expenses (including related income taxes) are those items that ordinarily are included in the determination of revenue requirements or amounts recoverable from customers in rates.&#160;&#160;Operating expenses represent the costs of rendering service to be covered by revenue, before coverage of interest and other capital costs.&#160;&#160;Other income and deductions include non-utility operating results, certain expenses judged not to be recoverable through rates, related income taxes and costs (i.e. interest expense) that utility operating income is intended to cover through the allowed rate of return on equity rather than as a direct cost-of-service revenue requirement.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The focus of the Consolidated Balance Sheets is on utility plant and capital because of the capital-intensive nature of the regulated utility business.&#160;&#160;The prominent position given to utility plant, capital stock, retained earnings and long-term debt supports regulated ratemaking concepts in that utility plant is the rate base and capitalization (including long-term debt) is the basis for determining the rate of return that is applied to the rate base.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Please refer to the Glossary of Terms following the Table of Contents for frequently used abbreviations and acronyms that are found in this report.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Basis of Consolidation&#160;</font>The accompanying consolidated financial statements include the accounts of the company and its wholly owned subsidiaries.&#160;&#160;Inter-company transactions have been eliminated in consolidation.&#160;&#160;Jointly owned generation and transmission facilities are accounted for on a proportionate consolidated basis using our ownership interest in each facility.&#160;&#160;Our share of the assets, liabilities and operating expenses of each facility are included in the corresponding accounts on the accompanying consolidated financial statements.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Investments in entities over which we do not maintain a controlling financial interest are accounted for using the equity method when we have the ability to exercise significant influence over their operations.&#160;&#160;Under this method, we record our ownership share of the net income or loss of each investment in our consolidated financial statements.&#160;&#160;We have concluded that consolidation of these investments is not required under FASB&#8217;s consolidation guidance for variable interest entities.&#160;&#160;See Note 4 - Investments in Affiliates.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Variable Interest Entities </font>The primary beneficiary of a variable interest entity must consolidate the financial statements of that entity.&#160;&#160;Transco and VYNPC are variable interest entities; however, we are not the primary beneficiary of either of these entities because we do not control the activities that are most relevant to their operating results.&#160;&#160;Our maximum exposure to loss is the amount of our equity investments in Transco and VYNPC.&#160;&#160;See Note 4 - Investments in Affiliates.</font></div>

<br>

<div id="FTR">

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160; </font></div>
