<br>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Use of Estimates</font> The preparation of financial statements in accordance with U.S. GAAP requires us to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities, disclosures of contingent assets and liabilities, and revenues and expenses.&#160;&#160;Actual results could differ from those estimates.&#160;&#160;In our opinion, areas where significant judgment is exercised include the valuation of unbilled revenue, pension plan assumptions, nuclear plant decommissioning liabilities, environmental remediation costs, regulatory assets and liabilities, and derivative contract valuations.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Regulatory Accounting</font>&#160;Our utility operations are regulated by the PSB, FERC and the Connecticut Department of Public Utility and Control, with respect to rates charged for service, accounting, financing and other matters pertaining to regulated operations.&#160;&#160;As required, we prepare our financial statements in accordance with FASB&#8217;s guidance for regulated operations.&#160;&#160;The application of this guidance results in differences in the timing of recognition of certain expenses from those of other businesses and industries.&#160;&#160;In order for us to report our results under the accounting for regulated operations, our rates must be designed to recover our costs of providing service, and we must be able to collect those rates from customers.&#160;&#160;If rate recovery of the majority of these costs becomes unlikely or uncertain, whether due to competition or regulatory action, we would reassess whether this accounting standard should continue to apply to our regulated operations.&#160;&#160;In the event we determine that we no longer meet the criteria for applying the accounting for regulated operations, the accounting impact would be a charge to operations of an amount that would be material unless stranded cost recovery is allowed through a rate mechanism.&#160;&#160;Based on a current evaluation of the factors and conditions expected to impact future cost recovery, we believe future recovery of our regulatory assets is probable.&#160;&#160;Criteria that could give rise to the discontinuance of accounting for regulated operations include: 1) increasing competition that restricts a company&#8217;s ability to establish prices to recover specific costs, and 2) a significant change in the manner in which rates are set by regulators from cost-based regulation to another form of regulation.&#160;&#160;In the event that we no longer meet the criteria under the guidance for regulated operations and there is not a rate mechanism to recover these costs, the impact would, among other things, result in a charge to operations of $11.8 million pre-tax at December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;See Note 9 - Retail Rates and Regulatory Accounting for additional information.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Unregulated Business </font>Our non-regulated business, SmartEnergy Water Heating Services, Inc., is a water heater rental business operating in portions of Vermont and New Hampshire.&#160;&#160;This non-regulated business is a subsidiary of CRC.&#160;&#160;Results of operations are included in Other Income and Other Deductions on the Consolidated Statements of Income.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Income Taxes </font>In accordance with FASB&#8217;s guidance for income tax accounting, we recognize deferred tax assets and liabilities for the cumulative effect of all temporary differences between financial statement carrying amounts and the tax basis of existing assets and liabilities using the tax rate expected to be in effect when the differences are expected to reverse.&#160;&#160;Investment tax credits associated with utility plant are deferred and amortized ratably to income over the lives of the related properties.&#160;&#160;We record a valuation allowance for deferred tax assets if we determine that it is more likely than not that such tax assets will not be realized.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We follow FASB&#8217;s guidance and methodology for estimating and reporting amounts associated with uncertain tax positions, including interest and penalties.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Revenue Recognition </font>Revenues from the sale of electricity to retail customers are recorded when service is rendered or electricity is distributed.&#160;&#160;These are based on monthly meter readings, and estimates are made to accrue unbilled revenue at the end of each accounting period.&#160;&#160;We record contractual or firm wholesale sales in the month that power is delivered.&#160;&#160;We also engage in hourly sales and purchases in the wholesale markets administered by ISO-NE through the normal settlement process.&#160;&#160;On a monthly basis, we aggregate these hourly sales and hourly purchases and report them as operating revenue and operating expenses.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Allowance for Uncollectible Accounts</font>&#160;We record allowances for uncollectible accounts based on customer-specific analysis, current assessments of past due balances and economic conditions, and historical experience.&#160;&#160;Additional allowances for uncollectible accounts may be required if there is deterioration in past due balances, if economic conditions are less favorable than anticipated, or for customer-specific circumstances, such as financial difficulty or bankruptcy.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010, our allowance for uncollectible accounts was $2.6 million, compared to $3.6 million at December 31, 2009.&#160;&#160;The change was largely due to a large customer bankruptcy in 2009 and the subsequent recovery of $1.1 million in 2010.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">(1)&#160; Write-offs, net of recoveries</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">(2)&#160;&#160;In 2009, we provided an allowance of approximately $1M for a commercial customer that declared bankruptcy.&#160;&#160;We reversed the allowance in 2010 as a result of favorable bankruptcy proceedings and subsequent collection in 2011 of the pre-bankruptcy receivable.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Purchased Power </font>We record the cost of power obtained under long-term contracts as operating expenses.&#160;&#160;These contracts do not convey to us the right to use the related property, plant or equipment.&#160;&#160;We engage in short-term purchases with other third parties and record them as operating expenses in the month the power is delivered.&#160;&#160;We also engage in hourly purchases through ISO-NE&#8217;s normal settlement process.&#160;&#160;These are included in operating expenses.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Valuation of Long-Lived Assets </font>We periodically evaluate the carrying value of long-lived assets, including our investments in nuclear generating companies, our unregulated investments, and our interests in jointly owned generating facilities, when events and circumstances warrant such a review.&#160;&#160;The carrying value of such assets is considered impaired when the anticipated undiscounted cash flow from the asset is separately identifiable and is less than its carrying value.&#160;&#160;In that event, a loss is recognized based on the amount by which the carrying value exceeds the fair value of the long-lived asset.&#160;&#160;No impairments of long-lived assets were recorded in 2010, 2009 or 2008.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Utility Plant </font>Utility plant is recorded at original cost.&#160;&#160;Replacements of retirement units of property are charged to utility plant.&#160;&#160;Maintenance and repairs, including replacements not qualifying as retirement units of property, are charged to maintenance expense. The costs of renewals and improvements of property units are capitalized.&#160;&#160;The original cost of units retired, net of salvage value, are charged to accumulated provision for depreciation.&#160;&#160;The primary components of utility plant at December 31 follow (dollars in thousands):</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We have legal retirement obligations for decommissioning related to our joint-owned nuclear plant, Millstone Unit #3, and have an external trust fund dedicated to funding our share of future costs.&#160;&#160;The year-end aggregate fair value of the trust fund was $5.7 million in 2010 and $5.1 million in 2009, and is included in Investments and Other Assets on the Consolidated Balance Sheets.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Non-legal Removal Costs:</font>&#160;Our regulated operations collect removal costs in rates for certain utility plant assets that do not have associated legal asset retirement obligations.&#160;&#160;Non-legal removal costs of about $11.5 million in 2010 and $10.7 million in 2009 are included in Other Deferred Credits and Other Liabilities on the Consolidated Balance Sheets.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Environmental Liabilities </font>We are engaged in various operations and activities that subject us to inspection and supervision by both federal and state regulatory authorities including the United States Environmental Protection Agency.&#160;&#160;Our policy is to accrue a liability for those sites where costs for remediation, monitoring and other future activities are probable and can be reasonably estimated.&#160;&#160;See Note 19 - Commitments and Contingencies.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Derivative Financial Instruments</font>&#160;We account for certain power contracts as derivatives under the provisions of FASB&#8217;s guidance for derivatives and hedging. This guidance requires that derivatives be recorded on the balance sheet at fair value.&#160;&#160;Derivatives are recorded as current and long-term assets or liabilities depending on the duration of the contracts.&#160;&#160;Our derivative financial instruments are related to managing our power supply resources to serve our customers, and are not for trading purposes. Contracts that qualify for the normal purchase and sale exception to derivative accounting are not included in derivative assets and liabilities. Additionally, we have not elected hedge accounting for our power-related derivatives.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Based on a PSB-approved Accounting Order, we record the changes in fair value of all power-related derivative financial instruments as deferred charges or deferred credits on the balance sheet, depending on whether the change in fair value is an unrealized loss or gain.&#160;&#160;Realized gains and losses on sales are recorded as increases to or reductions of operating revenues, respectively. For purchase contracts, realized gains and losses are recorded as reductions of or additions to purchased power expense, respectively.&#160;&#160;For additional information about power-related derivatives, see Note 6 - Fair Value and Note 16 - Power-Related Derivatives.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Government Grants</font>&#160;We recognize government grants when there is reasonable assurance that we will comply with the conditions attached to the grant arrangement and the grant will be received.&#160;&#160;Government grants are recognized in the Consolidated Statements of Income over the periods in which we recognize the related costs for which the government grant is intended to compensate.&#160;&#160;When government grants are related to reimbursements of operating expenses, the grants are recognized as a reduction of the related expense in the Consolidated Statements of Income.&#160;&#160;For government grants related to reimbursements of capital expenditures, the grants are recognized as a reduction of the basis of the asset and recognized in the Consolidated Statements of Income over the estimated useful life of the depreciable asset as reduced depreciation expense.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We record government grants receivable in the Consolidated Balance Sheets in Accounts Receivable. For additional information see Note 9 &#8211; Retail Rates and Regulatory Accounting &#8211; CVPS SmartPower<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">TM</font>.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our current rates include the recovery of costs that are eligible for government grant reimbursement by the DOE under the ARRA; however, the grant reimbursement is not reflected in our current rates.&#160;&#160;Grant reimbursements are recorded to a regulatory liability until they are reflected in rates.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Fair Value</font>&#160;We use a fair value hierarchy to indicate the relative reliability of the fair value measure. The highest priority is given to quoted prices in active markets, and the lowest to unobservable data, such as our internal information.&#160;&#160;Fair value measurements are applicable to financial instruments that are subject to mark-to-market accounting such as our investments in available-for-sale securities, restricted cash, cash equivalents and derivative contracts.&#160;&#160;See Note 5 &#8211; Financial Instruments and Note 6 &#8211; Fair Value.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Share-Based Compensation&#160;</font>Share-based compensation costs are measured at the grant date based on the fair value of the award and recognized as expense on a straight-line basis over the requisite service period.&#160;&#160;See Note 10 - Share-Based Compensation.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Pension and Benefits</font>&#160;Our defined benefit pension plans and postretirement welfare benefit plans are accounted for in accordance with FASB&#8217;s guidance for employee retirement benefits.&#160;&#160;We use the fair value method to value all asset classes included in our pension and postretirement medical benefit trust funds.&#160;&#160;See Note 17 - Pension and Postretirement Medical Benefits for more information.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Construction and plant expenditures on the Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows reflect actual payments made during the periods.&#160;&#160;Construction and plant-related expenditures and CVPS SmartPower<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">TM</font> reimbursements are accrued at the end of each reporting period.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010, $1.5 million of construction and plant-related accruals was included in Accounts Payable, and $1.7 million was included in Other Current Liabilities.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2009, $0.5 million of construction and plant-related accruals was included in Accounts Payable, and $0.6 million was included in Other Current Liabilities.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010, Accounts Receivable included $0.3 million representing the capital component of CVPS SmartPower<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">TM</font> reimbursements not yet received from the DOE. We reduced Construction work-in-progress during 2010 for this pending reimbursement.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We maintain a cash concentration account for payments related to our routine business activities.&#160;&#160;The book overdraft amount resulting from outstanding checks is recorded as a current liability at the end of each reporting period.&#160;&#160;Changes in the book overdraft position are reflected in operating activities on the Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Other non-cash expense and (income), net includes provision for uncollectible accounts, provision for rate refunds, the change in cash surrender value of whole life and variable life insurance policies held in our Rabbi Trust, share-based compensation, non-utility property depreciation and allowance for funds used during construction.&#160;&#160;Other investing activities include return of capital from investments in affiliates, non-utility capital expenditures, premiums paid on Rabbi Trust life insurance policies and death benefits received from such policies.&#160;&#160;Other financing activities include reductions in capital lease obligations, shares repurchased for mandatory tax withholdings and excess tax benefits relating to share-based compensation.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Recently Adopted Accounting Policies&#160;&#160;</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Variable Interest Entities:&#160;&#160;</font>In June 2009, the FASB issued additional consolidation guidance related to variable interest entities and includes the addition of entities previously considered &#8220;qualifying special-purpose entities&#8221;.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We have an equity investment in and long-term power purchase agreement with VYNPC (&#8220;VY PPA&#8221;).&#160;&#160;VYNPC has a power purchase agreement with Entergy-Vermont Yankee, the owner of the Vermont Yankee nuclear plant, and VYNPC purchases 83 percent of the total output of the plant.&#160;&#160;Under the VY PPA, we purchase our entitlement share of the output of the plant, which is 29 percent of the total plant output.&#160;&#160;We have evaluated our equity investment and the power purchase agreement with VYNPC under the FASB variable interest accounting guidance and have determined that they both represent variable interests.&#160;&#160;We are not considered the primary beneficiary of VYNPC; therefore, are not required to consolidate VYNPC because we do not control the activities that are most relevant to the operating results of VYNPC.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We have an equity investment in and receive transmission services from Transco.&#160;&#160;The transmission services are billed under the 1991 Transmission Agreement (&#8220;VTA&#8221;).&#160;&#160;All of the Vermont utilities are parties to the VTA and the VTA requires the Vermont utilities to pay their pro-rata share of Transco&#8217;s costs, including interest and a fixed rate of return on equity, less the revenues collected under the ISO-NE Open Access Transmission Tariff.&#160;&#160;We have evaluated our equity investment and the VTA with Transco under the FASB variable interest accounting guidance and have determined that both represent variable interests.&#160;&#160;We are not considered the primary beneficiary of Transco; therefore, we are not required to consolidate Transco because we do not control the activities that are most relevant to the operating results of Transco.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our maximum exposure to loss is the amount of our equity investments in Transco and VYNPC.&#160;&#160;See Note 4 &#8211; Investments in Affiliates.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The amended guidance did not have an impact on our financial position, results of operations and cash flows. The guidance became effective for us on January 1, 2010.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">VELCO and Transco</font> VELCO, through its wholly owned subsidiary, Vermont Electric Transmission Company, Inc., and Transco own and operate an integrated transmission system in Vermont over which bulk power is delivered to all electric utilities in the state.&#160;&#160;Transco, a Vermont limited liability company, was formed by VELCO and its owners.&#160;&#160;In June 2006, VELCO transferred its assets to Transco in exchange for 2.4 million Class A Units, and Transco assumed all of VELCO&#8217;s debt.&#160;&#160;VELCO and its employees now manage the operations of Transco under a Management Services Agreement between VELCO and Transco.&#160;&#160;Transco operates under an Operating Agreement among us, VELCO, Transco, Green Mountain Power and most of the other Vermont electric utilities.&#160;&#160;Transco also operates under the Amended and Restated Three Party Agreements, assigned to Transco from VELCO, among us, Green Mountain Power, VELCO and Transco.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We invested $34.9 million in Transco in 2010 and $20.8 million in 2009. Our direct ownership interest was 36.68 percent at December 31, 2010 and 33.35 percent at December 31, 2009.&#160;&#160;Our ownership interest in Transco is represented by Class A Units that receive a return on equity investments of 11.5 percent under the 1991 Transmission Agreement (&#8220;VTA&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Our total direct and indirect interest in Transco was 41.02 percent at December 31, 2010 and 38.68 percent at December 31, 2009.&#160;&#160;Transco is a variable interest entity but we are not the primary beneficiary.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our December 2010 investment in Class A Units included 1,306,400 units related to a new specific facility in the Brattleboro, Vermont area.&#160;&#160;For 10 years, we are responsible for certain costs associated with the facility.&#160;&#160;At the end of 10 years, the specific facility will become a Transco common facility that is paid for by all the Vermont utilities receiving transmission service from Transco.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Cash dividends received from VELCO were $1.3 million in 2010, 2009 and 2008.&#160;&#160;Accounts payable to VELCO were $5.8 million at December 31, 2010 and $5.6 million at December 31, 2009.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Transmission services provided by Transco are billed to us under the VTA.&#160;&#160;All Vermont electric utilities are parties to the VTA.&#160;&#160;This agreement requires the Vermont utilities to pay their pro rata share of Transco&#8217;s total costs, including interest and a fixed rate of return on equity, less the revenue collected under the ISO-NE Open Access Transmission Tariff and other agreements.&#160;&#160;In June 2007, FERC issued an order combining three FERC filings related to the VTA, including a request by five municipal utilities for FERC approval to withdraw from the VTA and take transmission service under a different tariff, and requests by Transco for revisions to the VTA.&#160;&#160;The parties reached a preliminary settlement in January 2008 and filed a definitive settlement agreement with the FERC in March 2008.&#160;&#160;The settlement agreement is supported by all parties, including us, and resolves all issues that were raised in the FERC proceedings.&#160;&#160;The FERC approved the settlement agreement on August 22, 2008, and related amendments to the Transco operating agreement necessary to implement the settlement were approved by the PSB.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Transco&#8217;s billings to us primarily include the VTA and charges and reimbursements under the NEPOOL Open Access Transmission Tariff (&#8220;NOATT&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Transco&#8217;s billings to us were a net credit of $3.8 million from Transco in 2010 and charges of $8 million in 2009 and $7.3 million in 2008; these amounts are included in Transmission - affiliates on our Consolidated Statements of Income.&#160;&#160;There were no accounts payable to Transco at December 31, 2010 and $0.8 million at December 31, 2009. Cash dividends received were $12.7 million in 2010, $9 million in 2009 and $9.1 million in 2008. Accounts receivable from Transco was $0.2 million at December 31, 2010 and there were no accounts receivable from Transco at December 31, 2009.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">VYNPC</font> VYNPC sold its nuclear plant to Entergy Nuclear Vermont Yankee, LLC (&#8220;Entergy-Vermont Yankee&#8221;) in July 2002.&#160;&#160;The sale agreement included a purchased power contract between VYNPC and Entergy-Vermont Yankee (&#8220;VY PPA&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Under the VY PPA, VYNPC pays Entergy-Vermont Yankee for generation at fixed rates and, in turn, bills the VY PPA charges from Entergy-Vermont Yankee with certain residual costs of service through a FERC tariff to the VYNPC sponsors, including us.&#160;&#160;The residual costs of service include VYNPC&#8217;s other operating expenses, including any expenses incurred in administering the VY PPA and the power contracts, and an allowed return on equity.&#160;&#160;Our entitlement to energy produced by the Vermont Yankee plant is about 29 percent.&#160;&#160;See Note 19 &#8211; Commitments and Contingencies, Long-term Power Purchases.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Although we own a majority of the shares of VYNPC, the power contracts, sponsor agreement and composition of the board of directors, under which it operates, effectively restrict our ability to exercise control over VYNPC.&#160;&#160;VYNPC is a variable interest entity, but we are not the primary beneficiary.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Yankee Atomic:</font>&#160;&#160;Yankee Atomic&#8217;s wholesale rates are currently based on a 2010 FERC-approved filing.&#160;&#160;Based on the approved filing, Yankee Atomic agreed to no change in its revenue requirements from the 2006 FERC-approved settlement. The 2006 approved settlement also provides for reconciling and adjusting future charges based on actual decontamination and dismantling expenses and reporting decommissioning trust fund&#8217;s actual investment earnings.&#160;&#160;Our share of decommissioning and other costs amounted to $0.4 million in 2010, 2009 and 2008. <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Plant decommissioning activities were completed in 2007 and the NRC amended Yankee Atomic&#8217;s operating license in August 2007 for operation of the Independent Spent Fuel Storage Installation.&#160;&#160;This amendment reduced the size of the licensed property to include only the land immediately around the Independent Spent Fuel Storage Installation.&#160;&#160;Yankee Atomic remains responsible for safe storage of the plant&#8217;s spent nuclear fuel and waste at the site until the DOE meets its obligation to remove the material from the site.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">DOE Litigation:</font>&#160;&#160;All three companies have been seeking recovery of fuel storage-related costs stemming from the default of the DOE under the 1983 fuel disposal contracts that were mandated by the United States Congress under the Nuclear Waste Policy Act of 1982.&#160;&#160;Under the Act, the companies believe the DOE was required to begin removing spent nuclear fuel and greater than Class C (&#8220;GTCC&#8221;) waste from the nuclear plants no later than January 31, 1998 in return for payments by each company into the nuclear waste fund.&#160;&#160;No fuel or GTCC waste has been collected by the DOE, and each company&#8217;s spent fuel is stored at its own site.&#160;&#160;Maine Yankee, Connecticut Yankee and Yankee Atomic collected the funds from us and other wholesale utility customers, under FERC-approved wholesale rates, and our share of these payments was collected from our retail customers.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In 2006, the United States Court of Federal Claims issued judgment in the spent fuel litigation.&#160;&#160;Maine Yankee was awarded $75.8 million in damages through 2002, Connecticut Yankee was awarded $34.2 million through 2001 and Yankee Atomic was awarded $32.9 million through 2001.&#160;&#160;In December 2006, the DOE filed a notice of appeal of the court&#8217;s decision and all three companies filed notices of cross appeals.&#160;&#160;In August 2008, the United States Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit reversed the award of damages and remanded the cases back to the trial court.&#160;&#160;The remand directed the trial court to apply the acceptance rate in 1987 annual capacity reports when determining damages.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On March 6, 2009, the three companies submitted their revised statement of claimed damages for the case on remand.&#160;&#160;Maine Yankee claimed $81.7 million through 2002, Connecticut Yankee claimed $39.7 million and Yankee Atomic claimed $53.9 million in damages through 2001.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The trial phase of the remanded case occurred in August 2009.&#160;&#160;Post-trial briefing was completed in early November 2009, and final arguments were heard on December 10, 2009.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">A final ruling in favor of the three companies was issued on September 7, 2010.&#160;&#160;Maine Yankee was awarded $81.7 million, Connecticut Yankee was awarded $39.7 million and Yankee Atomic was awarded $21.2 million.&#160;&#160;The DOE filed an appeal on November 8, 2010 and the three Yankee companies filed cross-appeals on November 19, 2010.&#160;&#160;Interest on the judgments does not start to accrue until all appeals have been decided.&#160;&#160;Our share of the claimed damages of $3.2 million is based on our ownership percentages described above.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Court of Federal Claims&#8217; original decision established the DOE&#8217;s responsibility for reimbursing Maine Yankee for its actual costs through 2002 and Connecticut Yankee and Yankee Atomic for their actual costs through 2001 related to the incremental spent fuel storage, security, construction and other costs of the spent fuel storage installation.&#160;&#160;Although the decision did not resolve the question regarding damages in subsequent years, the decision did support future claims for the remaining spent fuel storage installation construction costs.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">At December 31, 2010, our power-related derivatives consisted of FTRs.&#160;&#160;In 2010, there were no related unrealized gains or losses.&#160;&#160;In 2009, related unrealized losses of $0.4 million were recorded as other deferred charges &#8211; regulatory on the Consolidated Balance Sheet and related unrealized gains of $0.6 million were recorded as other deferred credits - regulatory. For a discussion of the valuation techniques used for power contract derivatives see Note 6 - Fair Value - Power-related Derivatives below.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The fair values of our first mortgage bonds and fixed rate industrial/economic development bonds are estimated based on quoted market prices for the same or similar issues with similar remaining time to maturity or on current rates offered to us.&#160;&#160;Fair values are estimated to meet disclosure requirements and do not necessarily represent the amounts at which obligations would be settled.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The table above does not include cash, special deposits, receivables and payables as the carrying values of those instruments approximate fair value because of their short duration.&#160;The carrying values of our variable rate industrial/economic development bonds approximate fair value since the rates are adjusted at least monthly.&#160;&#160;The carrying value of our credit facility borrowings approximate fair value since the rates can change daily.&#160;&#160;The fair value of our cash equivalents and restricted cash are included in Note 6 - Fair Value.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Concentration Risk</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>Financial instruments that potentially expose us to concentrations of credit risk consist primarily of cash, cash equivalents, special deposits and accounts receivable.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Essentially all of our restricted cash is invested in one issuer.&#160;&#160;However, the issuer is highly rated and the investment matured on February 1, 2011.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our accounts receivable are not collateralized.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, approximately 8 percent of total accounts receivable are with wholesale entities engaged in the energy industry. This industry concentration could affect our overall exposure to credit risk, positively or negatively, since customers may be similarly affected by changes in economic, industry or other conditions.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our practice to mitigate credit risk arising from our energy industry concentration with wholesale entities is to contract with creditworthy power and transmission counterparties or obtain letters of credit or guarantees from their creditworthy affiliates.&#160;&#160;We may also enter into third-party power purchase and sales contracts that require collateral based on credit rating or contain master netting arrangements in the event of nonpayment.&#160;&#160;Currently, we hold parental guarantees and/or letters of credit from certain transmission customers and forward power sale counterparties.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our material power supply contracts and arrangements are principally with Hydro-Qu&#233;bec and VYNPC.&#160;&#160;These contracts comprise the majority of our total energy (MWh) purchases.&#160;&#160;These supplier concentrations could have a material impact on our power costs, if one or both of these sources were unavailable over an extended period of time.&#160;&#160;We do not have the ability to seek collateral under these two contracts, but the contracts provide the ability to seek damages for non-performance.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">NOTE 6 - FAIR VALUE</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Effective January 1, 2008, we adopted FASB&#8217;s guidance for fair value measurements, as required.&#160;&#160;The guidance establishes a single, authoritative definition of fair value, prescribes methods for measuring fair value, establishes a fair value hierarchy based on the inputs used to measure fair value and expands disclosures about the use of fair value measurements; however, the guidance does not expand the use of fair value accounting in any new circumstances.&#160;&#160;The guidance defines fair value as &#8220;the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date.&#8221;</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Valuation Techniques</font> Fair value is not an entity-specific measurement, but a market-based measurement utilizing assumptions market participants would use to price the asset or liability.&#160;&#160;The FASB requires three valuation techniques to be used at initial recognition and subsequent measurement of an asset or liability:</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Market Approach:</font>&#160;&#160;This approach uses prices and other relevant information generated by market transactions involving identical or comparable assets or liabilities.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Income Approach:</font>&#160;&#160;This approach uses valuation techniques to convert future amounts (cash flows, earnings) to a single present value amount.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Cost Approach:</font>&#160;&#160;This approach is based on the amount currently required to replace the service capacity of an asset (often referred to as the &#8220;current replacement cost&#8221;).</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The valuation technique (or a combination of valuation techniques) utilized to measure fair value is the one that is appropriate given the circumstances and for which sufficient data is available.&#160;&#160;Techniques must be consistently applied, but a change in the valuation technique is appropriate if new information is available.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Fair Value Hierarchy</font> FASB guidance establishes a fair value hierarchy (&#8220;hierarchy&#8221;) to prioritize the inputs used in valuation techniques. The hierarchy is designed to indicate the relative reliability of the fair value measure. The highest priority is given to quoted prices in active markets, and the lowest to unobservable data, such as an entity&#8217;s internal information. The lower the level of the input of a fair value measurement, the more extensive the disclosure requirements. There are three broad levels:</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Level 1:</font>&#160;&#160;Quoted prices (unadjusted) are available in active markets for identical assets or liabilities as of the reporting date.&#160;&#160;Level 1 includes cash equivalents that consist of money market funds and directly held securities in our non-qualified Millstone Decommissioning Trust Fund.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Level 2:</font>&#160;&#160;Pricing inputs are other than quoted prices in active markets included in Level 1, which are directly or indirectly observable as of the reporting date.&#160;&#160;This value is based on other observable inputs, including quoted prices for similar assets and liabilities in markets that are not active.&#160;&#160;Level 2 includes commercial paper held in restricted cash and securities not directly held in our Millstone Decommissioning Trust Funds such as fixed income securities (Treasury securities, other agency and corporate debt) and equity securities.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Level 3:</font>&#160;&#160;Pricing inputs include significant inputs that are generally less observable.&#160;&#160;Unobservable inputs may be used to measure the asset or liability where observable inputs are not available.&#160;&#160;We develop these inputs based on the best information available, including our own data.&#160;&#160;Level 3 instruments include derivatives related to our forward energy purchases and sales, financial transmission rights and a power-related option contract.&#160;&#160;There were no changes to our Level 3 fair value measurement methodologies during 2010 and 2009.</font></div>

<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Page 72 of 128</font></div>

<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
<hr style="COLOR: black" noshade size="2">
</div>
</div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160; </font></div>
</div>
</div>

<br>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Millstone Decommissioning Trust</font> Our primary valuation technique to measure the fair value of our nuclear decommissioning trust investments is the market approach.&#160;&#160;We own a share of the qualified decommissioning fund and cannot validate a publicly quoted price at the qualified fund level.&#160;&#160;However, actively traded quoted prices for the underlying securities comprising the funds have been obtained.&#160;&#160;Due to these observable inputs, fixed income, equity and cash equivalent securities in the qualified fund are classified as Level 2.&#160;&#160;Equity securities are held directly in our non-qualified trust and actively traded quoted prices for these securities have been obtained.&#160;&#160;Due to these observable inputs, these equity securities are classified as Level 1.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We recognize transfers in and out of the fair value hierarchy levels at the end of the reporting period. &#160;There were no transfers of equity and debt securities within the fair value hierarchy levels during the period ended December 31, 2010.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Cash Equivalents and Restricted Cash </font>The market approach is used to measure the fair values of money market funds and other short-term investments included in cash equivalents and restricted cash. &#160;We have the ability to transact our money market funds at the net asset value price per share and can withdraw those funds without a penalty.&#160; We are able to obtain actively traded quoted prices for these funds; therefore they are classified as Level 1.&#160; We are able to obtain a quoted price for our 60-day commercial paper held in restricted cash; however, the quote was from a less active market.&#160;&#160;We have concluded that this investment does not qualify for Level 1 and is reflected as Level 2.&#160;&#160;Cash equivalents are included in cash and cash equivalents on the Consolidated Balance Sheets.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Power-related Derivatives </font>We have historically had three types of derivative assets and liabilities: forward energy contracts, FTRs, and a power-related option contract.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010, our derivatives consisted of FTRs.&#160;&#160;Our primary valuation technique to measure the fair value of these derivative assets and liabilities is the income approach, which involves determining a present value amount based on estimated future cash flows.&#160;&#160;However, when circumstances warrant, we may also use alternative approaches as described below to calculate the fair value for each type of derivative.&#160;&#160;Since many of the valuation inputs are not observable in the market, we have classified our derivative assets and liabilities as Level 3.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">To calculate the fair value of forward energy contracts, we typically use a mark-to-market valuation model that includes the following inputs: contract energy prices, forward energy prices, contract volumes and delivery dates, risk-free and credit-adjusted interest rates, counterparty credit ratings and our credit rating.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">To calculate the fair value of our FTR contracts we use two different approaches.&#160;&#160;For FTR contracts entered into with an auction date close to the reporting date, we use the auction clearing prices obtained from ISO-NE, which represents a market approach to determining fair value.&#160;&#160;Auction clearing prices are used to value all FTRs at December 31 each year.&#160;&#160;For FTR contract valuations performed at interim reporting dates, we use an internally developed valuation model to estimate the fair values for the remaining portions of annual FTRs.&#160;&#160;This model includes the following inputs:&#160;&#160;historic congestion component prices for the applicable locations, historic energy prices, forward energy prices, contract volumes and durations, and the applicable risk-free rate.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">To calculate the fair value of our power-related option contract, which expired at December 31, 2010, we used a binomial tree model that included the following inputs: forward energy prices, expected volatility, contract volume, prices and duration, and LIBOR swap rates.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">At December 31, 2010, there were no realized gains or losses included in earnings attributable to the change in unrealized gains or losses related to derivatives still held at the reporting date.&#160;&#160;This is due to our regulatory accounting treatment for all power-related derivatives.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Based on a PSB-approved Accounting Order, we record the change in fair value of power contract derivatives as deferred charges or deferred credits on the Consolidated Balance Sheet, depending on whether the change in fair value is an unrealized loss or gain.&#160;&#160;The corresponding offsets are current and long-term assets or liabilities depending on the duration.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">NOTE 7 - INVESTMENT SECURITIES</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Millstone Decommissioning Trust Fund&#160;</font>We have decommissioning trust fund investments related to our joint-ownership interest in Millstone Unit #3.&#160;&#160;The decommissioning trust fund was established pursuant to various federal and state guidelines.&#160;&#160;Among other requirements, the fund must be managed by an independent and prudent fund manager.&#160;&#160;Any gains or losses, realized and unrealized, are expected to be refunded to or collected from ratepayers and are recorded as regulatory assets or liabilities in accordance with the FASB guidance for Regulated Operations.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">An investment is impaired if the fair value of the investment is less than its cost and if management considers the impairment to be other-than-temporary.&#160;&#160;Regulatory authorities limit our ability to oversee the day-to-day management of our nuclear decommissioning trust fund investments and therefore we lack investing ability and decision-making authority.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, we consider all equity securities held by our nuclear decommissioning trusts with fair values below their cost basis to be other-than-temporarily impaired.&#160;&#160;The FASB guidance for Investments - Debt and Equity Securities, requires impairment of debt securities if: 1) there is the intent to sell a debt security; 2) it is more likely than not that the security will be required to be sold prior to recovery; or 3) the entire unamortized cost of the security is not expected to be recovered.&#160;&#160;For the majority of the investments shown below, we own a share of the trust fund investments.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In July 2009, we changed one of the fund managers of our available-for-sale equity investments.&#160;&#160;This resulted in a higher level of investments in available-for-sale securities and proceeds from sale of available-for-sale securities as reported on the Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows.&#160;&#160;In 2010, we had $0.1 million of realized gains and our realized losses were $0.1 million.&#160;&#160;The realized losses include $0.1 million of impairments associated with our equity securities; however, there were no permanent impairments or &#8216;credit losses&#8217; associated with our debt securities.&#160;&#160;&#160;In addition, there were no non-credit loss impairments to our debt securities in 2010.&#160;&#160;In 2009, we had $0.7 million of realized gains and our realized losses were $0.4 million.&#160;&#160;The realized losses include $0.2 million of impairments associated with our equity securities; however, there were no permanent impairments or &#8216;credit losses&#8217; associated with our debt securities.&#160;&#160;Additionally, in 2009, we recorded a non-credit loss impairment to our debt securities that is included in unrealized losses.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The fair value of these investments at December 31 is summarized below (dollars in thousands):</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">NOTE 8 &#8211; RESTRICTED CASH</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">At December 31, 2010, we had $23.5 million invested in a restricted cash fund comprised of unreimbursed VEDA bond financing proceeds.&#160;&#160;The investments in this fund consist primarily of commercial paper.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The bond proceeds are held in trust and we access these bond proceeds as reimbursement for capital expenditures made under certain production, transmission, distribution and general facility projects financed by the bond issue.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We recorded $5.9 million of the restricted cash as a current asset on the Consolidated Balance Sheet, which represents expenses paid that are expected to be reimbursed at the next requisition date.&#160;&#160;We expect to receive reimbursements of the remaining proceeds held in trust by early 2012.&#160;&#160;See Note 15 &#8211; Long-term Debt and Notes Payable, <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Industrial/economic development bonds.</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">NOTE 9 - RETAIL RATES AND REGULATORY ACCOUNTING</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Retail Rates </font>Our retail rates are approved by the PSB after considering the recommendations of Vermont&#8217;s consumer advocate, the DPS.&#160;&#160;Fair regulatory treatment is fundamental to maintaining our financial stability.&#160;&#160;Rates must be set at levels to recover costs, including a market rate of return to equity and debt holders, in order to attract capital.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Alternative Regulation Plan I:</font>&#160;&#160;On September 30, 2008, the PSB issued an order approving our alternative regulation plan.&#160;&#160;The plan became effective on November 1, 2008.&#160;&#160;It expires on December 31, 2011, but we have petitioned for an extension through December, 2013.&#160;&#160;The plan allows for quarterly PCAM adjustment to reflect changes in power supply and transmission-by-others costs); annual base rate adjustments to reflect changing costs; and an annual ESAM adjustment to reflect changes, within predetermined limits, from the allowed earnings level.&#160;&#160;Under the plan, the allowed return on equity is adjusted annually to reflect one-half of the change in the average yield on the 10-year Treasury note as measured over the last 20 trading days prior to October 15 of each year.&#160;&#160;The ESAM provides for the return on equity of the regulated portion of our business to fall between 75 basis points above or below the allowed return on equity before any adjustment is made.&#160;&#160;If the actual return on equity of the regulated portion of our business exceeds 75 basis points above the allowed return, the excess amount is returned to customers in a future period.&#160;&#160;If the actual return on equity of our regulated business falls between 75 and 125 basis points below the allowed return on equity, the shortfall is shared equally between shareholders and customers.&#160;&#160;Any earnings shortfall in excess of 125 basis points below the allowed return on equity is fully recovered from customers.&#160;&#160;As such, the minimum return for our regulated business is 100 basis points below the allowed return.&#160;&#160;These adjustments are made at the end of each fiscal year.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The ESAM also provides for an exogenous effects provision.&#160;&#160;Under this provision,<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font>we are allowed to defer the unexpected impacts, to the extent these costs exceed $0.6 million, of changes in GAAP, tax laws, FERC or ISO-NE rules and major unplanned operation, maintenance costs, such as those due to major storms and other factors including loss of load not due to variations in heating and cooling temperatures.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On December 31, 2009, the PSB issued its order approving our 2010 base rate filing, which increased rates 5.58 percent, effective for bills rendered beginning January 1, 2010. The allowed rate of return for 2010, calculated in accordance with the plan, was 9.59 percent.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On February 2, 2010, the PSB held a prehearing conference, followed by a workshop, to consider the proposal to amend the non-power cost cap formula of our alternative regulation plan to allow for full cost recovery for new initiatives arising after the effective date of the plan. The DPS supported the proposal, and the 2010 base rate filing increase approved by the PSB included recovery of costs for two new initiatives.&#160; On September 3, 2010, the PSB approved the implementation of a new initiatives adder under our alternative regulation plan.&#160;&#160;In order to qualify for treatment as a new initiative the following criteria must be met: 1) the risk associated with implementing the new initiative is of a nature that is distinct from the ordinary business risk that we assume in discharging our public service obligation, and 2) the costs associated with implementing the new initiative are material.&#160;&#160;In our 2010 base rate filing we were allowed recovery of $0.2 million for a new initiative that does not meet the PSB criteria.&#160;&#160;This amount will be returned to customers in 2011.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Using the methodology specified in our alternative regulation plan, we estimated the 2010 return on equity from the regulated portion of our business to be approximately 9 percent. We are required to file this calculation with the PSB by May 1, 2011. No ESAM adjustment was required since this return was within 75 basis points of our 2010 allowed return on equity of 9.59 percent.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In 2010, under the exogenous effects provision of the ESAM, we deferred $4.2 million of costs related to three major storms and tax law changes.&#160;&#160;On January 31, 2011 we filed with the PSB for recovery of these costs through the ESAM over a 12-month period commencing on July 1, 2011.&#160;&#160;The PSB has not yet acted on this filing.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The PCAM adjustments for 2010 were calculated to be an over-collection of $0.5 million in the first quarter, an under-collection of $1 million in the second quarter and an over-collection of less than $0.1 million in the third quarter.&#160;&#160;The over-collection in the first quarter was recorded as current liability and returned to customers over the three months ended September 30, 2010.&#160;&#160;The under-collection in the second quarter was recorded as a current asset and recovered from customers over the three months ended December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;The over-collection in the third quarter was recorded as current liability and will be returned to customers over the three months ended March 31, 2011.&#160;&#160;We filed PCAM reports, including supporting documentation, each quarter with the PSB identifying the over- and under-collections.&#160;&#160;In each case, the DPS recommended the PCAM report be approved as filed and the PSB accepted the DPS recommendation and approved the filing.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The PCAM adjustment for the fourth quarter of 2010 was an over-collection of $5.2 million and was recorded as a current liability.&#160;&#160;This over-collection will be returned to customers over the three months ending June 30, 2011. We filed a PCAM report, including supporting documentation, with the PSB identifying this over-collection.&#160;&#160;The PSB has not yet acted on this filing.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On February 24, 2011, we filed a request with the PSB to offset the $4.2 million 2010 ESAM deferral against the $5.2 million fourth quarter 2010 PCAM over-collection and return the net refund of $1 million to customers over the three months ending June 30, 2011. The DPS supports our request.&#160;&#160;The PSB has not yet acted on the request.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On May 1, 2010, we filed our 2009 ESAM calculation using the methodology specified in our alternative regulation plan.&#160;&#160;The 2009 return on equity from the regulated portion of our business was 9.87 percent.&#160;&#160;No ESAM adjustment was required in 2009 since this return was within 75 basis points of our 2009 allowed return on equity of 9.77 percent.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The PCAM adjustments for 2009 were calculated to be over-collections of $0.6 million in the first quarter, $0.5 million in the second quarter, $0.6 million in the third quarter and $1 million in the fourth quarter.&#160;&#160;These over-collections were recorded as current liabilities.&#160;&#160;We filed PCAM reports, including supporting documentation, each quarter with the PSB identifying the over-collections.&#160;&#160;In each case, the DPS recommended the PCAM report be approved as filed and the PSB accepted the DPS recommendation and approved the filing.&#160;&#160;The 2009 over-collections were returned to customers over the three months ended September 30, 2009, December 31, 2009, March 31, 2010 and June 30, 2010, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
