<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The second version was for a $24.4 million or an 8.34 percent increase in retail rates, reflecting an allowed ROE of 10.22 percent. This increase was premised upon the PSB approving certain modifications to our existing alternative regulation plan as discussed below in the section titled Alternative Regulation Plan II.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Under our existing alternative regulation plan, the annual change in the non-power costs, as reflected in our base rate filing, is limited to any increase in the U.S. Consumer Price Index for the northeast, less a 1 percent productivity adjustment. The non-power costs associated with the implementation of our Asset Management Plan and our CVPS SmartPower<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">TM</font> project are excluded from the non-power cost cap.&#160;&#160;&#160;Our 2011 non-power costs did not exceed the non-power cost cap.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On December 3, 2010, the DPS recommended that the PSB approve our requested 7.46 percent base rate adjustment under the existing alternative regulation plan with certain conditions.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On December 21, 2010, we filed the ARP MOU between us and the DPS with the PSB regarding certain amendments to the alternative regulation plan including the ROE provisions.&#160;&#160;As part of the settlement, an agreement was also reached with respect to our 2011 base rate filing.&#160;&#160;Under the ARP MOU we would be permitted to set our ROE for 2011 at 9.59 percent and implement a 7.67 percent retail rate increase effective with bills rendered January 1, 2011.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On December 29, 2010, the PSB issued an order allowing us to implement a 7.46 percent increase in retail rates, reflecting an allowed ROE of 9.18 percent, effective with bills rendered January 1, 2011.&#160;&#160;The PSB concluded that there was not sufficient time to conduct a meaningful assessment of the issues raised by the ARP MOU, particularly given the absence of pre-filed supporting testimony.&#160;&#160;The PSB has opened an investigation into our existing rates in order to assess whether further adjustment is necessary pending its review of the ARP MOU.&#160;&#160;As discussed below in Alternative Regulation II, the PSB has issued an order concerning our request to modify and extend our existing alternative regulation plan.&#160;&#160;This order will require consideration in the PSB&#8217;s investigation into our current rates. At this time we do not expect that this will result in any change to the 7.46 percent rate increase implemented on January 1, 2011.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Alternative Regulation Plan II:</font>&#160;&#160;On June 30, 2010, we filed a required Alternative Regulation Plan Analysis of Plan Performance with the PSB.&#160; This analysis evaluated the effectiveness of the Plan&#8217;s performance in achieving the goals of Vermont alternative regulation.&#160; As described in the evaluation, the implementation of the current plan has helped to advance these goals; however, we also identified concerns and impediments that limit its overall effectiveness in satisfying all of the objectives of Vermont alternative regulation.&#160;</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">To address these concerns, on July 6, 2010 we petitioned the PSB to approve changes to the current plan to: a) extend its duration; b) alter the methodology for implementing the non-power cost cap; and c) reset the allowed ROE as noted above to 10.22 percent.&#160;&#160;If these changes are approved as initially proposed, the revised plan will expire on December 31, 2013 and the allowed ROE will be reset as of January 1, 2011.&#160;&#160;Thereafter, the existing annual ROE adjustment methodology would apply for the duration of the plan.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The ARP MOU filed on December 21, 2010 would provide final resolution to all issues regarding our petition to modify and extend our existing alternative regulation plan. Under the ARP MOU, the term of the alternative regulation plan would be extended through 2013 and the allowed ROE would be set at 9.59 percent for 2011.&#160;&#160;In addition, the ARP MOU provides for a modification to the alternative regulation plan to include a benchmarking mechanism that affects the non-power cost cap for rate years 2012 and 2013.&#160;&#160;There is also a provision to adjust the non-power cost cap for any cost of service change resulting from an ROE change.</font></div>

<br>

<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160; </font></div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160; </font></div>
</div>
</div>

<br>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">As discussed above, the PSB felt a meaningful assessment of the ARP MOU could not occur before January 1, 2011 and opened an investigation.&#160;&#160;Technical hearings on the ARP MOU were held on January 5 and 6, 2011.&#160;&#160;We expect to receive a PSB order in the first quarter of 2011.&#160;&#160;The PSB may approve, reject or modify the ARP MOU.&#160;&#160;Based on its ruling on the ARP MOU, the retail rate increase ultimately approved for 2011 may be modified in the investigation.&#160;&#160;By order dated March 3, 2011, the PSB approved further amendments to the alternative regulation plan that: 1) extend its duration until December 31, 2013; 2) alter the methodology for implementing the non-power-cost cap contained in the plan; 3) reset our allowed ROE; and 4) remove provisions no longer applicable to the provision of our services. These amendments are consistent with the terms of an ARP MOU that was filed with the PSB on December 21, 2010, except that the PSB approved an ROE for us for 2011 of 9.45 percent, rather than the 9.59 percent contained in the ARP MOU.&#160;&#160;At this time we do not expect there will be any change to the 7.46 percent rate increase implemented on January 1, 2011.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Staffing Level Investigation</font> On February 13, 2009, the PSB opened an investigation into the staffing levels of the company as requested by us and the DPS.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On November 30, 2009, we filed the Staffing MOU with the PSB setting forth agreements that we reached with the DPS regarding the PSB&#8217;s investigation into our staffing levels. Under the Staffing MOU, in lieu of retaining a management consultant to perform a comprehensive review of our organizational structure and staffing, we and the DPS have agreed that we will reduce our staffing levels over a five-year period by a total of 17 positions as compared to the 549 positions we had on January 1, 2009. This reduction shall be in addition to the staffing reductions contemplated by the implementation of CVPS SmartPower<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">TM</font>. We retain discretion in how to achieve the staffing reductions, and the DPS has agreed that it shall not oppose the recovery in rates of all reasonable costs associated with staffing and related compensation during the term of the Staffing MOU, provided that recovery of such costs is otherwise consistent with normal ratemaking standards. By December 31, 2010 we had reduced staffing levels to 517 employees.&#160;&#160;&#160;Nothing in the Staffing MOU precludes us from seeking to add staff as reasonably necessary in response to new requirements imposed by the state or federal government.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On March 31, 2010, the PSB approved the Staffing MOU.&#160;&#160;The Staffing MOU allows CVPS to recover all reasonable costs associated with the staff reductions in accordance with our new initiatives amendment to the non-power cost cap formula of our alternative regulation plan. As discussed above, for these costs to qualify as a new initiative under the plan they would need to meet the criteria established by the PSB.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">CVPS SmartPower</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">TM</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>On October 27, 2009, the DOE announced that Vermont&#8217;s electric utilities will receive $69 million in federal stimulus funds to deploy advanced metering, new customer service enhancements and grid automation.&#160;&#160;As a participant on Vermont&#8217;s smart grid stimulus application, we expect to receive a grant of over $31 million.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On April 15, 2010, we signed an agreement with the DOE for our portion of the Smart Grid stimulus grant and project and the agreement became effective April 19, 2010.&#160;&#160;The agreement includes provisions for funding and other requirements.&#160;&#160;&#160;We are eligible to receive reimbursement of 50 percent of our total project costs incurred since August 6, 2009, up to $31 million.&#160;&#160;Through December 31, 2010, we incurred $4.7 million of costs, of which $2.4 million were operating expenses and $2.3 million were capital expenditures.&#160;&#160;We have submitted requests for reimbursement of $2.3 million and have received $1.7 million to date.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On April 7, 2010, we filed the CVPS SmartPower<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">TM</font> MOU with the PSB that included, among other things, the agreement we reached with the DPS on the recovery of costs we will incur due to CVPS SmartPower<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">TM</font> implementation.&#160;&#160;We received the PSB&#8217;s order approving the cost recovery principles contained in the CVPS SmartPower<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">TM</font> MOU on August 6, 2010.&#160;&#160;On September 3, 2010, the PSB recognized the CVPS SmartPower<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">TM</font> plan as an authorized initiative under the new initiative adder discussed above.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The CVPS SmartPower<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">TM</font> MOU allows us to defer the difference between the actual costs included in the approved CVPS SmartPower<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">TM</font> plan and amounts collected through rates.&#160;&#160;Actual 2010 costs exceeded the amounts collected through rates by less than $0.1 million and were recorded as a regulatory asset.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our current rates include the recovery of costs that are eligible for government grant reimbursement by the DOE under the ARRA; however, the grant reimbursement was not reflected in our 2010 rates.&#160;&#160;Grant reimbursements of $1.2 million for 2010 operating costs were recorded as a regulatory liability.&#160;&#160;Expected grant reimbursements are reflected in 2011 rates.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Regulatory Accounting </font>Under FASB&#8217;s guidance for regulated operations, we account for certain transactions in accordance with permitted regulatory treatment whereby regulators may permit incurred costs, typically treated as expenses by unregulated entities, to be deferred and expensed in future periods when recovered through future revenues.&#160;&#160;In the event that we no longer meet the criteria under accounting for regulated operations and there is not a rate mechanism to recover these costs, we would be required to write off $12.5 million of regulatory assets (total regulatory assets of $40.5 million less pension and postretirement medical costs of $28 million), $4.3 million of other deferred charges - regulatory and $5 million of other deferred credits - regulatory.&#160;&#160;This would result in a total charge to operations of $11.8 million on a pre-tax basis as of December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;We would be required to record pre-tax pension and postretirement costs of $27.5 million to Accumulated Other Comprehensive Loss and $0.5 million to Retained Earnings as reductions to stockholders&#8217; equity.&#160;&#160;We would also be required to determine any potential impairment to the carrying costs of deregulated plant.&#160;&#160;Regulatory assets, certain other deferred charges and other deferred credits are shown in the table below (dollars in thousands).</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The regulatory assets included in the table above are being recovered in retail rates and are supported by written rate orders. The recovery period for regulatory assets varies based on the nature of the costs.&#160;&#160;All regulatory assets are earning a return, except for income taxes, nuclear plant dismantling costs, and pension and postretirement medical costs.&#160;&#160;Other deferred charges &#8211; regulatory are supported by PSB-approved accounting orders or approved cost recovery methodologies, allowing cost deferral until recovery in a future rate proceeding.&#160;&#160;Most items listed in other deferred credits - regulatory are being amortized for periods ranging from two to three years.&#160;&#160;Pursuant to PSB-approved rate orders, when a regulatory asset or liability is fully amortized, the corresponding rate revenue shall be booked as a reverse amortization in an opposing regulatory liability or asset account.</font></div>

<td align="right" style="WIDTH: 45pt">
<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">(a)&#160;&#160;</font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The 2002 Long-Term Incentive Plan was amended in 2008.&#160;&#160;The amendments renamed the plan as the Omnibus Stock Plan, added 100,000 additional shares of our common stock to be issued under the plan and revised the plan to conform to certain other regulatory changes.&#160;&#160;The adoption of the amendments to the plan was authorized by the PSB on April 23, 2008 and by our shareholders on May 6, 2008.</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Omnibus Stock Plan authorizes the granting of stock options, stock appreciation rights, common shares and performance shares.&#160;&#160;The plan is intended to encourage stock ownership by recipients.&#160;&#160;Stock options have not been granted as a form of compensation since 2005 and stock appreciation rights have not been granted.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Total share-based compensation expense recognized in the income statement was $0.9 million in both 2010 and 2009 and $0.8 million in 2008.&#160;&#160;The total income tax benefit recognized in the income statement for share-based compensation was $0.3 million in 2010, $0.4 million in 2009 and $0.3 million in 2008.&#160;&#160;No compensation costs were capitalized.&#160;&#160;Cash received from exercise of stock options was $0.6 million in 2010, $0.4 million in 2009 and $1 million in 2008. The tax benefit realized for the tax deductions from option exercises and performance shares issued was $0.2 million in 2010, $0.3 million in 2009 and $0.4 million in 2008. These amounts are included in other paid in capital on the balance sheet.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Currently, any outstanding stock options that are exercised and other stock awards are settled from original issue common shares.&#160;&#160;Under the existing plans, they may also be settled by the issuance of treasury shares or through open market purchases of common shares.&#160;&#160;Awards other than stock options can also be settled in cash at the discretion of the Compensation Committee of our Board of Directors.&#160;&#160;Historically, these awards have not been settled in cash.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Common stock is granted as part of the Board of Directors&#8217; annual retainer. These shares vest immediately, however, individual directors can elect to defer receipt of their retainer under the terms of the Deferred Compensation Plan for Directors and Officers.&#160;&#160;Compensation expense was $0.2 million in 2010, 2009 and 2008.&#160;&#160;Unearned compensation expense at December 31, 2010 was of a nominal amount.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The weighted-average grant-date fair value of shares granted was $21.17 in 2010, $18.04 in 2009 and $21.18 per share in 2008.&#160;&#160;The fair value of shares vested totaled approximately $0.1 million in 2010, 2009 and 2008.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Performance Shares</font> Awards under the executive officer long-term incentive program are delivered in the form of contingently granted performance shares of common stock.&#160;&#160;At the start of each year a fixed number of performance shares are contingently granted for three-year service periods (referred to as performance cycles).&#160;&#160;The number of shares awarded at the end of each performance cycle is dependent on our performance compared to pre-established performance targets for relative TSR compared to all publicly traded electric and combined utilities, and on operational measures.&#160;&#160;The number of shares awarded at the end of the performance cycles ranges from zero to 1.5 times the number of shares targeted, based on actual performance versus targets.&#160;&#160;Dividends payable on performance shares during the performance cycle are reinvested into additional performance shares.&#160;&#160;Once the award is earned, shares become fully vested.&#160;&#160;If the participant&#8217;s employment is terminated mid-cycle due to retirement, death, disability or a change-in-control, that employee or their estate is entitled to receive a pro rata portion of shares at target performance.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The fair value of performance shares for operational measures was estimated based on the market value of the shares on the grant date and the expected outcome of each measure.&#160;&#160;The grant-date fair value of performance shares with operational measures granted in 2010 was $20.62 per share.&#160;&#160;Compensation cost is recognized over the three-year performance cycle and is adjusted for the actual percentage of target achieved.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The fair value of performance shares for TSR measures was estimated on the grant date using a Monte Carlo simulation model.&#160;&#160;The grant-date fair value of performance shares with TSR measures granted in 2010 was $20.51 per share.&#160;&#160;Compensation cost is recognized on a straight-line basis over the three-year performance cycle and is not adjusted for the actual percentage of target achieved.&#160;&#160;The weighted-average assumptions used in the Monte Carlo valuation for TSR performance shares granted during the past three years are shown in the table below.</font></div>

</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">First Mortgage Bonds:</font>&#160;Substantially all of our utility property and plant is subject to liens under our First Mortgage Bond indenture. There are no interim sinking fund payments due prior to maturity on any series of first mortgage bonds and all interest rates are fixed.&#160;&#160;The First Mortgage Bonds are callable at our option at any time upon payment of a make-whole premium, calculated as the excess of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments to bondholders, discounted at a rate that is 0.5 percent higher than the comparable U.S. Treasury Bond yield, over the early redemption amount.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Industrial/economic development bonds:</font>&#160;&#160;The CDA and VIDA bonds are tax-exempt, floating rate, monthly demand revenue bonds.&#160;&#160;There are no interim sinking fund payments due prior to their maturity.&#160;&#160;The interest rates reset monthly.&#160;&#160;Both series are callable at par as follows: 1) at our option or the bondholders&#8217; option on each monthly interest payment date; or 2) at the option of the bondholders on any business day.&#160;&#160;There is a remarketing feature if the bonds are put for redemption.&#160;&#160;Historically, these bonds have been remarketed in the secondary bond market.&#160;&#160;These two series of bonds are both supported by letters of credit, discussed below.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On December 2, 2010, VEDA issued $30 million of tax-exempt Recovery Zone Facility Bonds, Central Vermont Public Service Corporation Issue, Series 2010 and loaned the proceeds to us under a Loan and Trust Agreement dated December 1, 2010.&#160;&#160;The bonds carry a fixed interest rate of 5 percent and will mature on December 15, 2020.&#160;&#160;The proceeds will be used to fund certain capital improvements to our production, transmission, distribution and general facilities.&#160;&#160;The VEDA bonds are secured by a $30 million issue of first mortgage bonds, Series VV, issued under our Indenture of Mortgage dated as of October 1, 1929, as amended and supplemented.&#160;&#160;As security, the terms of the Series VV first mortgage bonds mirror those of the VEDA bonds.&#160;&#160;VEDA has no obligation to pay interest and principal on the VEDA bonds except from proceeds provided by us.&#160;&#160;There are no interim sinking fund payments due prior to the maturity of the VEDA bonds, and they are not callable prior to maturity at our option.&#160;&#160;The bond proceeds are held in trust and we access these bond proceeds as reimbursement for capital expenditures made under certain production, transmission, distribution and general facility projects.&#160;&#160;The trust funds holding the bond proceeds are recorded as restricted cash on the Consolidated Balance Sheets.</font></div>

Realty, Inc.&#160;&#160;These cross-default provisions generally relate to an inability to pay debt or debt acceleration, inappropriate affiliate transactions, a breach of warranty or performance of an obligation, or the levy of significant judgments, attachments against our property or insolvency.&#160;&#160;Currently, we are not in default under any of our debt financing documents.&#160;&#160;Scheduled sinking fund payments and maturities for the next five years are, $20 million in 2011, $0 in 2012, $5.8 million in 2013, $0 in 2014 and $5 million in 2015.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Letters of credit: </font>We have two outstanding unsecured letters of credit, issued by one bank, that support the CDA and VIDA revenue bonds.&#160;&#160;These letters of credit total $11.1 million in support of the two revenue bond issues totaling $10.8 million, discussed above. We pay an annual fee of 2.4 percent on the letters of credit.&#160;These letters of credit expire on November 30, 2012. The letters of credit contain cross-default provisions to our wholly owned subsidiaries. These cross-default provisions generally relate to an inability to pay debt or debt acceleration, the levy of significant judgments or insolvency.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010, there were no amounts drawn under these letters of credit.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Credit Facility:</font> We have a three-year, $40 million unsecured revolving credit facility with a lending institution pursuant to a Credit Agreement dated November 3, 2008 that will expire in November 2011.&#160;&#160;The borrowings under this agreement have been reclassified as Notes Payable on the Consolidated Balance Sheet at December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;The Credit Agreement contains financial and non-financial covenants.&#160;&#160;Our obligation under the Credit Agreement is guaranteed by our wholly owned, unregulated subsidiaries, C.V. Realty and CRC.&#160;&#160;The purpose of the facility is to provide liquidity for general corporate purposes, including working capital and power contract performance assurance requirements, in the form of funds borrowed and letters of credit.&#160;&#160;Financing terms and costs include an annual commitment fee of 0.15 percent on the unused balance, plus interest on the outstanding balance of amounts borrowed at various interest options and a commission of 0.7 percent on the average daily amount of letters of credit outstanding.&#160;&#160;Terms also include the requirement to collateralize any outstanding letters of credit in the event of a default under the credit facility.&#160;&#160;The facility contains a Material Adverse Effect clause (a standard that requires greater adversity than a Material Adverse Change clause).&#160;&#160;The clause could allow the lending institution to deny a transaction under the credit facility at the point of request.&#160;&#160;The credit facility also contains cross-default provisions to any of our subsidiaries.&#160;&#160;These cross-default provisions generally relate to an inability to pay debt or debt acceleration, the levy of significant judgments or voluntary or involuntary liquidation, reorganization or bankruptcy.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010, there were $13.7 million in loans and $5.5 million in letters of credit outstanding under this credit facility.&#160;&#160;We had periodic borrowings under this facility during 2010.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We also have a three-year, $15 million unsecured revolving credit facility with a different lending institution pursuant to a Credit Agreement dated December 22, 2010 that expires in December 2013.&#160;&#160;This facility replaced a 364-day $15 million unsecured revolving credit facility that matured on December 29, 2010.&#160;&#160;The purpose of and our obligation under this credit agreement is the same as described above.&#160;&#160;Financing terms and costs include an annual commitment fee of 0.5 percent on the unused balance and a fee of 2.0 percent on the average daily amount of letters of credit outstanding.&#160;&#160;Various interest rate options exist for amounts borrowed under this facility.&#160;&#160;This facility does not contain a Material Adverse Effect clause.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010, there were no borrowings or letters of credit outstanding under this credit facility.&#160;&#160;Through December 31, 2010, we have not used this facility for borrowings or letters of credit.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Long-term Debt Issues:</font>&#160;&#160;On July 15, 2010, we entered into a commitment to issue $40 million of first mortgage bonds at 5.89 percent on June 15, 2011 in a private placement transaction, pending regulatory approvals.&#160;&#160;The proceeds will be used to help finance our capital expenditures, debt retirements, investments in Transco and other corporate purposes.&#160;&#160;These bonds will be issued to one purchaser under a shelf facility that was put in place on February 4, 2011 after receiving regulatory approval on November 30, 2010.&#160;&#160;The shelf facility allows us to issue up to an additional $60 million of first mortgage bonds directly to the purchaser through December 31, 2012.&#160;&#160;Neither party has any obligation to issue or purchase the additional $60 million first mortgage bonds available under the shelf facility.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Covenants:&#160;&#160;</font>Our long-term debt indentures, letters of credit, credit facilities, articles of association and material agreements contain financial covenants.&#160;&#160;The most restrictive financial covenants include maximum debt to total capitalization of 65 percent, and minimum interest coverage of two times.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010 we were in compliance with all financial covenants related to our various debt agreements, articles of association, letters of credit, credit facilities and material agreements.&#160;&#160;A significant reduction in future earnings or a significant reduction to common equity could restrict the payment of common and preferred dividends or could cause us to violate our maintenance covenants.&#160;&#160;If we were to default on a covenant, the lenders could take such actions as terminate their obligations, declare all amounts outstanding or due immediately payable, or take possession of or foreclose on mortgaged property.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Dividend and Optional Stock Redemption Restrictions:&#160;&#160;</font>Our revolving credit facilities described above restricts optional redemptions of capital stock and other restricted payments as defined.&#160;&#160;The First Mortgage Bond indenture and our Articles of Association also contain certain restrictions on the payment of cash dividends on and optional redemptions of all capital stock.&#160;&#160;Under the most restrictive of these provisions, $85.8 million of retained earnings was not subject to such restriction at December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;The Articles also restrict the payment of common dividends or purchase of any common shares if the common equity level falls below 25 percent of total capital, applicable only as long as Preferred Stock is outstanding.&#160;&#160;Our Articles of Association also contain a covenant that requires us to maintain a minimum common equity level of about $3.3 million as long as any Preferred Stock is outstanding.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">NOTE 16 - POWER-RELATED DERIVATIVES</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We are exposed to certain risks in managing our power supply resources to serve our customers, and we use derivative financial instruments to manage those risks.&#160;&#160;The primary risk managed by using derivative financial instruments is commodity price risk.&#160;&#160;Currently, our power supply forecast shows energy purchase and production amounts in excess of our load requirements through 2011.&#160;&#160;Because of this projected power surplus, we entered into one forward power sale contract for 2011.&#160;&#160;This forward sale was initially structured as a physical sale of excess power.&#160;&#160;In January 2011 the sale contract was renegotiated as a rate swap that settles financially.&#160;&#160;We have concluded that neither the original physical sale nor the subsequent rate swap contract are derivatives, since a notional amount does not exist under the terms of either contract.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On occasion, we will forecast a temporary power supply shortage such as when Vermont Yankee becomes unavailable.&#160;&#160;We typically enter into short-term forward power purchase contracts to cover a portion of these expected power supply shortages, which helps to reduce price volatility in our net power costs.&#160;&#160;We have not yet entered into a forward purchase contract for the 2011 Vermont Yankee refueling outage.&#160;&#160;Our power supply forecast shows that in 2012, our load requirements will exceed our energy purchase and production amounts, as certain committed long-term power purchase contracts begin to expire.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On August 12, 2010, we executed a significant long-term power purchase contract with HQUS and we have concluded that this contract meets the &#8220;normal purchase, normal sale&#8221; exception to derivatives accounting; therefore, we are not required to calculate the fair value of this contract.&#160;&#160;For additional information on this contract, see Note 19 - Commitments and Contingencies - New Hydro-Qu&#233;bec Agreement.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Several years ago, we entered into the Hydro-Qu&#233;bec Sellback #3 contract, a long-term purchased power contract that allows the seller to repurchase specified amounts of power with advance notice. The option under this contract expired December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;In addition, we are able to economically hedge our exposure to congestion charges that result from constraints on the transmission system with FTRs.&#160;&#160;FTRs are awarded to the successful bidders in periodic auctions administered by ISO-NE.&#160;&#160;We do not use derivative financial instruments for trading or other purposes.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Accounting for power-related derivatives is discussed in Note 2- Summary of Significant Accounting Policies - Derivative Financial Instruments.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Outstanding power-related derivative contracts at December 31 are as follows:</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font><br>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Realized gains and losses on derivative instruments are conveyed to or recovered from customers through the PCAM and have no net impact on results of operations.&#160;&#160;Derivative transactions and related collateral requirements are included in net cash flows from operating activities in the Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows.&#160;&#160;For information on the location and amounts of derivative fair values on the Consolidated Balance Sheets see Note 6 - Fair Value.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Certain of our power-related derivative instruments contain provisions for performance assurance that may include the posting of collateral in the form of cash or letters of credit, or other credit enhancements.&#160;&#160;Our counterparties will typically establish collateral thresholds that represent credit limits, and these credit limits vary depending on our credit rating.&#160;&#160;If our current credit rating were to decline, certain counterparties could request immediate payment and full, overnight ongoing collateralization on derivative instruments in net liability positions.&#160;&#160;We have no derivative instruments with credit-risk-related contingent features that were in a liability position on December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;For information concerning performance assurance, see Note 19 - Commitments and Contingencies - Performance Assurance.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">NOTE 17 - PENSION AND POSTRETIREMENT MEDICAL BENEFITS</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We have a qualified, non-contributory, defined-benefit pension plan covering unionized and non-unionized employees hired prior to April 1, 2010, subject to certain eligibility criteria.&#160;&#160;Under the terms of the Pension Plan, employees are vested after completing five years of service, and can receive a pension benefit when they are at least age 55 with a minimum of 10 years of service. They are eligible to choose between various payment options such as a monthly benefit or a one-time lump-sum amount depending on factors such as years of service earned at the date of retirement.&#160;&#160;Our funding policy is to contribute to the pension trust fund the greater of the annual actuarial cost or the statutory minimum.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On November 9, 2009, our board of directors voted to approve changes to the pension plan and 401(k) plan with a conversion date of April 1, 2010.&#160;&#160;The pension plan described above was closed to employees hired after the conversion date.&#160;&#160;All employees hired after the conversion date are now given, in addition to the existing match on 401(k) contributions up to 4.25 percent, a core 401(k) contribution of 3 percent of base pay, or a total of up to 7.25 percent. The core contribution will be subject to a three-year cliff vesting schedule.&#160;&#160;For employees hired before the conversion date, the pension benefits described above will remain in effect. In addition, employees hired before the conversion date receive a core 401(k) contribution of .50 percent of eligible base pay into the 401(k) plan in addition to the current 401(k) company match of up to 4.25 percent, or a total of up to 4.75 percent. The pension plan was also be enhanced on the conversion date by offering the so-called &#8220;Rule of 85.&#8221;&#160;&#160;Under the Rule of 85, if an employee is at least 55 years old with 10 years of service and their combined service and age totals at least 85, they will be eligible for an unreduced pension benefit.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We also sponsor a defined-benefit postretirement medical plan that covers all employees who retire with 10 or more years of service after age 45 and who are at least age 55.&#160;&#160;We fund this obligation through a Voluntary Employees&#8217; Benefit Association and a 401(h) Subaccount in the Pension Plan.&#160;&#160;Pre-age 65 retirees participate in plan options similar to active employees.&#160;&#160;Post-age 65 retirees receive limited coverage with a $10,000 annual individual maximum.&#160;&#160;Company contributions to retiree medical premiums are capped for employees retiring after 1995 at $0.3 million per year for pre-age 65 retirees and are capped at a nominal amount for post-age 65 retirees.&#160;&#160;There are no retiree contributions for pre-1996 retirees.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Beginning in 2009, the postretirement benefit was enhanced with sharing of one-half of the Medicare Part D subsidy that we received.&#160;&#160;Under this enhancement, we split the shared subsidy portion evenly between the pre-age 65 and post-age 65 retiree plans.&#160;&#160;Medicare Part D reduced our postretirement medical benefit costs by $0.8 million in 2010 and $1.7 million in 2009.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">FASB&#8217;s guidance for employee retirement benefits requires an employer with a defined benefit plan or other postretirement plan to recognize an asset or liability on its balance sheet for the overfunded or underfunded status of the plan.&#160;&#160;For pension plans, the asset or liability is the difference between the fair value of the plan&#8217;s assets and the projected benefit obligation.&#160;&#160;For postretirement benefit plans, the asset or liability is the difference between the fair value of the plan&#8217;s assets and the accumulated postretirement benefit obligation.</font></div>

</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Investment Strategy:</font>&#160;Our pension investment policy seeks to achieve sufficient growth to enable the Pension Plan to meet our future benefit obligations to participants, maintain certain funded ratios and minimize near-term cost volatility.&#160;&#160;Current guidelines specify generally that 54 percent of plan assets be invested in equity securities and 46 percent of plan assets be invested in debt securities.&#160;&#160;The debt securities are primarily comprised of long-duration bonds to match changes in plan liabilities.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our postretirement medical benefit plan investment policy seeks to achieve sufficient funding levels to meet future benefit obligations to participants and minimize near-term cost volatility.&#160;&#160;Current guidelines specify generally that 60 percent of the plan assets be invested in equity securities and 40 percent be invested in debt securities.&#160;&#160;Fixed-income securities are of a shorter duration to better match the cash flows of the postretirement medical obligation.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Concentrations of Risk:</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>Benefit plan assets that potentially expose us to concentrations of risk include, but are not limited to, significant investments in a single entity, industry, country, commodity or type of security.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">To mitigate concentrations of risk arising from our benefit plan investments in debt and equity securities, we pursue a range of investment strategies using a well-diversified array of equity and fixed income funds.&#160;&#160;We also employ a &#8220;liability-driven&#8221; investing strategy in our pension portfolio, which is a strategy that matches the duration of liabilities and assets to mitigate the negative impact that movements in the interest rates can have on our benefit obligations and funded status.&#160;&#160;Approximately 25 percent of our liabilities are matched with plan assets.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>

</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The increase in the Postretirement Medical Plan funded status of $7 million for 2010 versus 2009 resulted from an increase of $3.4 million in the fair value of assets as shown in the table above, and a decrease of $3.6 million in the benefit obligation, primarily due to the reasons described above and employer contributions.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Fair Value Measures</font>&#160;As of December 31, 2009, we adopted FASB guidance that requires additional information about the fair value measurements of plan assets that must be disclosed separately for each annual period for each plan asset category.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Valuation Techniques:</font>&#160;Fair value guidance emphasizes that market-based measurement should be based on assumptions that market participants would use to price the benefit plan assets.&#160;&#160;The fair value guidance includes three valuation techniques to be used at the initial recognition and subsequent measurement of benefit plan assets: 1) Market Approach; 2) Income Approach; and 3) Cost Approach.&#160;&#160;Also see Note 6 - Fair Value for additional information about these valuation techniques.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The valuation technique used to determine the fair value of the debt and equity securities included in our pension and postretirement medical trust funds is the market approach.&#160;&#160;These securities are considered to be Level 1 in the fair value hierarchy since quoted prices are available in active markets for these assets.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">O</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">ther&#160;&#160;</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Long-term Disability:</font>&#160;We record non-accumulating post-employment long-term disability benefits in accordance with FASB&#8217;s guidance for Contingencies.&#160;&#160;For 2010, the year-end post-employment medical benefit obligation was $1.2 million, of which $1 million was recorded as Accrued pension and benefit obligations and $0.2 million was recorded as Other current liabilities.&#160;&#160;For 2009, the year-end post-employment benefit obligation was $1.2 million, of which $1.1 million was recorded as Accrued pension and benefit obligations and $0.1 million was recorded as Other current liabilities.&#160;&#160;The pre-tax post-employment benefit costs charged to expense (credit), including insurance premiums, were $0.2 million in 2010, $(0.1) million in 2009 and $0.1 million in 2008.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font><br>
&#160;</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">401(k) Savings Plan:</font>&#160;Most eligible employees choose to participate in our 401(k) Savings Plan. This savings plan provides for employee pre-tax and post-tax contributions up to specified limits. We match employee pre-tax contributions after one year of service.&#160;&#160;Eligible employees are at all times vested 100 percent in their pre-tax and post-tax contribution account and in their matching employer contribution.&#160;&#160;As discussed above, additional changes to our 401(k) Savings Plan became effective on April 1, 2010.&#160;&#160;Our matching contributions amounted to $1.7 million in 2010, $1.5 million in 2009 and $1.4 million in 2008.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Other Benefits:</font>&#160;We also provide a SERP to certain of our executive officers.&#160;&#160;The SERP is designed to supplement the retirement benefits available through our qualified Pension Plan and for officers newly hired after April 1, 2010 to supplement the retirement benefits available through our defined contribution plan.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">For 2010, the accumulated year-end SERP benefit obligation, based on a discount rate of 4.95 percent, was $3.6 million, of which $3.5 million was recorded as Accrued pension and benefit obligations and $0.1 million was recorded as Other current liabilities in the Consolidated Balance Sheets.&#160;&#160;The 2009 accumulated year-end SERP benefit obligation, based on a discount rate of 5.05 percent, was $3.6 million, of which $3.4 million was recorded as Accrued pension and benefit obligations and $0.2 million was recorded as Other current liabilities in the Consolidated Balance Sheets.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The accumulated SERP benefit obligation included a comprehensive gain of $0.1 million in 2010.&#160;&#160;The accumulated SERP benefit obligation included an immaterial comprehensive loss in 2009 and a comprehensive gain of $0.3 million in 2008.&#160; The pre-tax SERP benefit costs charged to expense totaled $0.2 million in 2010 and $0.3 million in both 2009 and 2008.&#160;</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Benefits are funded through life insurance policies held in a Rabbi Trust.&#160;&#160;Rabbi Trust assets are not considered plan assets for accounting purposes.&#160;&#160;The year-end balance included in Investments and Other Assets on our Consolidated Balance Sheets was $7 million in 2010 and $6.5 million in 2009.&#160;&#160;Rabbi Trust expenses, including changes in cash surrender value, are included in Other deductions on our Consolidated Statements of Income.&#160;&#160;The pre-tax amounts charged (credited) to expense were $0.1 million for 2010, ($0.6) million for 2009 and $2.6 million for 2008.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Capitalized Repairs Project:</font> The Capitalized Repairs Project included the review of 1999 through 2009 property, plant and equipment additions included in Utility Plant on the Consolidated Balance Sheets.&#160;&#160;The review was performed to identify capitalized additions, which now result in accelerated income tax deductions.&#160;&#160;In 2010, as a result of our Capitalized Repairs Project, excluding the impact of the related unrecorded tax benefit, we recorded $13.6 million to prepayments and $14.2 million to deferred income tax liabilities on the Consolidated Balance Sheets.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Casualty Loss Refund Claim Settlement:</font>&#160;&#160;Our Casualty Loss refund claims for the tax years 2003 through 2006, which were previously denied during the IRS audit of these years, were reviewed and settled by IRS Appeals during 2010.&#160;&#160;Our settlement allowed 100 percent of the Casualty Loss refund claims for the tax years 2003 through 2005, which totaled $1.9 million plus $0.4 million interest, and allowed none of the 2006 tax year refund claim.&#160;&#160;In 2010, the remaining Casualty Loss refund unrecognized tax benefit of $1 million was removed from the balance of unrecognized tax benefits.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">During 2010, unrecognized tax benefits were increased by $ 2.6 million which, due to the impact of deferred tax accounting, resulted in $0.3 million that would affect the effective tax rate if recognized.&#160;&#160;The $2.6 million increase in unrecognized tax benefits is the net of a $3.6 million increase in unrecognized tax benefits established for our Capitalized Repairs deduction and a $1 million decrease in unrecognized tax benefits due to the settlement of our Casualty Loss claims.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">There were no unrecognized tax benefits that would affect the effective tax rate if recognized at December 31, 2009 and $0.4 million at December 31, 2008.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We recognize interest related to unrecognized tax benefits as interest expense and penalties are recorded as other deductions.&#160;&#160;There was no interest expense in 2010, a $0.1 million reversal of previously recorded interest expense in 2009 and less than $0.1 million of interest expense in 2008.&#160;&#160;There was no accrued interest related to unrecognized tax benefits at December 31, 2010 and 2009.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The 2004 through 2006 tax years, although audited by the IRS, and the 2007 through 2009 tax years remain open to examination.&#160;&#160;The 2008 tax year is currently under examination by the IRS.&#160;&#160;For state tax purposes the 2007 through 2009 tax years remain open to examination by the states of New York, New Hampshire, Maine, Connecticut and Vermont.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Valuation Allowance:</font>&#160;&#160;FASB&#8217;s guidance for income taxes prohibits the recognition of all or a portion of deferred income tax benefits if it is more likely than not that the deferred tax asset will not be realized.&#160;&#160;During 2010, based upon FASB income tax guidance, we recorded a $1 million deferred tax asset representing the excess of tax basis over book value for our investment in VYNPC.&#160;&#160;We also recorded an equal valuation allowance as it is more likely than not that this deferred tax asset will not be realized.&#160;&#160;There was no tax impact for this transaction.&#160;&#160;During December 2008, we established a $0.2 million valuation allowance.&#160;&#160;At issue was the ability to utilize a state capital loss carryforward prior to the expiration of the carryforward period.&#160;&#160;During 2009 we obtained information that led us to conclude it was more likely than not that the capital loss will be utilized during the five-year carryforward period and we reversed the valuation allowance<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">.</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Health Care Legislation:</font>&#160;On March 23, 2010, the PPACA was signed into law. The PPACA is a comprehensive health care reform bill that includes revenue-raising provisions for nearly $400 billion over 10 years through tax increases on high-income individuals, excise taxes on high-cost group health plans, and new fees on selected health-care-related industries.&#160;&#160;In addition, on March 25, 2010, the Health Care and Education Affordability Reconciliation Act of 2010 was passed into law, which modifies certain provisions of the PPACA.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Together, the legislation repeals the current rule permitting a tax deduction for prescription drug coverage expense under our postretirement medical plan that is actuarially equivalent to that provided under Medicare Part D.&#160;&#160;This provision is effective for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2012.&#160;&#160;As required, in 2010 we recorded an increase of $2.1 million in regulatory assets and an increase of $2.8 million in deferred income taxes liabilities on the Consolidated Balance Sheets, resulting in an increase of $0.7 million in income tax expense on the Consolidated Statements of Income, related to postretirement medical expenditures that will not be deductible in the future.&#160;&#160;This legislative change is considered an exogenous event and is included in the exogenous effects deferral.&#160;&#160;See Note 9 &#8211; Retail Rates and Regulatory Accounting for additional information.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Tax Bonus Depreciation:</font>&#160;&#160; The Small Business Jobs Act of 2010, which became law on September 27, 2010, extended 50 percent bonus depreciation to 2010.&#160;&#160;In addition, as a result of the Tax Relief, Unemployment Insurance Reauthorization, and Job Creation Act of 2010, which became law on December 17, 2010, the 50 percent bonus depreciation was extended through 2012, and a 100 percent expensing was allowed for property placed in service after September 8, 2010 through 2011.&#160;&#160;The combined impact of the additional bonus depreciation allowed as a result of these Acts was $6.7 million that was recorded to prepayments and deferred income tax liabilities on the current year Consolidated Balance Sheet.&#160;&#160;These legislative changes are considered exogenous events and are included in the exogenous effects deferral.&#160;&#160;See Note 9 - Retail Rates and Regulatory Accounting for additional information.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">NOTE 19 - COMMITMENTS AND CONTINGENCIES</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Long-Term Power Purchases </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Vermont Yankee:</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>We are purchasing our entitlement share of Vermont Yankee plant output through the VY PPA between Entergy-Vermont Yankee and VYNPC.&#160;&#160;We have one secondary purchaser that receives less than 0.5 percent of our entitlement.&#160;&#160;See Note 4 &#8211; Investments in Affiliates for additional information on the VY PPA.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Entergy-Vermont Yankee has no obligation to supply energy to VYNPC over its entitlement share of plant output, so we receive reduced amounts when the plant is operating at a reduced level, and no energy when the plant is not operating.&#160;&#160;We purchase replacement energy as needed when the Vermont Yankee plant is not operating or is operating at reduced levels.&#160;&#160;We typically acquire most of this replacement energy through forward purchase contracts and account for those contracts as derivatives.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The plant normally shuts down for about one month every 18 months for maintenance and to insert new fuel into the reactor.&#160;&#160;A refueling outage was completed in May 2010 and estimated incremental costs for replacement power were factored into our 2010 base rates.&#160;&#160;Our total VYNPC purchases were $58.7 million in 2010, $64 million in 2009 and $57.7 million in 2008.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We have a forced outage insurance policy to cover additional costs, if any, of obtaining replacement power from other sources if the Vermont Yankee plant experiences unplanned outages.&#160;&#160;The current policy covers March 22, 2010 through March 21, 2011.&#160;&#160;This outage insurance does not apply to derates or acts of terrorism.&#160;&#160;The coverage applies to unplanned outages of up to 90 consecutive calendar days per outage event, and provides for payment of the difference between the hourly spot market price and $42/MWh. The aggregate maximum coverage is $9 million with a $1.2 million deductible. We do not plan to renew the outage insurance.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Prices under the VY PPA increase $1 per megawatt-hour each calendar year and will be $44 per MWh in 2011 and $45 per MWh in 2012.&#160;&#160;The VY PPA contains a provision known as the &#8220;low market adjuster&#8221; that calls for a downward adjustment in the contract price if market prices for electricity fall by defined amounts.&#160;&#160;Estimated annual purchases are expected to be $65.7 million for 2011 and $16.6 million for 2012 when the contract expires in March.&#160;&#160;A summary of the VY PPA, including the actual amount for 2010 and the estimated average amounts for 2011 and 2012, is shown in the table below.&#160;&#160;The total cost estimates are based on projected MWh purchase volumes at PPA rates, plus estimates of VYNPC costs, primarily net interest expense and the cost of capital.&#160;&#160;Actual amounts may differ.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On June 22, 2010, we, along with GMP, made a claim under the September 6, 2001 VY PPA.&#160;&#160;The claim is that Entergy-Vermont Yankee breached its obligations under the agreement by failing to detect and remedy the conditions that resulted in cooling tower-related failures at the Vermont Yankee nuclear plant in 2007 and 2008. Those failures caused us and GMP to incur substantial incremental replacement power costs.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We are seeking recovery of the incremental costs from Entergy-Vermont Yankee under the terms of the VY PPA based upon the results of certain reports, including an NRC inspection, in which the inspection team found that Entergy-Vermont Yankee, among other things, did not have sufficient design documentation available to help it prevent problems with the cooling towers.&#160;&#160;The NRC released its findings on October 14, 2008.&#160;&#160;In considering whether to seek recovery, we also reviewed the 2007 and 2008 root cause analysis reports by Entergy-Vermont Yankee and a December 22, 2008 reliability assessment provided by Nuclear Safety Associates to the State of Vermont.&#160;&#160;Entergy-Vermont Yankee disputes our claim.&#160;&#160;We cannot predict the outcome of this matter at this time.</font></div>

<br>
