<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160; </font></div>
</div>
</div>

<br>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The VY PPA contains a formula for determining the VYNPC power entitlement following an uprate in 2006 that increased the plant&#8217;s operating capacity by approximately 20 percent.&#160;&#160;VYNPC and Entergy-Vermont Yankee are seeking to resolve certain differences in the interpretation of the formula.&#160;&#160;At issue is how much capacity and energy VYNPC Sponsors receive under the VY PPA following the uprate.&#160;&#160;Based on VYNPC&#8217;s calculations the VYNPC Sponsors should be entitled to slightly more capacity and energy than they have been receiving under the VY PPA since the uprate.&#160;&#160;We cannot predict the outcome of this matter at this time.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our contract for power purchases from VYNPC ends in March 2012, but there is a risk that we could lose this resource if the plant shuts down for any reason before that date. An early shutdown could cause our customers to lose the economic benefit of an energy volume of close to 50 percent of our total committed supply and we would have to acquire replacement power resources for approximately 40 percent of our estimated power supply needs.&#160;&#160;Based on forward market prices as of December 31, 2010, the incremental replacement cost of lost power is estimated to be $14.3 million over the remaining life of the contract.&#160;&#160;We are not able to predict whether there will be an early shutdown of the Vermont Yankee plant or whether the PSB would allow timely and full recovery of increased costs related to such shutdown.&#160;&#160;An early shutdown, depending upon the specific circumstances, could involve recovery of increased costs under the PCAM but, in general, would not be expected to materially impact financial results if the costs are recovered in retail rates in a timely fashion.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On February 24, 2010, in a non-binding vote, the Vermont Senate voted against allowing the PSB to consider granting the Vermont Yankee plant another 20-year operating license after 2012.&#160; The new Vermont Legislature elected on November 2, 2010 could vote differently, although the political makeup of the House and Senate remains largely unchanged.&#160; Also, Vermont elected a new governor who advocated as a member of the Vermont Senate and during the gubernatorial campaign that the Vermont Yankee plant should close when its current license expires.&#160; While circumstances could change and we expect to engage in a constructive dialogue with the new administration and legislature related to the continued operation of the Vermont Yankee plant, we are unable to predict the outcome at this time.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On March 10, 2011, the NRC voted 4-0 to approve the 20-year license extension through March 21, 2032 requested by Entergy-Vermont Yankee.&#160;&#160;This approval removes the last federal level regulatory requirement for relicensing of the Vermont Yankee station.&#160;&#160;However, the Vermont Legislature has not approved the license extension and such approval is considered unlikely at this time.&#160;&#160;Under Vermont law, in addition to a favorable Vermont legislative vote, the PSB needs to issue a Certificate of Public Good for the plant to continue to operate after March 21, 2012.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Entergy-Vermont Yankee is attempting to overcome legislative concerns, but has also recently intimated that it may challenge the state&#8217;s authority as it relates to relicensing.&#160;&#160;In April 2010, we began a new round of negotiations on a new contract.&#160;&#160;While we rejected Entergy-Vermont Yankee&#8217;s December 2009 public proposal of contract terms, we continue to exchange information and proposals with them.&#160;&#160;We cannot predict the outcome of this matter at this time.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Hydro-Qu&#233;bec:</font> We are purchasing power from Hydro-Qu&#233;bec under the VJO power contract.&#160;&#160;The VJO power contract has been in place since 1987 and purchases began in 1990.&#160;&#160;Related contracts were subsequently negotiated between us and Hydro-Qu&#233;bec, altering the terms and conditions contained in the original contract by reducing the overall power requirements and related costs.&#160;&#160;The VJO power contract runs through 2020, but our purchases under the contract end in 2016.&#160;&#160;The average level of deliveries under the current contract decreases by approximately 19 percent after 2012, and by approximately 84 percent after 2015.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The annual load factor is 75 percent for the remainder of the VJO power contract, unless the contract is changed or there is a reduction due to the adverse hydraulic conditions described below.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">There are two sellback contracts with provisions that apply to existing and future VJO power contract purchases.&#160;&#160;The first resulted in the sellback of 25 MW of capacity and associated energy through April 30, 2012, which has no net impact currently since an identical 25 MW purchase was made in conjunction with the sellback. We have a 23 MW share of the 25 MW sellback. However, since the sellback ends six months before the corresponding purchase ends, the first sellback will result in a 23 MW increase in our capacity and energy purchases for the period from May 1, 2012 through October 31, 2012.</font></div>

<br>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160; </font></div>
</div>
</div>

<br>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">A second sellback contract provided benefits to us that ended in 1996 in exchange for two options to Hydro-Qu&#233;bec.&#160;&#160;The first option was never exercised and expired December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;The second gives Hydro-Qu&#233;bec the right, upon one year&#8217;s written notice, to curtail energy deliveries in a contract year (12 months beginning November 1) from an annual capacity factor of 75 to 50 percent due to adverse hydraulic conditions as measured at certain metering stations on unregulated rivers in Quebec. This second option can be exercised five times through October 2015 but due to the notice provision there is a maximum remaining application of three times available.&#160;&#160;To date, Hydro-Qu&#233;bec has not exercised this option. We have determined that this second option is not a derivative because it is contingent upon a physical variable.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">There are specific contractual provisions providing that in the event any VJO member fails to meet its obligation under the contract with Hydro-Qu&#233;bec, the remaining VJO participants will &#8220;step-up&#8221; to the defaulting party&#8217;s share on a pro-rata basis.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, our obligation is about 47 percent of the total VJO power contract through 2016, and represents approximately $285.7 million, on a nominal basis.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In accordance with FASB&#8217;s guidance for guarantees, we are required to disclose the &#8220;maximum potential amount of future payments (undiscounted) the guarantor could be required to make under the guarantee.&#8221;&#160;&#160;Such disclosure is required even if the likelihood is remote.&#160;&#160;With regard to the &#8220;step-up&#8221; provision in the VJO power contract, we must assume that all members of the VJO simultaneously default in order to estimate the &#8220;maximum potential&#8221; amount of future payments.&#160;&#160;We believe this is a highly unlikely scenario given that the majority of VJO members are regulated utilities with regulated cost recovery.&#160;&#160;Each VJO participant has received regulatory approval to recover the cost of this purchased power contract in its most recent rate applications.&#160;&#160;Despite the remote chance that such an event could occur, we estimate that our undiscounted purchase obligation would be an additional $335.1 million for the remainder of the contract, assuming that all members of the VJO defaulted by January 1, 2011 and remained in default for the duration of the contract.&#160;&#160;In such a scenario, we would then own the power and could seek to recover our costs from the defaulting members or our retail customers, or resell the power in the wholesale power markets in New England.&#160;&#160;The range of outcomes (full cost recovery, potential loss or potential profit) would be highly dependent on Vermont regulation and wholesale market prices at the time.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Total purchases from Hydro-Qu&#233;bec were $63 million in 2010, $63.1 million in 2009 and $63.7 million in 2008.&#160;&#160;Annual capacity costs decreased by $2.2 million starting November 1, 2009, and that cost reduction will continue for six contract years.&#160;&#160;A summary of the Hydro-Qu&#233;bec actual charges for 2010 and the projected charges for the remainder of the contract are shown in the table below.&#160;&#160;Projections are based on certain assumptions including availability of the transmission system and scheduled deliveries, so actual amounts may differ (dollars in thousands, except per kWh amounts):</font></div>

</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Independent Power Producers:</font> <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>We receive power from several Independent IPPs.&#160;&#160;&#160;These plants use water or biomass as fuel.&#160;&#160;Most of the power comes through a state-appointed purchasing agent that allocates power to all Vermont utilities under PSB rules.&#160;&#160;Our total purchases from IPPs were $22.9 million in 2010, $22.6 million in 2009 and $26.4 million in 2008.&#160;&#160;Estimated annual purchases are expected to range from $7.7 million to $22.6 million for the years 2011 through 2015.&#160;&#160;Cost will begin to drop when a major contract obligation ends in 2012.&#160;&#160;These estimates are based on assumptions regarding average weather conditions and other factors affecting generating unit output, so actual amounts may differ.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our share of operating expenses for these facilities is included in the corresponding operating accounts on the Consolidated Statements of Income.&#160;&#160;Each participant in these facilities must provide for its financing.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We have a 1.7303 joint-ownership percentage in Millstone Unit #3, in which DNC is the lead owner with 93.4707 percent of the plant joint-ownership.&#160;&#160;In August 2008 the NRC approved a request by DNC to increase the Millstone Unit #3 plant&#8217;s generating capacity by approximately 7 percent.&#160;&#160;We were obligated to pay our ownership share of the related costs.&#160;&#160;The uprate was completed during the scheduled refueling outage that concluded in November 2008 and our share of plant generation increased by 1.4 MW.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In January 2004 DNC filed, on behalf of itself and the two minority owners, including us, a lawsuit against the DOE seeking recovery of costs related to the storage of spent nuclear fuel arising from the failure of the DOE to comply with its obligations to commence accepting such fuel in 1998.&#160; A trial commenced in May 2008.&#160; On October 15, 2008, the United States Court of Federal Claims issued a favorable decision in the case, including damages specific to Millstone Unit #3.&#160; The DOE appealed the court&#8217;s decision in December 2008.&#160;&#160;On February 20, 2009, the government filed a motion seeking an indefinite stay of the briefing schedule. On March 18, 2009, the court granted the government&#8217;s request to stay the appeal.&#160;&#160;On November 19, 2009, DNC filed a motion to lift the stay.&#160;&#160;On April 12, 2010, the stay was lifted and a staggered briefing schedule was proposed, to which DNC has responded with a request to expedite the briefing schedule so that the appeals of all parties can be heard concurrently.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On June 30, 2010, the DOE filed its initial brief in the spent fuel damages litigation. This brief focuses on the costs awarded in connection with Millstone Unit #3.&#160;&#160;DNC replied to the government&#8217;s brief in August, 2010.&#160;&#160;The government&#8217;s reply brief was filed September 14, 2010 and briefing on the appeal is now complete.&#160;&#160;Oral argument on the government&#8217;s appeal occurred before the Federal Circuit on January 12, 2011.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We continue to pay our share of the DOE Spent Fuel assessment expenses levied on actual generation and will share in recovery from the lawsuit, if any, in proportion to our ownership interest.&#160;&#160;We expect that our share of a recovery, if any, would be credited to our retail customers.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Future Power Agreements</font>&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">New Hydro-Qu&#233;bec</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Agreement:</font>&#160;&#160;On August 12, 2010 we, along with Green GMP, VPPSA, Vermont Electric Cooperative, Inc., Vermont Marble, Town of Stowe Electric Department, City of Burlington, Vermont Electric Department, Washington Electric Cooperative, Inc. and the 13 municipal members of VPPSA (collectively, the &#8220;Buyers&#8221;) entered into an agreement for the purchase of shares of 218 MW to 225 MW of energy and environmental attributes from HQUS commencing on November 1, 2012 and continuing through 2038.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The rights and obligations of the Buyers under the HQUS PPA, including payment of the contract price and indemnification obligations, are several and not joint or joint and several. Therefore, we shall have no responsibility for the obligations, financial or otherwise, of any other party to the HQUS PPA. The parties have also entered into related agreements, including collateral agreements between each Buyer and HQUS, a Hydro-Qu&#233;bec guaranty, an allocation agreement among the Buyers, and an assignment and assumption agreement between us and Vermont Marble, related to the pending acquisition.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The HQUS PPA will replace approximately 65 percent of the existing VJO power contract discussed above, which along with the VY PPA supply the majority of Vermont&#8217;s current power needs. The VJO power contract and the VY PPA expire within the next several years.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The obligations of HQUS and each Buyer are contingent upon the receipt of certain governmental approvals. On August 17, 2010, the Buyers filed a petition with the PSB asking for Certificates of Public Good under Section 248 of Title 30, Vermont Statutes Annotated. The PSB has established a schedule for the docket including technical hearings and final legal briefs in the first quarter of 2011.&#160;&#160;In the event the HQUS PPA is terminated with respect to any Buyer as a result of such Buyer&#8217;s failure to receive governmental approvals, each of the other Buyers will have an option to purchase the additional energy.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Under the Agreement, subject to regulatory approval, we would be entitled to purchase an energy quantity of up to 85.4 MW from November 1, 2015 to October 31, 2016; 96.4 MW from November 1, 2016 to October 31, 2020; 98.4 MW from November 1, 2020 to October 31, 2030; 112.1 MW from November 1, 2030 to October 31, 2035; and 26.7 MW from November 1, 2035 to October 31, 2038.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Other Future Power Agreements:&#160;&#160;</font>As we continue to build and diversify our power portfolio as planned and to comply with state law which establishes goals for including renewable power in our mix, we have recently signed several agreements for clean and competitively priced renewable energy.&#160;&#160;On September 9, 2010 we agreed to terms for purchasing output over nine years from Iberdrola Renewables&#8217; planned Deerfield Wind Project.&#160;&#160;The agreement was signed by the parties on December 13, 2010.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Other recently signed agreements include: two separate agreements to purchase 30.3 percent of the actual output from Granite Reliable Wind project for 20 years beginning April 1, 2012 and an additional 20 percent for 15 years beginning in November 2012; an agreement to purchase the entire 4.99 MW output of Ampersand Gilman Hydro for five years starting April 1, 2012; and 15 MW of around-the-clock energy from J.P. Morgan Ventures Energy for the calendar years 2013 through 2015.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Nuclear Decommissioning Obligations </font>We are obligated to pay our share of nuclear decommissioning costs for nuclear plants in which we have an ownership interest.&#160;&#160;We have an external trust dedicated to funding our joint-ownership share of future Millstone Unit #3 decommissioning costs.&#160;&#160;DNC has suspended contributions to the Millstone Unit #3 Trust Fund because the minimum NRC funding requirements have been met or exceeded.&#160;&#160;We have also suspended contributions to the Trust Fund, but could choose to renew funding at our own discretion as long as the minimum requirement is met or exceeded.&#160;&#160;If a need for additional decommissioning funding is necessary, we will be obligated to resume contributions to the Trust Fund.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We have equity ownership interests in Maine Yankee, Connecticut Yankee and Yankee Atomic.&#160;&#160;These plants are permanently shut down and completely decommissioned except for the spent fuel storage at each location.&#160;&#160;Our obligations related to these plants are described in Note 4 - Investments in Affiliates.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We also had a 35 percent ownership interest in the Vermont Yankee nuclear power plant through our equity investment in VYNPC, but the plant was sold in 2002.&#160;&#160;Our obligation for plant decommissioning costs ended when the plant was sold, except that VYNPC retained responsibility for the pre-1983 spent fuel disposal cost liability.&#160;&#160;VYNPC has a dedicated Trust Fund that meets most of the liability.&#160;&#160;Changes in the underlying interest rates that affect the earnings and the liability could cause the balance to be a surplus or deficit.&#160;&#160;Excess funds, if any, will be returned to us and the other former owners and must be applied to the benefit of retail customers.</font></div>

<br>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Nuclear Insurance</font> The Price-Anderson Act provides a framework for immediate, no-fault insurance coverage for the public in the event of a nuclear power plant accident that is deemed an &#8220;extraordinary nuclear occurrence&#8221; by the NRC.&#160; The EPACT reinstated and extended the Price-Anderson Act for 20 years.&#160; There are two levels of coverage.&#160; The primary level provides liability insurance coverage of $375 million, or the maximum private insurance available.&#160; If this amount is not sufficient to cover claims arising from an accident, the second level applies offering additional coverage up to $12.6 billion per incident.&#160; For the second level, each operating nuclear plant must pay a retrospective premium equal to its proportionate share of the excess loss, up to a maximum of $111.9 million per reactor per incident, limited to a maximum annual payout of $17.5&#160;million per reactor.&#160; These assessments will be adjusted for inflation and U.S. Congress can modify or increase the insurance liability coverage limits at any time through legislation.&#160; Currently, based on our joint-ownership interest in Millstone Unit #3, we could become liable for about $0.3 million of such maximum assessment per incident per year.&#160; Maine Yankee, Connecticut Yankee and Yankee Atomic maintain $100 million in Nuclear Liability Insurance, but have received exemptions from participating in the secondary financial protection program.&#160;</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Performance Assurance </font>We are subject to performance assurance requirements through ISO-NE under the Financial Assurance Policy for NEPOOL members.&#160;&#160;At our current investment-grade credit rating, we have a credit limit of $3.2 million with ISO-NE.&#160;&#160;We are required to post collateral for all net purchased power transactions in excess of this credit limit.&#160;&#160;Additionally, we are currently selling power in the wholesale market pursuant to contracts with third parties, and are required to post collateral under certain conditions defined in the contracts.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">At December 31, 2010, we had posted $6.6 million of collateral under performance assurance requirements for certain of our power contracts, $5.5 million of which was represented by a letter of credit and $1.1 million of which was represented by cash and cash equivalents.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2009, we had posted $5.4 million of collateral under performance assurance requirements for certain of our power contracts, all of which was represented by restricted cash.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We are also subject to performance assurance requirements under our Vermont Yankee power purchase contract (the 2001 Amendatory Agreement).&#160;&#160;If Entergy-Vermont Yankee, the seller, has commercially reasonable grounds to question our ability to pay for our monthly power purchases, Entergy-Vermont Yankee may ask VYNPC and VYNPC may then ask us to provide adequate financial assurance of payment. We have not had to post collateral under this contract.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Environmental </font>Over<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>the years, more than 100 companies have merged into or been acquired by CVPS.&#160;&#160;At least two of those companies used coal to produce gas for retail sale.&#160;&#160;Gas manufacturers, their predecessors and CVPS used waste disposal methods that were legal and acceptable then, but may not meet modern environmental standards and could represent a liability.&#160;&#160;These practices ended more than 50 years ago.&#160;&#160;Some operations and activities are inspected and supervised by federal and state authorities, including the Environmental Protection Agency.&#160;&#160;We believe that we are in compliance with all laws and regulations and have implemented procedures and controls to assess and assure compliance.&#160;&#160;Corrective action is taken when necessary.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">As of December 31, 2010, our Environmental Reserve was $0.8 million, compared to $1.6 million in 2009, and $1.7 million in 2008. A summary of the Environmental Reserve as of December 31, 2010 follows (dollars in thousands):</font></div>

</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The reserve for environmental matters is included as current and long-term liabilities on the Consolidated Balance Sheets and represents our best estimate of the cost to remedy issues at these sites based on available information as of the end of the applicable reporting periods.&#160;&#160;Below is a brief discussion of the significant sites for which we have recorded reserves.</font></div>

<br>
<div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160; </font></div>
</div>

<div id="PN" style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; WIDTH: 100%">
<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Page 104 of 128</font></div>

<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
<hr style="COLOR: black" noshade size="2">
</div>
</div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160; </font></div>
</div>
</div>

<br>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Cleveland Avenue Property</font>: The Cleveland Avenue property in Rutland, Vermont, was used by a predecessor to make gas from coal.&#160;&#160;Later, we sited various operations there.&#160;&#160;Due to the existence of coal tar deposits, PCB contamination and the potential for off-site migration, we conducted studies in the late 1980s and early 1990s to quantify the nature and extent of contamination and potential costs to remediate the site.&#160;&#160;Investigation at the site continued, including work with the State of Vermont to develop a mutually acceptable solution.&#160;&#160;In June 2010, both the VANR and the Environmental Protection Agency approved separate remediation work plans for the manufactured gas plant and PCB waste at the site.&#160;&#160;Remedial work started in August 2010 and concluded in early December 2010.&#160;&#160;We discovered more PCB contamination than anticipated at this site and it was necessary to excavate and dispose of additional material.&#160;&#160;As a result, the reserve was increased by $0.6 million in 2010. Remediation is nearly complete as of December 31, 2010. Some additional sitework including grading and vegetation planting will occur in 2011.&#160;&#160;In February 2011, we submitted a Construction Completion Report for the project to the EPA and VANR for review.&#160;&#160;The report documented remedial construction and confirmatory sampling activities.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, our remaining obligation is less than $0.1 million.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Brattleboro Manufactured Gas Facility</font>:&#160;In the 1940s, we owned and operated a manufactured gas facility in Brattleboro, Vermont.&#160;&#160;We ordered a site assessment in 1999 at the request of the State of New Hampshire.&#160;&#160;In 2001, New Hampshire indicated that no further action was required, although it reserved the right to require further investigation or remedial measures.&#160;&#160;In 2002, the Vermont Agency of Natural Resources notified us that our corrective action plan for the site was approved.&#160;&#160;That plan is now in place.&#160;&#160;We have reviewed our reserve for this site based on a probabilistic 2006 cost estimate of remediation and determined that it is adequate.&#160;&#160;The liability for site remediation is expected to range from $0.1 million to $1.3 million.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, our remaining obligation is $0.5 million.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Currently, the Windham Regional Commission and the Town of Brattleboro are pursuing the redevelopment of the gas plant site and waterfront area into vehicle parking with green space. This concept calls for the removal of the remnant gas plant building plus covering and otherwise avoiding contaminated areas instead of removing contaminated soil and debris.&#160;&#160;We are assessing the cost implications of this conceptual plan. Currently we do not believe the impact of the plan will be material.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Dover, New Hampshire, Manufactured Gas Facility:</font>&#160;In 1999, PSNH contacted us about this site.&#160;&#160;PSNH alleged that we were partially liable for cleanup, since the site was previously operated by Twin State Gas and Electric, which merged into CVPS on the same day that PSNH bought the facility.&#160;&#160;In 2002, we reached a settlement with PSNH in which certain liabilities we might have had were assigned to PSNH in return for a cash settlement we paid based on completion of PSNH&#8217;s cleanup effort.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, our remaining obligation was less than $0.1 million.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Middlebury Lower Substation:</font> By letter dated February 5, 2010, the VANR Sites Management Section informed us they require additional investigation of the soil contamination at the Middlebury Lower Substation.&#160;&#160;This was a result of voluntarily submitted information from an internal soil sampling that we completed in the fall of 2009.&#160;&#160;The soil sampling showed elevated levels of TPH, which will require remediation.&#160;&#160;Substation reconstruction started in October 2010 after a delay for an archeological investigation.&#160;&#160;The environmental site work consists of the removal and landfill disposal of the slightly contaminated soil.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, our remaining obligation was less than $0.1 million.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Salisbury Substation:</font> We completed internal testing and found PCBs and TPH, as well as small quantities of pesticides in the soil and concrete at this site.&#160;&#160;The substation is located adjacent to the Salisbury hydroelectric power station.&#160;&#160;It is scheduled to be retired and replaced during 2011.&#160;&#160;Final results indicated that PCB, TPH, and pesticide concentrations exceed state and federal regulatory limits at portions at the site.&#160;&#160;We submitted a letter to the VANR Sites Management Section proposing that PCB remediation efforts would be sufficient mitigation for TPH and pesticide contamination, and proposed to collect soil samples for confirmatory testing of these compounds.&#160;&#160;A cost estimate was made, and we reserved $0.2 million for the cost of the cleanup at this site.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">To management&#8217;s knowledge, there is no pending or threatened litigation regarding other sites with the potential to cause material expense.&#160;&#160;No government agency has sought funds from us for any other study or remediation.</font></div>

</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Catamount Indemnifications</font> On December 20, 2005, we completed the sale of Catamount, our wholly owned subsidiary, to CEC Wind Acquisition, LLC, a company established by Diamond Castle Holdings, a New York-based private equity investment firm.&#160;&#160;Under the terms of the agreements with Catamount and Diamond Castle Holdings, we agreed to indemnify them, and certain of their respective affiliates, in respect of a breach of certain representations and warranties and covenants, most of which ended June 30, 2007, except certain items that customarily survive indefinitely.&#160;&#160;Indemnification is subject to a $1.5 million deductible and a $15 million cap, excluding certain customary items.&#160;&#160;Environmental representations are subject to the deductible and the cap, and such environmental representations for only two of Catamount&#8217;s underlying energy projects survived beyond June 30, 2007.&#160;&#160;Our estimated &#8220;maximum potential&#8221; amount of future payments related to these indemnifications is limited to $15 million.&#160;&#160;We have not recorded any liability related to these indemnifications.&#160;&#160;To management&#8217;s knowledge, there is no pending or threatened litigation with the potential to cause material expense.&#160;&#160;No government agency has sought funds from us for any study or remediation.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Leases and support agreements </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Capital Leases:&#160;&#160;</font>We had obligations under capital leases of $4.4 million at December 31, 2010 and $5.3 million at December 31, 2009.&#160;&#160;The current and long-term portions are included as liabilities on the Consolidated Balance Sheets, and are offset by Property Under Capital Leases included in Utility plant.&#160;&#160;We account for capital leases under FASB&#8217;s guidance for leases.&#160;&#160;In accordance with FASB&#8217;s guidance for regulated operations and based on our ratemaking treatment, amortizations of leased assets are recorded as operating expenses on the income statement, depending on the nature and function of the leased assets.&#160;&#160;Of the $4.4 million, $4.2 million is related to the Hydro-Qu&#233;bec Phase II transmission facilities and the remaining $0.2 million is related to several five-year office and computing equipment leases.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We participated with other electric utilities in the construction of the Phase II transmission facilities in New England, which were completed at a total initial cost of $487 million.&#160;&#160;Under a 30-year support agreement relating to participation in the facilities, we agreed to pay our 5.132 percent share of Phase II costs, including capital costs plus the costs of owning and operating the facilities, over a 25-year recovery period that ends in 2015, plus operating and maintenance expenses for the life of the agreement, in exchange for the rights to use a similar share of the available transmission capacity through 2020.&#160;&#160;Approximately $33 million of additional investments have been made to the Phase II transmission facilities since they were initially constructed.&#160;&#160;All costs under these agreements are recorded as transmission expense in accordance with our ratemaking policies.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010, the $4.2 million unamortized balance was comprised of $19.3 million related to our share of original costs and additional investments, offset by $15.1 million of accumulated amortization.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We also participated with other electric utilities in the construction of the Hydro-Qu&#233;bec Phase I transmission facilities in northeastern Vermont and northern New Hampshire, which were completed at a total cost of $140&#160;million.&#160;&#160;Under the 30-year support agreement relating to participation in the facilities, we were obligated to pay our 4.55 percent share of Phase I capital costs over a 20-year recovery period that ended in 2006, plus operating and maintenance expenses for the life of the agreement, in exchange for the rights to use a similar share of the available transmission capacity through 2016.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010, we had recorded accumulated amortizations of $4.9 million representing our share of the original costs associated with the Phase I transmission facility.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Phase I and Phase II support agreements provide options for extending the agreements an additional 20 years.&#160;&#160;Each option must be exercised two years before each agreement terminates, and the transmission facilities for Phase I and Phase II must operate simultaneously for the interconnection to operate, therefore both agreements would need to be extended to be operative.&#160;&#160;Future annual payments relating to the Phase I and Phase II transmission facilities are expected to decline from $3 million in 2011 to $2.5 million in 2016.&#160;&#160;If we elect to extend both agreements, annual payments are expected to increase during the renewal terms.&#160;&#160;Approximately $0.5 million of the annual costs are currently reimbursed to us pursuant to the ISO-NE Open Access Transmission Tariff.</font></div>

<td nowrap valign="bottom" width="1%" style="PADDING-BOTTOM: 4px; TEXT-ALIGN: left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">&#160;</font></td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Operating Leases:</font>&#160;We have two master lease agreements for vehicles and related equipment.&#160;&#160;On October 30, 2009, we signed a vehicle lease agreement to finance many of the vehicles covered by a former agreement.&#160;&#160;Our guarantee obligation under this lease will not exceed 8 percent of the acquisition cost. The maximum amount of future payments under this guarantee at December 31, 2010 is approximately $0.4 million. The total future minimum lease payments required for all lease schedules under this agreement at December 31, 2010 is $3.7 million.&#160;&#160;The maximum amount approved for lease under this agreement is $5.5 million, of which $5.3 million was outstanding at December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2009, the maximum amount available for lease under this agreement was $5.5 million, of which $5.4 million was outstanding.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On October 24, 2008, we entered into an operating lease for new vehicles and other related equipment.&#160;&#160;Our guarantee obligation under this lease is limited to 5 percent of the acquisition cost.&#160;&#160;The maximum amount of future payments under this guarantee is approximately $0.1 million.&#160;&#160;The total future minimum lease payments required for all lease schedules under this agreement at December 31, 2010 is $2.2 million. As of December 31, 2010 there is no credit line in place for additions under this agreement in 2011.&#160;&#160;The total acquisition cost of all lease additions under this agreement at December 31, 2010 was $2.9 million.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2009 the total acquisition cost of all lease additions under this agreement was $2.6 million.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Other operating lease commitments are considered minimal, as most are cancelable after one year from inception or the future minimum lease payments are of a nominal amount.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">At December 31, 2010, future minimum rental payments required under non-cancelable operating leases are expected to total $5.4 million, consisting of $1.8 million in 2011, $1.4 million in 2012, $1.2 million in 2013, $0.7 million in 2014 and $0.3 million thereafter.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Total rental expense, which includes pole attachment rents in addition to the operating lease agreements described above, amounted to $6.1 million in 2010, $6.3 million in 2009 and 2008. These are included in Other operation on the Consolidated Statements of Income.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Reserve for Loss on Power Contract </font>In 2005, we established a reserve for a loss on a terminated power sales agreement in connection with the sale of a subsidiary&#8217;s franchise.&#160;&#160;The reserve is being amortized on a straight-line basis through 2015 as the cash is paid out under the underlying supply contracts.&#160;&#160;The amortization is being credited to purchased power expense on the Consolidated Statement of Income.&#160;&#160;The balance of the reserve was $6 million at December 31, 2010 and $7.2 million at December 31, 2009.&#160;&#160;The current and long-term portions are included as liabilities on the Consolidated Balance Sheets.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Customer Bankruptcy&#160;</font>On October 26, 2009, a large customer filed for bankruptcy protection.&#160;&#160;In December 2010, the PSB approved the final bankruptcy plan and in January 2011, the court approved the plan and final settlement.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, we reversed the reserve of $1.1 million that was previously recorded in 2009 and received payment in January 2011.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Legal Proceedings</font> We are involved in legal and administrative proceedings in the normal course of business.&#160;&#160;We do not believe that the ultimate outcome of these proceedings will have a material adverse effect on our financial position, results of operations or cash flows.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Appropriated Retained Earnings</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">&#160;</font>Major hydroelectric project licenses provide that after an initial 20-year period, a portion of the earnings of such project in excess of a specified rate of return is to be set aside in appropriated retained earnings in compliance with FERC Order No. 5, issued in 1978.&#160;&#160;Appropriated retained earnings included in retained earnings on the Consolidated Balance Sheets were $0.8 million at December 31, 2010 and 2009.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">NOTE 20 &#8211; PENDING ACQUISITIONS</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Vermont Marble Power Division:</font>&#160;&#160;On April 30, 2010, we signed a purchase and sale agreement with Omya, Inc. to purchase certain generating, transmission and distribution assets of Vermont Marble located in the State of Vermont.&#160;&#160;Under this agreement, we will pay $33.2 million for the transmission and distribution assets and generating assets comprised of four hydroelectric generating stations.&#160;&#160;The agreement contains usual and customary purchase and sale terms and conditions and is contingent upon federal and state regulatory approvals.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">With Omya, Inc., we filed a joint petition with the PSB on August 2, 2010, requesting that they consent to the proposed sale by Omya and purchase by us of assets used in the public service business of Vermont Marble and approve certain related matters. As part of the proposed purchase and sale, we will acquire from Vermont Marble, among other things, four hydroelectric facilities on Otter Creek and Vermont Marble&#8217;s transmission and distribution facilities, which include approximately 56 miles of 46 kV transmission lines, 11 miles of 2.4/4.16 kV distribution lines, one distribution substation in the Village of Proctor, and two transmission substations. On September 14, 2010, the PSB held a prehearing conference and subsequently established a schedule for resolution of the docket including technical hearings and the filing of final legal briefs.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On October 28, 2010, we received approval from FERC, subject to certain conditions, for the proposed transaction.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On February 25, 2011, we filed an MOU between us, the DPS, the Town of Proctor and Omya, with the PSB that resolves all the outstanding issues between the parties concerning our acquisition of Vermont Marble. As part of the settlement, we will pay $28.3 million for the generating assets and approximately $1 million for the transmission and distribution assets. We will be allowed recovery from customers of $27 million for the generating assets and the $1 million for the transmission and distribution assets.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The agreement includes a five-year, six-step phase-in of residential rate changes for existing Vermont Marble customers, which will be funded by Omya up to an amount estimated to be approximately $1.1 million. The agreement also requires creation of a value sharing pool that provides for certain excess value received by us to be split between our customers, Omya and our shareholders if energy market prices and hydro improvements create more value than anticipated.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On March 4, 2011 we signed an amended and restated purchase and sale agreement with Omya, Inc. to incorporate the terms of the MOU filed on February 25, 2011.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Readsboro Electric Department:&#160;&#160;</font>On October 27, 2010, we signed a purchase and sale agreement with Readsboro.&#160;&#160;The $0.4 million purchase price includes all of the assets of Readsboro including about 14 miles of distribution line and associated equipment, and the exclusive franchise Readsboro holds to serve its 319 customers.&#160;&#160;The sale is contingent upon approval by the PSB. On February 24, 2011 we, along with the DPS and Readsboro, filed a petition with the PSB that resolves the issues outstanding in our acquisition of Readsboro.&#160;&#160;The PSB is expected to rule on the petition for approval of the transaction in the first half of 2011.<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">NOTE 21- SEGMENT REPORTING</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our reportable operating segments include:&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Central Vermont Public Service Corporation (&#8220;CV - VT&#8221;)</font>, represents our principal utility operations, which engages in the purchase, production, transmission, distribution and sale of electricity in Vermont.&#160;&#160;East Barnet is included with CV- VT in the table below.&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Other Companies</font> represents our non-utility operations and consists of CRC, and C.V. Realty, Inc.&#160;&#160;CRC was formed to hold our subsidiaries that invest in unregulated business opportunities and is the parent company of SmartEnergy Water Heating Services, Inc., which engages in the sale and rental of electric water heaters in Vermont and New Hampshire.&#160;&#160;C.V. Realty, Inc. is a real estate company whose purpose is to own, acquire, buy, sell and lease real and personal property and interests.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">None</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline"><a name="Item9a">Item 9A.</a>&#160;Controls and Procedures</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Management of the company, under the supervision and with participation of our Chief Executive Officer and Principal Financial and Accounting Officer, conducted an evaluation of the effectiveness of the design and operation of the company&#8217;s disclosure controls and procedures (as defined in Rule 13a-15(e) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the &#8220;Exchange Act&#8221;)), as of December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;Based on this evaluation, our Chief Executive Officer and Principal Financial and Accounting Officer concluded that, as of December 31, 2010, the company&#8217;s disclosure controls and procedures are effective at the reasonable assurance level.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Management&#8217;s Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting, as defined in Rule 13a-15(f) under the Securities and Exchange Act of 1934.&#160;&#160;The company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and of the preparation and fair presentation of the Company&#8217;s financial statements for external reporting purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Under the supervision of our Chief Executive Officer and Principal Financial and Accounting Officer, and with participation of management, we assessed the effectiveness of the company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting based on the framework established in &#8220;Internal Control - Integrated Framework&#8221; issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission.&#160;&#160;Based on this evaluation, we have concluded that the company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting was effective as of December 31, 2010.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting has been audited by Deloitte &amp; Touche LLP, the independent registered public accounting firm that audited our consolidated financial statements, whose report is included below.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Changes in Internal Control over Financial Reporting</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font>There were no changes in internal control over financial reporting that occurred during the quarter ended December 31, 2010 that have materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, the company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">To the Board of Directors and Stockholders of</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Central Vermont Public Service Corporation</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We have audited the internal control over financial reporting of Central Vermont Public Service Corporation and subsidiaries (the "Company") as of December 31, 2010, based on criteria established in <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Internal Control &#8212; Integrated Framework </font>issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission.&#160; The Company's management is responsible for maintaining effective internal control over financial reporting and for its assessment of the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting, included in the accompanying Management&#8217;s Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting.&#160; Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the Company's internal control over financial reporting based on our audit.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We conducted our audit in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States).&#160; Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether effective internal control over financial reporting was maintained in all material respects.&#160; Our audit included obtaining an understanding of internal control over financial reporting, assessing the risk that a material weakness exists, testing and evaluating the design and operating effectiveness of internal control based on the assessed risk, and performing such other procedures as we considered necessary in the circumstances.&#160; We believe that our audit provides a reasonable basis for our opinion.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">A company's internal control over financial reporting is a process designed by, or under the supervision of, the company's principal executive and principal financial officers, or persons performing similar functions, and effected by the company's board of directors, management, and other personnel to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.&#160; A company's internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that (1) pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the company; (2) provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the company are being made only in accordance with authorizations of management and directors of the company; and (3) provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use, or disposition of the company's assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Because of the inherent limitations of internal control over financial reporting, including the possibility of collusion or improper management override of controls, material misstatements due to error or fraud may not be prevented or detected on a timely basis.&#160; Also, projections of any evaluation of the effectiveness of the internal control over financial reporting to future periods are subject to the risk that the controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In our opinion, the Company maintained, in all material respects, effective internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2010, based on the criteria established in <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Internal Control &#8212; Integrated Framework </font>issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We have also audited, in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States), the consolidated financial statements as of and for the year ended December 31, 2010 of the Company and our report dated March 14, 2011, which report expressed an unqualified opinion on those consolidated financial statements and refers to the reports of other auditors (which as to Vermont Electric Power Company, Inc. included an explanatory paragraph concerning a change in accounting for non-controlling interests).</font></div>
